hrp|17005736|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-80f3-2a8.responsibilities: Reporting to the Senior Manager, you will lead a team of executives and service contractors for the management of buildings/facilities maintenance to support Authority's operations across multiple premises. As owner of all related systems, you will be responsible for site inspections, cost analysis, budgeting, preparing work quotations/tender specifications, procurement of services, attending to feedback and ad-hoc decisions. You will constantly review work processes and procedures to enhance facilities operations, adopt good industry practices, and ensure compliance with government regulations. Your roles include: Integrated Facilities Management: Oversee facilities management operations including housekeeping with oversight of security operations across HQ and satellite offices through our IFMS Operations Command Centre (OCC). Technical Systems Management: Monitor and maintain all electrical and mechanical systems including chilled water systems, VRV and DX systems, High-Tension and Low-Tension electrical systems. Perform data analysis on real-time data from IoT sensors, OCC dashboards, and smart energy meters. Prepare/present monthly progress of Smart FM and utilities utilisation reports to Senior Management. Sustainability & Energy Management: Identify utilities wastage, monitor waste management, recommend improvements, and develop policies for Smart FM and energy management to meet WOG and Authority’s Green Plan targets, including reporting efforts. Innovation & Smart Technologies:Manage implementation of new initiatives including smart FM technologies, sensors and IoT devices. Manage customer service-oriented support services including concierge services and logistic support for offices and events. Contract & Vendor Management: Review, manage and supervise term contracts to ensure performance, meeting KPIs/SLAs, compliance, and timely renewals across all premises. Ensure day to day safe, effective, smooth, uninterrupted operations of LTA’s premises with quality service levels and timely closure of all maintenance and logistics requests, feedbacks. To ensure high availability of all equipment/systems/services/premises. Compliance & Safety: Ensure regulatory compliance, safety standards, and uninterrupted operations at all facilities. Manage emergency operations and other duties as assigned to meet organisational objectives, including specifications review/input for new build/improvement projects concerning facility management and operations. Relocation Management: Manage phased transition of existing offices and taking over new offices and manage reinstatement and return of existing premises to landlords.
hrp|17005736|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-80f3-2a8.requirements: Tertiary qualification in facilities management/engineering with at least 8 years of relevant experience (strong ACMV/mechanical background essential). Experience in commercial office environments and large-scale facility management. Experience in data analytics for smart FM technologies and building maintenance. Proven leadership skills with successful track record in service delivery. Technically sound with knowledge of M&E maintenance, vendor management, and building regulation compliance. Certified BCA Energy Auditors, Singapore Certified Energy Managers have added advantage. Able to work weekends and after hours when required. As part of the shortlisting process for the role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and / or undergo further assessment

As owner of all related systems, you will be responsible for site inspections, cost analysis, budgeting, preparing work quotations/tender specifications, procurement of services, attending to feedback and ad-hoc decisions. You will constantly review work processes and procedures to enhance facilities operations, adopt good industry practices, and ensure compliance with government regulations. Your roles include: Integrated Facilities Management: Oversee facilities management operations including housekeeping with oversight of security operations across HQ and satellite offices through our IFMS Operations Command Centre (OCC). Technical Systems Management: Monitor and maintain all electrical and mechanical systems including chilled water systems, VRV and DX systems, High-Tension and Low-Tension electrical systems. Perform data analysis on real-time data from IoT sensors, OCC dashboards, and smart energy meters. Prepare/present monthly progress of Smart FM and utilities utilisation reports to Senior Management. Sustainability & Energy Management: Identify utilities wastage, monitor waste management, recommend improvements, and develop policies for Smart FM and energy management to meet WOG and Authority’s Green Plan targets, including reporting efforts. Innovation & Smart Technologies:Manage implementation of new initiatives including smart FM technologies, sensors and IoT devices. Manage customer service-oriented support services including concierge services and logistic support for offices and events. Contract & Vendor Management: Review, manage and supervise term contracts to ensure performance, meeting KPIs/SLAs, compliance, and timely renewals across all premises. Ensure day to day safe, effective, smooth, uninterrupted operations of LTA’s premises with quality service levels and timely closure of all maintenance and logistics requests, feedbacks. To ensure high availability of all equipment/systems/services/premises. Compliance & Safety: Ensure regulatory compliance, safety standards, and uninterrupted operations at all facilities. Manage emergency operations and other duties as assigned to meet organisational objectives, including specifications review/input for new build/improvement projects concerning facility management and operations. Relocation Management: Manage phased transition of existing offices and taking over new offices and manage reinstatement and return of existing premises to landlords.
hrp|17005736|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9cff-25c.requirements: Knowledge in facilities management/engineering with at least 5 years of relevant experience (strong ACMV/mechanical background essential). Experience in commercial office environments and large-scale facility management. Experience in data analytics for smart FM technologies and building maintenance. Proven leadership skills with successful track record in service delivery. Technically sound with knowledge of M&E maintenance, vendor management, and building regulation compliance. Certified BCA Energy Auditors, Singapore Certified Energy Managers have added advantage. Able to work weekends and after hours when required. Candidates with more experience will be considered for the higher position. As part of the shortlisting process for the role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and / or undergo further assessment

hrp|17021099|005056a3-53e2-1fd0-bdb5-de3.responsibilities: • Develop project briefs, requirements, technical specifications for the procurement of consultancy, data collection and construction contracts for projects related to coastal protection and/or building and infrastructure works. • Assist team in plan, execute and manage the entire cycle of developing project brief, tendering, proposal evaluation processes, project award and initiation processes, with focus on coastal and environmental aspects. • Understand and identify the conditions and constraints in Sentosa environment and propose feasible solutions • Project management of external consultants to carry out coastal protection, drainage and infrastructure related studies, planning and designs and including all works assigned by the supervisor. Especially manage, review and provide coastal and environmental inputs to consultants’ coastal and environmental modelling works. • Where required, conduct inspections with respective Technical professional to ensure that all works are carried out in accordance to EMMP. • Part of the team to develop, review and enhance long term coastal protection planning strategies for SDC, which include: • Identifying and assessing the risks from sea-level rise and climate change; and opportunities (eg integration of coastal protection measures with long-term land use plans); • Identifying and assessing overseas best practices, emerging risks, as well as other policies that may impact the proposed strategies; • Performing quantitative and qualitative analysis to determine implications and costs of the proposed strategies; • Formulating data management plan with Data Manager (GIS); and • Assisting operation team to plan for operational readiness on flood response • Plan and develop stakeholder engagement plans, to educate, increase awareness and get buy-in for SDC and Government’s initiatives and programmes from our stakeholders • Liaising with and providing the necessary inter-agency support to PUB, the national Coastal Protection Agency, NParks and other agencies. • Spearheading research collaborations with agencies and academic partners, including nature based solutions.
hrp|17021099|005056a3-53e2-1fd0-bdb5-de3.requirements: • Degree in Engineering (preference in Civil and Environmental Engineering) and/or Master’s Degree in Coastal Engineering, Hydro-informatics or a closely related discipline • Minimum 10 years of post-graduate experience in the construction industry with at least 5 years of relevant experience in coastal engineering • Familiar with various coastal & drainage modelling and GIS software, spatial and temporal data processing and analysis • Consultancy experience in multi-disciplinary engineering projects or infrastructure projects would be an advantage. • Possess strong written and communication skill in English and able to engage stakeholders from diverse background. This is a 3-year contract with the possibility of renewal. We regret that only shortlisted candidates will be notified.
hrp|17021099|005056a3-53e2-1fd0-bdb5-de3.description: Coastal protection planning, research and stakeholder engagement

hrp|17070944|005056a3-53e2-1fd0-bfaa-0bf.responsibilities: Perform food radioactivity testing and all related functions to support SFA food safety monitoring and surveillance programs. Expand the testing capability of the Food Radioactivity Specialist Team to cover all the relevant radionuclides specified in the Codex Alimentarius General Standard for Contaminants and Toxins in Food and Feed, which entails method establishment and method validation for the achievement of method accreditation by the Singapore Accreditation Council for alpha, beta and gamma emitting radionuclides. Implement laboratory quality assurance programs to ensure that the laboratory practices are in full compliance with ISO/IEC 17025:2017 standards. Prepare method and equipment SOPs and quality documents used by the Team. Conduct method validation for test methods and prepare method validation and measurement uncertainty reports. Prepare weekly and monthly reports to update management on significant test findings and provide risk assessments and recommendations where necessary to support SFA's standard setting and policymaking in food radioactivity regulatory control. Procurement of lab supplies and equipment to support the operations of the lab. Participate in collaboration projects with National and International partners on developing and enhancing testing capabilities for supporting the pertinent natural and artificial radionuclides surveillance programs. Deliver presentations on specialized areas and prepare manuscripts for scientific publications. Conduct training and organize proficiency testing programs for ASEAN participants as well as commercial laboratories to upgrade radionuclides testing capability in Singapore and ASEAN region.
hrp|17070944|005056a3-53e2-1fd0-bfaa-0bf.requirements: Requirements The candidate should have a BSc, MSc or PhD in Chemistry, Radiochemistry, or other related scientific fields. Good knowledge and hand-on experience in sample extraction, cleanup and detection of foodborne chemical or radiochemical hazards will be an advantage. Prior experiences with radioanalytical instruments (alpha spectrometer, liquid scintillation counter, gamma spectrometer) and Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometer will be an advantage. Prior experiences in implementing ISO/IEC 17025:2017 laboratory quality. Self-motivated, proactive, and resourceful. Able to work independently, and in a team. Organized and able to multitask. Strong written and communication skills. Proficient in MS Office applications (Word, Excel, Power Point etc.). Work Location National Centre for Food Science, 7 International Business Park, Singapore 609919.
hrp|17070944|005056a3-53e2-1fd0-bfaa-0bf.description: The mission of SFA is to ensure and secure a supply of safe food for Singapore. The National Centre for Food Science (NCFS) supports SFA’s vision of ensuring safe food for all by being a national reference laboratory on food science, conducting food safety monitoring to generate scientific data for enforcement of food regulations, support of risk assessment and protection of consumer health. NCFS oversees the application of science and technology to enable an evidence-based approach for ensuring food safety in partnership with stakeholders across the entire food chain and research institutions to address emerging food safety and security concerns. You will be part of a dynamic team of the Food Safety Rapid Response Department (FSRRD) under NCFS to provide support to SFA’s food safety regulatory testing and market monitoring programs. This is a fantastic opportunity for you to learn and apply a wide range of cutting-edge testing and diagnostic techniques to solve real world problems and safeguard the food safety for Singaporeans. The Specialist Teams under FSRRD strive to continue developing our scientific knowledge and testing capabilities to keep pace with the challenges of emerging foodborne chemical, radiochemical and biological hazards. We collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to enhance food safety standards in the region, and support food security initiatives such as high-tech farming and novel food innovation. You will be deployed to the Food Radioactivity Specialist Team under FSRRD, playing a key role in developing new analytical methods for strengthening and broadening the testing capabilities and for enabling risk assessment to support SFA’s operation needs for food safety regulatory function and market monitoring programs. Based on the operation needs of the Department and your career advancement path, there are ample job rotation opportunities to broaden your scientific knowledge and sharpen your professional skills.

hrp|17071113|005056a3-d347-1fe0-bfae-38a.responsibilities: The jobholder is responsible for the Governance, Risk, audit and process management of enterprise ICT infrastructure services systems (such as end-user devices, virtualised infrastructure, active directory, network, serve, etc.) that are across all MHA Home Team Departments (HTDs). The principal accountabilities of the job holder are: • Manage ICT Infrastructure Security Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC). Define business processes and controls. Champion IT Operation automation for compliance. • Serve as Point of Contact for ICT Project Handovers, ensuring "Security by Design". Lead new ICT security initiatives and infrastructure enhancements to comply with government policies. • Ensure vendors fulfil service levels and take corrective actions. Manage contracts to ensure vendors meet operational needs. • Identify and evaluate cost-effective technical solutions (e.g., infrastructure refresh). Manage procurement, including tender specifications, evaluation, and awards. • Manage GRC processes and documentations. Handle 24/7 Security operations with tight response times. • Lead end-to-end device deployment (laptops, etc.) across agencies. Coordinate site readiness and user communications. • Oversee OS standardization and provisioning via MDM (Intune, SCCM). Ensure devices meet security baselines (encryption, hardening). • Manage OEMs for hardware availability. Maintain 100% inventory accuracy.
hrp|17071113|005056a3-d347-1fe0-bfae-38a.requirements: • Tertiary qualification in Electronics/ Electrical Engineering, Computer Studies, or related disciplines such as ICT Technology or Cyber Security. • Minimally 1 year working experience in cyber security related programs such as audits support, risk assessments, audit findings remediation and cyber security compliance management. • In-depth understanding of desktop clients/servers, cloud infrastructure and networks, working knowledge/skills in system administration such as Microsoft Windows Server and Active Directory. Relevant certification from Microsoft and other professional bodies would be an added advantage. Personal Characteristics & Behaviours We are looking for motivated individual(s) who: • is excellent in communication (both oral and written) for diverse audiences. • ability to apply risk-based approaches to audits. • has strong project, vendor, and contract-management skills. • can work independently without the need for close supervision, able to prioritize tasks, and remain calm under pressure. • is competent, self-motivated, proactive, dedicated, and responsible. All new appointees will be appointed on a two-year contract in the first instance. We wish to inform that only shortlisted candidates will be notified within 4 weeks upon closing of the advertisement. As part of the shortlisting process for this role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment. #L1-FL1
hrp|17071113|005056a3-d347-1fe0-bfae-38a.description: HTX is the world’s first Science and Technology agency that integrates a diverse range of scientific and engineering capabilities to innovate and deliver transformative and operationally ready solutions for homeland security. As a statutory board of the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and integral to the Home Team, HTX works at the forefront of science and technology to empower Singapore’s frontline of security. Our shared mission is to amplify, augment and accelerate the Home Team’s advantage and secure Singapore as the safest place on planet earth. You play an important role in the implementation and maintenance of ICT end-user devices, networks and infrastructures for a Home Team Department (e.g. Singapore Police Force, Singapore Civil Defence Force, Singapore Prison Service, Immigration & Checkpoints Authority, etc.), ensuring their operational readiness at all times.

hrp|17090096|005056a3-d347-1fe1-809a-89f.responsibilities: Strategic Planning & Digital Transformation Leadership • Lead the Group's digital transformation roadmap and cross-cutting initiatives that span multiple departments and operational areas. • Conduct comprehensive landscape studies to understand operational challenges, evolving needs, and market trends. • Analyse research findings to identify key insights that inform strategic decision-making. • Work collaboratively with key stakeholders to redesign processes, envision future operational states, and define strategic and operational metrics. • Coordinate for HDB Digital Steering Committee secretariat operations and facilitate strategic decision-making processes. • Develop and implement comprehensive digital transformation strategies aligned with organisational goals. • Lead HDB AI and Digital Initiatives Track, ensuring strategic alignment and effective implementation. • Coordinate HDB ICT Planning including Digital Blueprint development and mapping of departments' product offices with defined timelines. • Perform feasibility studies and cost analyses to determine the viability of centralised/ synergised new products and initiatives. • Continuously scan the market for ICT trends and tools that support operations transformation, enhance user experience, improve organisational efficiency, strengthen ICT service reliability, and drive operational excellence. • Serve as coordination hub for strategic planning initiatives and facilitate steering committee activities to ensure alignment across departments. Centralised Product Development & Innovation • Generate creative and innovative ideas and concepts for new products that address identified operational needs and market opportunities. • Define comprehensive roadmaps based on vision and product specifications, including detailed design parameters, feature requirements, and performance criteria. • Create prototypes and conduct testing to validate product designs, test hypotheses, and verify functionalities. • Analyse resulting data to inform product refinements and improvements. • Experiment with emerging ICT solutions and tools, systematically evaluating their effectiveness and potential for organisational implementation. • Manage the procurement of required software, systems, and services essential for product development initiatives. • Evaluate and actively manage project risks encompassing timeliness, budget constraints, quality standards, and compatibility with HDB's operational environment. • Facilitate seamless handover of pilot deployments to operations departments, ensuring smooth integration and successful expansion. • Execute comprehensive procurement activities in accordance with established guidelines and best practices. Cross-Departmental Coordination & Integration • Coordinate Group and Department digital planning and operations meetings, ensuring strategic alignment across all business units. • Coordinate Group ICT meetings, including agenda preparation, stakeholder engagement prior to meetings, and ensuring all relevant parties are informed and aligned. • Monitor project progress and implementation status, providing regular updates to management and stakeholders. • Conduct follow-up actions from meetings and ensure timely completion of assigned tasks and deliverables. • Collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams to harness synergistic opportunities for backend systems integration. • Coordinate with diverse teams to address centralised product updates and enhancements, ensuring continuous improvement and optimal performance. • Work closely with cross-functional teams and service providers to pilot new technologies that deliver tangible benefits to the Group. • Engage with stakeholders across the organisation to align ICT initiatives with organisational goals and strategic priorities. Innovation & Technology Piloting • Develop pilot projects that showcase cross-departmental synergies and integration opportunities. • Pilot emerging technologies (AI, automation) to assess their suitability for HDB operations. • Evaluate vendor solutions and platforms through controlled pilot environments. • Test integration capabilities with existing HDB systems and processes. • Coordinate bottom-up technology idea formulation and innovation framework development. • Network with GovTech and industry players for Proof-of-Concept (POC) projects and collaborative initiatives. Digital Capability Development & Change Management • Work with stakeholders across the Group to improve digital literacy and skills through targeted training programmes and capability-building initiatives. • Develop and implement strategies to enhance digital competency levels across Group. • Facilitate knowledge transfer and best practice sharing to build organisational digital capabilities. • Support change management initiatives to drive digital adoption and transformation across the Group. • Implement effective change management strategies to ensure successful project adoption across the Group. • Use pilot projects as change management tools to demonstrate benefits and build user confidence. • Create success stories and case studies to support broader digital transformation initiatives. • Collaborate with stakeholders on culture building and competency development. System Maintenance & Support • Take responsibility for deployed centralised system design and functionalities, ensuring optimum performance and reliability across all platforms. • Perform routine and corrective maintenance activities, including software enhancements, bug fixes, comprehensive testing, and system commissioning. • Conduct detailed analyses on system functionalities to identify improvement opportunities and operational efficiencies. • Gather and address user feedback systematically, identify operational challenges and gaps in centralised systems, and implement targeted improvements. • Collaborate with departmental System Administrators to harness synergistic opportunities and expedite enhancement implementation. • Evaluate, prioritise, and manage enhancement lists to ensure strategic alignment and resource optimisation. Quality Assurance & User Experience • Conduct comprehensive user testing and monitor post-launch product performance metrics. • Gather structured user feedback and implement data-driven enhancements to improve user satisfaction. • Manage all centralised product documentation including technical specifications, user manuals, and change management collaterals. • Maintain and regularly update product documentation to reflect current system capabilities and procedural changes. Strategic Planning & Governance • Coordinate the Group Digital Work Plan, ensuring alignment with strategic objectives and operational requirements. • Work collaboratively with departments on prioritisation of digital projects and coordinate regular updates to enable close monitoring of progress and outcomes. • Conduct comprehensive monitoring and gap analysis of digital transformation initiatives. • Framework review and sustainability planning for digital transformation journey. • Benchmarking against global digital transformation leaders and industry best practices. • Stay current with industry trends, emerging technologies, cybersecurity developments, and advancements in product development methodologies. • Apply industry best practices and standards to all development and implementation activities to ensure the organisation remains competitive and secure. Data Management • Support the Chief Data Officer in managing HDB's data assets, ensuring data quality and fitness for use. • Assess data requests ensuring appropriate access controls and data governance compliance.

Successful candidates will be offered a 1+1 year contract in the first instance. Conversion to perm is dependent on good performance. hrp|17091095|005056a3-d347-1fe1-80df-f74.description: In this role, you will be managing a wide-ranging suite of applications that the Development Control Group uses. hrp|17094258|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-80ad-c09.responsibilities: You will be part of the core team that is responsible for sustaining HDB’s high level of organisational resilience to anticipate, prepare and respond to a wide spectrum of risks, operational disruptions, threats and emergencies at Whole of Government and boardwide level. These efforts would comprise of risk and incident management, business continuity and other emergency plans, delivered through iterative, user-focused methodologies. Applying product office principles, you will champion user-centricity by working with other stakeholders and partners within and outside HDB to plan, conceptualise, design, develop, and implement a new Command, Control, and Communications (C3) system as a comprehensive product solution to support effective coordination, decision-making, and communications during emergencies and crises in accordance with policies, resilience frameworks, budgetary controls, and operational requirements. You will work on the product lifecycle of the C3 system, including planning, design, development, testing, deployment, and transition to operations incl maintenance. Key works can include managing project governance, schedules, budget, procurement activities, vendor performance, contractual deliverables and overseeing system testing, exercises, and readiness onboarding/assessments, including regular progress reporting, simulation exercises and trainings/briefings to ensure a high level of organisational preparedness.

You are a self-motivated team player, with an inquisitive mind-set, good analytical, interpersonal, writing and presentation skills. Candidates with relevant experience in risk-management, operational readiness and crisis management / emergency preparedness role or experience in development and implementation of users-centric and integrated workflow system will have an added advantage. You should also be self-driven and have a strong sense of purpose and mission in yourself and work you are involved in. Successful applicants will be offered a 2 year contract for a start. Fresh graduates are welcome to apply. All applicants will be notified on whether they are shortlisted for the position within 4 weeks of the closing date of this job posting

hrp|17105974|005056a3-d347-1fe1-80e2-08e.responsibilities: • Design and implement strategic procurement and contracting strategies to meet desired outcomes in supporting MHA’s and HTX’s operations. • Work closely with the Project Management Teams (PMTs) or users from Home Team Departments (HTDs) and HTX Functions to provide professional advice on building projects and facility management services procurement including design of tender and specifications, and evaluation approach to maximise flexibility and staging for favourable tender outcomes. • Provide advice and support for contract management practices. • Collaborate with the HTDs and HTX Functions to analyse HTD and HTX procurement data, costs drivers, operational needs, industry factors, and conduct inter-departmental joint review of common requirements to drive demand aggregation initiatives and develop the most appropriate procurement strategy. • Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including PMTs, Legal and Finance to ensure governance in procurement processes. • Provide input on procurement planning, prioritisation of projects (high complexity and value) for management reporting. • Capture lessons learnt as case studies including good practices and irregularities and present for sharing and learning. • Supervise a team of Procurement Specialists in carrying out the procurement function (from preparing tender documents to contract award), and to ensure timeliness of procurement and contract formation. • Review and assess team members’ workload and coach them for professional development. • Stay up to date with market trends and advancements; costs and performance and their applications to HTDs and HTX Functions. Observe, evaluate related market trends and development, cost and performance and recommend their applications to HTDs/HTX procurements in terms of desired KPI, cost and efficiency (e.g., impact of pandemic-related expenses and construction material price impacts). • Negotiates with suppliers for strategic buys and establishment of master agreements/enterprise agreements to achieve cost effective outcomes and favourable terms and conditions for MHA and HTX.
hrp|17105974|005056a3-d347-1fe1-80e2-08e.requirements: •Possess a degree preferably with at least 8 years of relevant experience in areas of procurement ranging from acquisition of services, strategic sourcing, integrated workforce and public private partnership, preferably in the Public Built Environment Sector. •Excellent knowledge of procurement strategies, procedures, standards and guidelines specified in the Government Instruction Manual on Procurement, Finance Circulars and existing rules and regulations • Good knowledge of strategic sourcing, project management and demand aggregation activities. • Keen interest in developing knowledge and enhancing competency in the respective teams. • Able to work in a dynamic fast paced environment and manage workload well. • Strong analytical and communication skills • Must be able to work well in a team. • Min 3 years of supervisory experience in leading a team. All new hires are appointed on a two-year contract in the first instance and will be assessed and considered for permanent tenure over time, based on performance. As part of the shortlisting process for this role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment. All applicants will be updated on the status of their applications within 4 weeks upon closing of the advertisement. #LI-CW1

HTX integrates a diverse range of scientific and engineering capabilities to innovate and deliver transformative and operationally ready solutions for homeland security. hrp|17108013|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-80e8-ffa.responsibilities: You are expected to assess the vulnerability and risk; formulate the plans and solution and determine the budget required. You will be expected to collaborate with various state agencies and internal units (e.g. JTC clusters and Jurong Island tenants) in the course of work, to assess and determine the security operation requirement. When required, you will also work with the various security vendors and technical consultants to specify the technical specifications of the proposed security systems. You will also update the JI Security Master Plan based on the latest security threat environment and continue to meet state agencies policy and regulations. You will also be the planner to look into the future expansion or relocation of the JI checkpoints to meet future business demand and capacity in JI. You will be expected to staff the requirements to the management, to seek Approval of Requirements for the procurement of security systems and solutions for Jurong Island. You will develop the specification for the tender and carry out the procurement process to eventually bring in the capabilities and to operationalise the capabilities. As the Project-in-charge, you will lead and guide the team in the implementation of the project, adhering to the timeline and carry out testing and the successful commissioning of the project. You will need to be versatile and be able to work across the departments within SD for operational synergy and efficiency. Specially, you are expected to be familiar with JI checkpoint and security operations and at times be required to support ongoing security operations and project implementation held from JI Operations Centre.

hrp|17109282|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-80f3-31e.responsibilities: Manage the Digital AV Preservation system which includes a media asset management system and file-based QC to ensure every piece of content that is being archived goes through a stringent, in-depth QC process before it is archived to LTO Tape. Conduct research on developments in preservation of broadcast and digital media content, evaluate and recommend appropriate preservation processes for AV records to senior management. Seek approval and implement improvements to preservation methods and workflows. Incorporate Artificial Intelligence in areas of facial recognition, speech recognition and statistical learning to workflow systems and operations Contribute and drive the technical engagements with vendors to evaluate, verify, test and accept end-to-end OTT platform solutions Design, specify, refine and maintain the multi-screen multimedia content-based OTT client experiences on apps and devices including browsers, Android and iOS apps Ensure timely Migration of preserved records in LTO tape library. Ensure proper documentation of digitisation process and technical metadata, and perform QC checks and technical checks on the digitised files Oversee the procurement of new equipment, supplies, services for repair and periodic preventive maintenance of AV equipment needed for the preservation and migration of audio/video records. Coordinate with internal and external parties, answer queries including checking on AV equipment, recommend appropriate SLAs and explore deployment of proper equipment for preservation work. Review policies, procedures and standards for AV preservation. Review ISO-certified preservation processes and align them with international archiving practices. Explore and recommend new technologies and platforms relating to broadcast and digital media preservation in consultation with management. Plan for business continuity of NAS preservation and digitisation works as well as to prepare Sound and Moving Image Lab for emergency recovery and crisis management.
hrp|17109282|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-80f3-31e.requirements: 2-5 years of working experience in AV preservation or broadcast industry, with minimum 2 years of hands-on experience in IT related and software design development / testing cycle of IOS, Android and Web applications Experience in video conservation and preservation work in archives setting preferred. Good team player with the ability to multi-task, perform research (especially on historical topics) and present findings Excellent knowledge of video and/ or audio preservation standards/formats and compression codecs adopted internationally, with experience in practical application of standards Strong understanding of enterprise level storage architecture, drive formatting, partitioning and raids Work location will be at the National Archives of Singapore. We regret that only shortlisted candidates will be notified. Successful candidates will be appointed on a project contract until 31 Dec 2026.
hrp|17109282|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-80f3-31e.description: The National Library Board (NLB) nurtures Readers for Life, Learning Communities and a Knowledgeable Nation by promoting reading, learning and history through our network of 28 libraries across Singapore, the National Library and the National Archives of Singapore. At NLB, you can look forward to a flexible, hybrid work environment with rewarding, impactful deliverables that improve the lives of the community. With caring colleagues, you will be in an ideal environment for professional development, innovation and impact. We can offer you: • A chance to Impact the Community, bridge gaps and empower everyone with the opportunity for learning and discovery. • An opportunity to Innovate and Push Boundaries. We value ideas, curiosity and a passion for innovation to transform our libraries and archives. • An organisation that Cares for your Growth and Wellbeing through investment in staff development and wellbeing in a supportive and collaborative environment. You will be part of the team which is responsible for the management (Ingest, Quality Control [QC] and Archive), organisation and preservation of broadcast and digital media records of national and historical significance to Singapore, using the best available processes and technology that meet international AV preservation standards. The work contributes to a future ready National Archives of Singapore (NAS) under the National Library (NL)-NAS Masterplan and supports the Libraries of the Future Masterplan, which in turn supports Singapore’s national initiatives such as Smart Nation.

hrp|17122307|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-81be-9ea.description: Workforce Singapore (WSG) is developing strategies and programmes to engage community-based organisations that support Professionals, Managers, Executives and Technicians (PMETs) in their later-stage careers. Through deeper relationships, capability-building initiatives, and improved linkages to resources and opportunities, we aim to help these groups better encourage and enable PMETs in their 50s and 60s to achieve their aspirations and thrive in their later-stage careers. As Senior Manager, you will work closely with WSG’s leadership to develop strategies and programmes to strengthen transition support for Senior Workers, such as building community capabilities. You will drive the implementation of these strategies and programmes, to facilitate initiatives that encourage PMETs in their 50s and 60s to pursue later-stage career aspirations. You will lead the sourcing and engagement of these community organisations. You will be building trust, fostering collaboration, and enabling peer support structures that help senior PMETs leverage their experience, skills, and networks for continued career success. You will be part of a larger team that develops innovative means of supporting senior PMET employment.

Performance Monitoring and KPI Management - Monitor vendor performance against established KPIs or service requirements, conduct regular performance reviews and implement corrective measures to address underperformance or service gaps. 3. Service Workflow and Quality Oversight - Oversee end-to-end service workflows, including processing of high-volume service requests and referrals, conducting suitability assessments, coordinating resource allocation, and liaising with the clients' care network to optimise service delivery. 4. Stakeholder Relationship and Issue Management - Maintain effective working relationships with vendors, providing frontline support for operational queries and managing day-to-day escalation of issues or safety concerns in collaboration with supervisors for timely resolution. 5. Operational Assessment and Continuous Improvement – Analyze data, review existing vendor workflows and service delivery processes to identify risks and improvement opportunities, contribute recommendations and support implementation of solutions that enhance operational efficiency and client safety. 6. Programme Development and Policy Review - Contribute to programme development, implementation and evaluation processes, including data collection and reviews of the operational policies and procedures to ensure effectiveness and regulatory compliance. 7. Team Support - Guide support staff in executing administrative and supportive functions for vendor programmes, ensuring tasks are completed to organisational standards. 8. Crisis Response and Service Recovery – Participate in recovery efforts for critical incidents involving vendors and PSV clients, which may include direct engagement with involved persons to ensure continuity of care and implement service continuity plans.
hrp|17135905|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-81fd-be1.requirements: Requirements • Educational Background in Social Work, Psychology, or related disciplines • Minimum 1-2 years of relevant experience working with vulnerable children and families, and/or in vendor/service management roles in the social service settings • Highly organised with strong attention to detail; proficient in data management and analysis • Excellent communication and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work calmly and deliver results in stressful situations • Demonstrate professionalism, empathy and interpersonal skills when engaging both internal and external stakeholders • Proactive mindset and receptive to feedback, changes and innovation to improve processes and service delivery • A motivated team player who is also able to work independently
hrp|17135905|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-81fd-be1.description: Description of Group Looking for a workplace with passion and commitment to empower and restore lives of the vulnerable population in Singapore? Join the Rehabilitation and Protection Group (RPG)! Description of Division/Branch RPG provides statutory intervention and leads in child protection and adult protection policies and processes to safeguard Children and Young Persons (CYPs) as well as Vulnerable Adults (VAs) in Singapore. The science and art of our work remain very much firmly rooted in keeping vulnerable persons safe from harm, working in partnership with families and stakeholders such as the schools, hospitals and other community partners. The Performance and Vendor Management (PVM) unit plays a pivotal role in enhancing client safety and optimising manpower resources through the strategic outsourcing of operational functions to vendors. Your role will primarily focus on overseeing vendor services which are critical in ensuring the safety, well-being and continuity of care for PSV clients. In this role, you will maintain oversight of vendors, working closely with them to ensure effective service delivery and compliance with practice standards. As a member of the PVM team, you will also collaborate with internal stakeholders such as Operations, Service Planning, and Procurement teams to identify opportunities and align vendor services with PSV’s business needs across various functions. You will contribute to risk mitigation efforts and support the division in achieving optimal value from vendor partnerships. This role will also provide you with valuable exposure to different areas within vendor management, offering opportunities for professional development and cross-functional learning.

Working with government agencies, social service providers, and key stakeholders, you will shape and implement learning initiatives that enhance the competencies of protection professionals, ultimately contributing to better outcomes for vulnerable individuals and families. hrp|17140807|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-8296-14f.description: Join Us at MSF – A Meaningful, People-Centric Career! At MSF, our mission is to nurture and build resilient individuals, strong families, and a caring society. We offer meaningful and impactful people-centric careers in the design and delivery of policies, services and programmes. We are an all-inclusive and family friendly workplace where career growth is prioritised through a comprehensive suite of development opportunities to help our officers succeed today as well as be future-ready. We do this through various formal and informal learning and development programmes for officers to build different competencies and gain diverse work experiences within MSF, the Public as well as the Social Service Sectors. Description of Division/Branch: As part of the RPG Protective Service (PSV), the Partner & Capability Development (PCD) division drives partner management and capability building to deliver effective protection services for individuals and families experiencing violence, abuse, or neglect. We strengthen coordination of common services and enable holistic management of services run by social service agencies and vendors. The division advances evidence-based and trauma-informed practices to better support both RPG staff and the social service sector.

hrp|17151760|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-82ee-9d8.description: The Asian Civilisations Museum is the only museum in the region devoted to exploring the rich artistic heritage of Asia, especially the ancestral cultures of Singaporeans. Opened in 1997 and in its present building by the Singapore River since 2003, the museum traces its roots to the Raffles Museum, founded in the middle of 19th century. ACM focuses on the many historical and artistic connections between the cultures of Asia, and between Asia and the world. Singapore’s history as a port city that brought people together from all over the world is used as a means of examining the history of Asia. Objects on display tell stories of the trade and the exchange of ideas that were the result of international commerce, as well as the flow of religions and faith through Asia. Asian Civilisation Museum manages the Peranakan Museum. The Peranakan Museum (TPM) explores the art and culture of Peranakan communities in Southeast Asia and possesses one of the finest and most comprehensive collections of Peranakan objects. Galleries on three floors illustrate the cultural traditions and distinctive visual arts of Peranakans. In this role, you will contribute to the delivery of inspiring and engaging museum experiences by planning and managing exhibitions, gallery displays, museum rotation projects and gallery maintenance for the Asian Civilisations Museum / Peranakan Museum. You will handle artefacts and work out the best way to display them with fellow passionate museum professionals.

By the end of the programme, you will be equipped with core procurement competencies and diverse experiences, ready to drive government procurement transformation and impact national growth.

hrp|17162525|005056a3-d347-1fe1-83c0-ded.responsibilities: Key Responsibilities Corporate Finance & Treasury • Lead funding and treasury strategies and operations to ensure sufficient liquidity and cost effective financing to support operating and development needs. • Advise senior management on capital structure, and financing strategies and options, considering market conditions and financial risks. • Oversee cashflow forecasting and planning, foreign currency exposure and the investment of surplus funds within approved parameters. hrp|17186192|005056a3-d347-1fe1-84be-583.responsibilities: Strategic AI Masterplanning • Drive the strategic AI masterplan across AI domains in HTX, aligning it with MHA strategic objectives and Home Team operational needs. • Act as the central planning hub for all AI initiatives, including the review of scope, timeline and budget before approval. • Conduct strategic foresighting and scenario planning to identify emerging technology opportunities across the AI domains. Programme Management • Lead AI programmes delivery, budgeting and resource allocation; produce regular dashboards and reports on AI adoption, performance and organisational AI maturity. • Coordinate with cross-functional teams to ensure timely delivery of AI projects and initiatives. • Provide technical expertise for the procurement of AI solutions, including reviewing specifications and evaluating vendor proposals. AI Governance & Risk Management • Develop and continuously update the AI Governance strategy and playbook covering key principles such as explainability, fairness, privacy, security, accountability, robustness and sustainability. • Establish metrics, monitoring processes and KPIs and provide regular updates of AI governance key performance metrics to senior leadership. Ecosystem Development & Collaboration • Design and execute an engagement strategy to build a vibrant AI ecosystem of industry, academia and government partners. • Identify, evaluate and recommend technology and vendor solutions that meet Home Team’s AI use-case requirements. • Organise outreach events, workshops and presentations; track ecosystem engagement KPIs and produce regular status reports. Stakeholder & Cross-Agency Coordination • Liaise with Home Team Departments, Programme Management Centres, Whole-of-Government (WoG) agencies and statutory boards to align AI requirements, ensure interoperability and facilitate data sharing. • Collaborate across cross-functional teams (Solutioning, Certifications, R&D, Product Development, Platforms, Data Engineering, Infrastructure) to gather and consolidate AI inputs for AI masterplanning. Leadership & People Management • Supervise a team of AI specialists and foster a culture of innovation, collaboration and continuous learning. • Conduct presentations to senior management on AI masterplan roll-out , governance updates, programmes progress and ecosystem collaboration outcomes.
hrp|17186192|005056a3-d347-1fe1-84be-583.requirements: • Post-graduate / tertiary qualification in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, AIor related quantitative/analytical fields. • Minimum 15 years of technology development in AI-related domains, with at least 8 years in senior roles that include strategic planning, ecosystem collaboration, programme management and governance; at least 3 years delivering large-scale, multi-site AI projects. • Strong understanding of AI domains not limited to Vision AI, Embodied AI, Language AI, LLM & LMM, AI Safety & Security, and Emerging AI; experience with AI/ML, data science and analytics, and knowledge of AI Governance policies and frameworks. • Demonstrated track record of driving strategic planning cycle, formulating strategic masterplans, and driving their successful implementation with clear, quantifiable impact. • Demonstrated track record of building strategic partnerships, evaluating vendor solutions, negotiating contracts and leading collaborative AI initiatives with industry, academia and government partners. • Experience in procurement, budgeting, financial tracking and resource allocation for AI programmes. • Excellent verbal and written communication; ability to provide briefings and influence senior stakeholders across HTX and Home Team departments; strong facilitation and interpersonal skills. • Understanding of Home Team departmental business and technical requirements; familiarity with homeland-security contexts. • Good strategic foresight & innovation. • Excellent cross-agency collaboration & communication. • Comfortable to travel occasionally. hrp|17186192|005056a3-d347-1fe1-84be-583.description: The Deputy Director will provide strategic leadership across AI masterplanning, AI governance, and AI collaboration and programme management. For AI governance, the Deputy Director will establish robust frameworks that embeds responsible AI practices throughout HTX’s initiatives. For AI collaboration and programme management, the role will foster strategic AI collaboration with industry, academia and other government agencies, and programme manage end to end, cross functional AI projects. Together, these efforts will deliver AI solutions that support our public safety mission, improve citizen experience, and increase operational productivity.

hrp|17187112|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-87a2-151.responsibilities: Responsibilities: • Be a member in the OM team for the day-to-day operations and management of office building, facilities, security, projects and office space planning in AGC. • Oversees and manage the Integrated Facilities Management (IFM) vendor and administration of the contract to ensure maintenance of the office premises is efficiently managed and in accordance to contract requirements. • Ensures vendors meet the contractual obligations and goods/ services are delivered in accordance with the service agreements. • Manages current processes and systems and to develop and execute improvement plans to enhance operations and internal stakeholder satisfaction and engagement. • Oversees the management of office equipment and furniture, maintenance of Mechanical and Electrical services/ systems, Fire protection system, VOIP systems, AVVC system and facilities operations with the in-house IFM, including service requests, and fault reporting. • Oversees the testing and maintenance of the Fire Alarm System, Fire Protection System and PA System, including comms to affected officers. • Management of public utilities and telecommunications usage including verifying and monitoring payment. • Oversees the management/ stock take of AGC fixed assets and inventories and Records Management filing in accordance with relevant guidelines. • Prepares AOR papers, ITQ/ ITT specifications, calling, evaluating and award of tenders for contracts and putting up approval papers for the procurement of items/ contracts under the portfolio. • Provides support in other portfolio such as projects management, events/logistics management, workplace safety and health, emergency preparedness and inventory stock management (where required). • Performs any other duties assigned by the Operations Department.
hrp|17187112|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-87a2-151.requirements: Requirements: • Qualifications in Building, Projects & Facilities Management, Mechanical & Electrical Engineering, or equivalent. • Minimum 3 years of relevant working experience in managing IFM/ MEP system/ project management or equivalent. • Familiar in government procurement and financial Instruction Manuals is preferred. • Possess good writing and communication skills. • Familiar with the use of Microsoft Office applications. • Positive mindset, meticulous, result-oriented and analytical. • Strong team player and ability to work independently. Our Commitment to You The AGC offers a salary commensurate with your experience and qualifications, Annual Variable bonuses, performance bonuses and annual increments based on merit. We invest in our officers and support their career aspirations so that they can reach their fullest potential. We also place great importance on our officers’ physical and mental well-being through work-life harmony programmes. Successful candidates will be appointed on a contract basis in the first instance. Should you encounter difficulty in applying for this role, please email us directly at AGC_HR_Recruit@agc.gov.sg before the closing date of this job posting. Kindly attach your resume and indicate this position you are keen on in the email subject.

hrp|17188502|005056a3-d347-1fe1-84c4-678.responsibilities: Key Responsibilities: (a) Engage the industry/vendors to better understand the industry readiness and best practices in specific sectors (namely facilities management sectors such as cleaning, landscaping, infrastructure maintenance etc.); (b) Develop negotiation strategies and negotiate with suppliers to secure favorable terms, pricing or service levels for the Government, while ensuring there is sufficient room for the suppliers to build their capabilities in the industry; (c) Manage the project and procurement process, while ensuring compliance with IM on Procurement and the agency’s procurement processes; (d) Oversee the complete procurement lifecycle, from industry engagement through to evaluation and awarding of the procurement contracts; (e) Manage and monitor contractors’ performance against performance indicators and dispute resolution with contractors; (f) Proper contract management, including the management of contract variations and exercise options, and ensure timely renewal or termination of contracts; (g) Regular contract reviews and risk assessments should be conducted to identify opportunities for improvement and mitigate potential issues; (h) Working with internal (e.g. Finance and relevant policy Divisions, and Senior Management) and external stakeholders (e.g. fellow Government agencies, and suppliers) to support the project; and (i) Any other matters related to the project.
hrp|17188502|005056a3-d347-1fe1-84c4-678.requirements: Functional Skills: (a) Good understanding of Public Sector procurement and finance would be an advantage (b) Prior experience with Project Management would be an advantage (c) At least three years of experience in the public or private sector procurement Qualifications & Others: (a) Confident communicator with good writing and presentation skills (b) Positive attitude and self-motivated (c) Good interpersonal skills, and able to effectively interact and build relationships with diverse internal and external stakeholders (d) Able to work well independently and as a team (e) Possess a self-driven attitude and being instrumental/ resourcefulness with problem solving
hrp|17188502|005056a3-d347-1fe1-84c4-678.description: We are looking for an experienced Procurement officer to carry out procurement activities for the Integrated Operations (IO) team in the Municipal Services Office, such as engaging the industry for specific sectors, negotiating with vendors and managing the IO contracts.

hrp|17196968|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-84ea-1e3.responsibilities: [What you will be working on] Key Responsibilities: 1. Lead the Singapore Tourism Accelerator (STA) a) Coordination with Innovation Vendors: Collaborate with appointed innovation vendor to ensure a seamless global sourcing and matchmaking process between tech companies and tourism industry stakeholders. Ensure that the technology solutions align with the industry’s needs and the strategic goals of STB. b) Procurement Management: Oversee procurement aspects, including budget tracking and contract management of the appointed innovation vendor. Ensure that all procurement activities comply with STB's guidelines and are executed efficiently. c) Matchmaking and Pilot Management: Lead the matchmaking process to ensure the right solutions are paired with industry stakeholders for testing. Oversee the management of pilots, ensuring that the milestones are met, timelines are adhered to, and any roadblocks are addressed. d) Demo Day Coordination: Plan and execute Demo Day to showcase the proven solutions, including managing the logistics, coordinating with participants, and ensuring impactful presentations that demonstrate the value of each proven tech solution. 2. Overall Lead for Tcube LEARN Pillar As the lead for the Tcube LEARN pillar, you will oversee Tcube’s content strategy and events, ensuring they inspire, educate, and drive digital transformation within the tourism industry. Your role will involve strategic oversight and hands-on execution of key initiatives to effectively showcase emerging tech solutions, successful pilots, and real-world applications in the tourism sector. a) Tcube Content Strategy: -Lead the development and execution of a comprehensive content strategy that highlights Tcube’s initiatives, including case studies, articles, research papers, and videos. -Collaborate with external partners (tech companies, universities, and industry experts) to produce high-quality content aligned with Tcube’s strategic goals. -Oversee the documentation and presentation of all Tcube pilot projects to clearly demonstrate their impact on the tourism industry. b) Tcube Events: -Identify and leverage relevant industry events, conferences, and forums to showcase Tcube’s work. -Lead the planning and execution of events such as panel sessions, workshops, and presentations, ensuring they align with the following objectives: ​-Inspiration: Showcase innovative technologies to inspire fresh thinking and new applications in the tourism sector. -Learning: Provide opportunities for stakeholders to build knowledge and practical tools for navigating digital transformation. -Showcase: Present successful case studies and tangible technology solutions that have positively impacted the industry. -Transformation: Promote a culture of change by equipping stakeholders with the skills necessary to drive digital transformation within their organizations. 3) Tcube Advisor for Core Tourism Industries As the Tcube Advisor for one of the Core Tourism Industries, you will play a pivotal role in shaping its technology landscape. You will provide strategic insights and recommendations to STB line units, helping them adopt and implement cutting-edge technologies to drive operational efficiency and enhance the tourism experience. a) Industry Tech Landscape Scan: -Conduct regular scans of the tech landscape in key priority areas to understand the trends and solutions that are relevant to the industry. -Stay informed on the latest technological advancements in the priority areas and ensure that these developments are incorporated into Tcube’s strategies for industry transformation. b) Identify Key Solutions and Tech Companies: -Work with tech experts to identify and evaluate tech solutions that address the pain points of core industries. -Build and maintain strong relationships with tech providers and partners to create a pipeline of solutions that can support the digital transformation of the tourism sector. c) Support Line Units on tech adoption: -Provide guidance and strategic advice to STB line units, helping them adopt and implement new technologies to improve operations, increase efficiency, and enhance visitor experiences. -Work closely with line units to ensure smooth technology integration and monitor its impact on business outcomes.
hrp|17196968|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-84ea-1e3.requirements: [What we are looking for] -At least 2 years experience in marketing, project management or stakeholder management -Strong project management skills, with ability to deliver multiple projects. -Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with ability to maintain relationships with potential partners and apply negotiation tactics and risk assessment in developing partnership arrangements -Good business acumen and analytical skills to think strategically and make sound judgements -Ideally to have some experience in marketing -Independent and highly motivated individual -Collaborative mindset with the ability to work in a team-oriented environment -Strong command of written and spoken English
hrp|17196968|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-84ea-1e3.description: [What the role is] We are looking for a proactive and results-driven individual to lead several key initiatives that support STB’s tourism innovation efforts. Tcube, or the Tourism Technology Transformation Cube, brings STB’s digital initiatives, resources and thought-leadership content onto a single platform to support our sector’s digital transformation. As the co-manager of the Singapore Tourism Accelerator (STA), you will be responsible for overseeing the accelerator’s operations, including managing the innovation vendor, the procurement process, matchmaking of stakeholders with tech companies, pilot management, and executing the Demo Day. This will involve close collaboration with industry stakeholders to ensure successful matchmaking and meaningful pilot outcomes. Additionally, you will take the lead in driving the Tcube LEARN pillar, which includes curating and delivering content and events designed to inspire and educate the industry on digital transformation. In this role, you will partner with key tech companies and industry stakeholders to create thought leadership content, such as case study articles and videos. You will also be responsible for capturing and documenting the outcomes of all Tcube pilots to showcase the successful implementation of technology within the tourism sector. Beyond content creation, you will strategically assess opportunities for Tcube to engage industry stakeholders at key events and forums, driving thought leadership through panel sessions, workshops, and showcases. Success in this role means effectively driving industry engagement through impactful content and events, managing cross-functional collaborations with internal and external stakeholders, and ensuring that Tcube’s initiatives contribute to the digital transformation of the tourism sector. This position requires someone who is both strategic and operational, capable of managing multiple projects, and delivering tangible outcomes that elevate industry tech transformation.

hrp|17196968|005056a3-d347-1fe1-86a1-733.responsibilities: [What you will be working on] Key Responsibilities: 1. Lead the Singapore Tourism Accelerator (STA) a) Coordination with Innovation Vendors: Collaborate with appointed innovation vendor to ensure a seamless global sourcing and matchmaking process between tech companies and tourism industry stakeholders. Ensure that the technology solutions align with the industry’s needs and the strategic goals of STB. b) Procurement Management: Oversee procurement aspects, including budget tracking and contract management of the appointed innovation vendor. Ensure that all procurement activities comply with STB's guidelines and are executed efficiently. c) Matchmaking and Pilot Management: Lead the matchmaking process to ensure the right solutions are paired with industry stakeholders for testing. Oversee the management of pilots, ensuring that the milestones are met, timelines are adhered to, and any roadblocks are addressed. d) Demo Day Coordination: Plan and execute Demo Day to showcase the proven solutions, including managing the logistics, coordinating with participants, and ensuring impactful presentations that demonstrate the value of each proven tech solution. 2. Overall Lead for Tcube LEARN Pillar As the lead for the Tcube LEARN pillar, you will oversee Tcube’s content strategy and events, ensuring they inspire, educate, and drive digital transformation within the tourism industry. Your role will involve strategic oversight and hands-on execution of key initiatives to effectively showcase emerging tech solutions, successful pilots, and real-world applications in the tourism sector. a) Tcube Content Strategy: -Lead the development and execution of a comprehensive content strategy that highlights Tcube’s initiatives, including case studies, articles, research papers, and videos. -Collaborate with external partners (tech companies, universities, and industry experts) to produce high-quality content aligned with Tcube’s strategic goals. -Oversee the documentation and presentation of all Tcube pilot projects to clearly demonstrate their impact on the tourism industry. b) Tcube Events: -Identify and leverage relevant industry events, conferences, and forums to showcase Tcube’s work. -Lead the planning and execution of events such as panel sessions, workshops, and presentations, ensuring they align with the following objectives: ​-Inspiration: Showcase innovative technologies to inspire fresh thinking and new applications in the tourism sector. -Learning: Provide opportunities for stakeholders to build knowledge and practical tools for navigating digital transformation. -Showcase: Present successful case studies and tangible technology solutions that have positively impacted the industry. -Transformation: Promote a culture of change by equipping stakeholders with the skills necessary to drive digital transformation within their organizations. 3) Tcube Advisor for Core Tourism Industries As the Tcube Advisor for one of the Core Tourism Industries, you will play a pivotal role in shaping its technology landscape. You will provide strategic insights and recommendations to STB line units, helping them adopt and implement cutting-edge technologies to drive operational efficiency and enhance the tourism experience. a) Industry Tech Landscape Scan: -Conduct regular scans of the tech landscape in key priority areas to understand the trends and solutions that are relevant to the industry. -Stay informed on the latest technological advancements in the priority areas and ensure that these developments are incorporated into Tcube’s strategies for industry transformation. b) Identify Key Solutions and Tech Companies: -Work with tech experts to identify and evaluate tech solutions that address the pain points of core industries. -Build and maintain strong relationships with tech providers and partners to create a pipeline of solutions that can support the digital transformation of the tourism sector. c) Support Line Units on tech adoption: -Provide guidance and strategic advice to STB line units, helping them adopt and implement new technologies to improve operations, increase efficiency, and enhance visitor experiences. -Work closely with line units to ensure smooth technology integration and monitor its impact on business outcomes.

hrp|17197814|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-8dfc-3b9.description: Join Us at MSF for A Meaningful, People-Centric Career! At MSF, our mission is to nurture and build resilient individuals, strong families, and a caring society. We offer meaningful and impactful people-centric careers in the design and delivery of policies, services and programmes. We are an all-inclusive and family friendly workplace where career growth is prioritised through a comprehensive suite of development opportunities to help our officers succeed today as well as be future-ready. We do this through various formal and informal learning and development programmes for officers to build different competencies and gain diverse work experiences within MSF, the Public as well as the Social Service Sectors. You will be part of the Rehabilitation and Protection Group (RPG) that undertakes the statutory functions in the rehabilitation of adult and youth offenders, and the protection of children, families and vulnerable adults (VAs). Guided by our mission to prevent harm, protect and rehabilitate individuals, and strengthen families at risk, RPG strives toward its vision of transformed lives and safe, thriving families. Description of Branch: Partner and Capability Development Branch The Partner and Capability Development (PCD) Branch focuses on building the collective capabilities of staff and partner agencies. The team seeks to enhance the coordination of common services, enabling integrated management of partners, vendors and related stakeholders. Future Capability Development Section/ Sector Development Team You will be part of the Future Capability Development Section/ Sector Development Team that oversees the capability building of the Rehabilitative Service’s sector partners, namely the Social Service Agencies that deliver pre-Court Diversionary Programmes and pre-Family Guidance Order (FGO) services, Voluntary Children’s Homes (VCH) and Hostels, and Responsible Gambling providers (RG). As part of capability building efforts, the Sector Development Team also delivers trainings to support sector partners in delivering services and MSF-funded programmes to clients. We are looking for dynamic individuals who share our passion in supporting the rehabilitation of our beneficiaries and working closely with our partners.

hrp|17197814|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-8dfc-3e1.description: Join Us at MSF for A Meaningful, People-Centric Career! At MSF, our mission is to nurture and build resilient individuals, strong families, and a caring society. We offer meaningful and impactful people-centric careers in the design and delivery of policies, services and programmes. We are an all-inclusive and family friendly workplace where career growth is prioritised through a comprehensive suite of development opportunities to help our officers succeed today as well as be future-ready. We do this through various formal and informal learning and development programmes for officers to build different competencies and gain diverse work experiences within MSF, the Public as well as the Social Service Sectors. You will be part of the Rehabilitation and Protection Group (RPG) that undertakes the statutory functions in the rehabilitation of adult and youth offenders, and the protection of children, families and vulnerable adults (VAs). Guided by our mission to prevent harm, protect and rehabilitate individuals, and strengthen families at risk, RPG strives toward its vision of transformed lives and safe, thriving families. Description of Branch: Partner and Capability Development Branch The Partner and Capability Development (PCD) Branch focuses on building the collective capabilities of staff and partner agencies. The team seeks to enhance the coordination of common services, enabling integrated management of partners, vendors and related stakeholders. Future Capability Development Section/ Sector Development Team You will be part of the Future Capability Development Section/ Sector Development Team that oversees the capability building of the Rehabilitative Service’s sector partners, namely the Social Service Agencies that deliver pre-Court Diversionary Programmes and pre-Family Guidance Order (FGO) services, Voluntary Children’s Homes (VCH) and Hostels, and Responsible Gambling providers (RG). As part of capability building efforts, the Sector Development Team also delivers trainings to support sector partners in delivering services and MSF-funded programmes to clients. We are looking for dynamic individuals who share our passion in supporting the rehabilitation of our beneficiaries and working closely with our partners.

hrp|17293628|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-88d4-4ab.responsibilities: We are seeking a proactive and passionate individual to lead the development and implementation of central policies that elevate leadership and workforce excellence across the Government Procurement function. Key Responsibilities Leadership and Talent Development • Drive the implementation of leadership and talent development strategies for the Government Procurement function, including leadership rotations, succession planning, and talent engagement initiatives to build a strong leadership pipeline across agencies. • Serve as the secretariat for the Joint Finance and Procurement Talent Development Committee and act as the primary liaison with HR counterparts across agencies to coordinate and implement talent initiatives effectively.
