hrp|17307047|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-89a1-061.responsibilities: SM/AD shall perform the following Daily Procurement Operations: Managing procurement requests from laboratory teams, processing purchase orders within approved budgets, and coordinating with suppliers to ensure timely delivery of laboratory supplies and equipment. This includes maintaining inventory levels, monitoring expenditure against budget allocations, and preventing supply shortages that could disrupt testing activities. Contract Management and Vendor Relations: Negotiating contracts with suppliers, managing vendor performance, conducting regular contract reviews, and building strategic partnerships with key suppliers. This involves ensuring all agreements meet regulatory requirements, deliver value for money, and align with budgetary constraints whilst optimising cost-effectiveness. Regulatory Compliance and Quality Assurance: Ensuring all procured laboratory supplies comply with Healthcare Services Regulations, Biological Agents and Toxin Act, and ISO 15189 standards whilst maintaining cost efficiency. This includes maintaining documentation, conducting compliance audits, managing budget implications of regulatory requirements, and working with regulatory bodies when required. Strategic Planning and Process Improvement: Developing procurement strategies aligned with laboratory operational needs and financial parameters, implementing process improvements, and providing advisory services to laboratory users. This involves forecasting procurement needs, budget planning, conducting market research to identify cost-effective solutions, and ensuring optimal resource allocation. Stakeholder Coordination: Liaising between laboratory teams, CDA business partners in Procurement and Finance, and external vendors to ensure seamless service delivery and financial accountability. This includes managing expectations, resolving conflicts, monitoring budget performance, and facilitating communication across different departments. Emergency Response and Contingency Planning: Managing urgent procurement situations within emergency budget provisions to prevent operational disruptions and developing contingency plans for critical supplies to maintain laboratory operations continuity whilst ensuring financial controls remain in place.
hrp|17307047|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-89a1-061.requirements: At least 3-6 years handling procurement and budget management in healthcare environment with a proven record in leading the procurement team and overseeing financial planning processes Good understanding of government procurement policies, financial regulations, and end-to-end procurement, contract management, and budget administration Knowledge in supply chain management, or equivalent with knowledge of budgetary principles and financial management Excellent organisation skills and attention to details in procurement processes, contract review, and budget monitoring and reporting Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills (written and oral Ability to work effectively in a multi-disciplinary team and in collaboration with internal and external stakeholders, including finance and procurement departments. Committed to their work with a proactive and resilient attitude towards achieving procurement objectives within budgetary constraints and financial accountability standards As part of the shortlisting process for this role, candidates may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment.
hrp|17307047|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-89a1-061.description: • The SM/AD play a pivotal role in sustaining uninterrupted laboratory operations and involves leading end-to-end procurement, contract management, and budget oversight services whilst collaborating closely with laboratory teams and business partners to deliver strategic procurement solutions and financial stewardship. • The successful candidate will manage vendor relationships, ensure compliance with Healthcare Services Regulations, Biological Agents and Toxin Act, and ISO 15189 standards, whilst providing proactive planning and advisory services to support the laboratory's daily operations. • This role offers the opportunity to drive operational excellence through innovative procurement strategies and stakeholder management in a fast-paced healthcare environment.

hrp|17318462|005056a3-d347-1fe1-8f9e-d28.responsibilities: Design Management Support in conducting feasibility studies for sustainable design and space planning, fit-out and infrastructure projects which will encompass budgeting, obtaining funding approval, design, project programming, procurement, regulatory compliance, design review and quality assurance. Work with internal and external stakeholders to identify requirements and propose conceptual design for the Campus Masterplan and Campus Rejuvenation projects and integrate them into project briefs and designs. Evaluate and recommend appropriate sustainable design and space planning solutions to meet the project objectives, requirements and budget. Review, challenge and value-add on the designs/specification/drawings submitted by consultants and contractors to achieve quality, compliance and value for money. Manage and review architecture, space planning, interior design and material proposals from consultants and contractors, and to ensure compliance to specifications and code requirements. Provide technical support for special projects and cross-functional initiatives. Strategic Planning and Project Management Provide overall strategic planning and project management support, which encompasses fund management, procurement, design development, consultancy and construction management, commissioning and project handover. Liaise and coordinate with internal and external stakeholders on project requirements and compliances. This will include remodeling of space in phases, planning and managing processes for funding approvals, consultations and clearances with authorities and government agencies, seeking approval from NYP’s management and oversight committees. Liaise and coordinate with consultants and contractors and monitor the timeliness of the deliverables for implementation of the project. Handling and managing project data and information, including organizing data for analysis and management reporting, ensuring proper documentation and filing for future records. Monitor and update project programme and progress, including dashboard development and control for management reporting. Assist in the development of a Building Information Modeling (BIM) framework and oversee the implementation. Strategic Planning and Project Management ​ Manage design and interface coordination through different project phases to ensure operational continuity. Review project schedules and ensure minimal disruption to operations. Attend consultant and site meetings with the Project Team and carry out site inspections to ensure compliance with sustainability goals, quality standards, project timeline and budget. Manage external/outsourced resources (consultants and site supervisory staff) to execute the projects. Ensure that contractors carry out work in a safe manner with the necessary risk assessments and workplace safety measures in place to manage project risks. Provide technical support to stakeholders in the resolution of technical issues when needed. Undertake any other tasks or responsibilities as required by Management in the course of work.

hrp|17318463|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-8dee-f4a.responsibilities: Role Overview In this role, you will lead initiatives to integrate upstream operational systems into accurate, timely, and compliant financial records and reporting. You will work closely with finance teams, system managers, IT partners, and internal stakeholders to deliver sustainable digital finance solutions that enhance efficiency, transparency, and accountability in the use of public funds. Key Responsibilities Finance Systems Integration & Digital Enablement Actively configure, enhance, and maintain finance system capabilities, including automation, AI‑enabled insights, data integrity, end‑to‑end traceability, and long‑term solution sustainability. Collaborate with finance users, system managers, and IT partners to translate policy, operational, and reporting requirements into well‑governed system, integration, and AI-supported solutions. Proactively implement and integrate emerging digital tools such as data analytics and automation). Conduct risk assessments and design controls as foundational elements of solution development from the outset. Process Optimisation and Continuous Improvement Drive finance and procurement process transformation initiatives to reduce manual work, improve processing efficiency, and strengthen internal controls and compliance, leveraging automation and AI where appropriate. Analyse finance process flows to identify opportunities for intelligent automation, standardisation, and risk reduction. Develop and maintain clear process maps and documentation to facilitate approvals, training, change management and audit discussions. Oversee system administration duties, including user access management, periodic access reviews, and compliance with segregation‑of‑duties requirements, including controls over AI-enabled workflows. Data Stewardship Manage financial datasets with a strong focus on data accuracy, completeness, auditability, and compliance with data governance standards. Support the end‑to‑end system including requirements gathering, user acceptance testing, implementation, and post‑implementation review. Stakeholder Engagement & Change Support Engage stakeholders across finance, IT, and professional groups to align digital and AI-enabled transformation initiatives with organisational priorities and operating realities. Contribute to change management activities, including the creation of user communications, development of training materials, and provision of post‑implementation support to ensure sustainable adoption of new processes, systems and AI-supported ways of working.
hrp|17318463|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-8dee-f4a.requirements: Professional Experience At least 5 years of relevant experience in finance transformation, ERP implementation, finance systems integration, or product‑related roles supporting finance or procurement functions. Practical experience working within regulated, audit‑intensive, or public‑sector environments is preferred, particularly where strong governance and compliance requirements apply. Proficiency in using Microsoft 365 tools (such as workflow automation, collaboration, documentation) to support process improvement and cross‑functional projects. Functional Knowledge Sound understanding of core finance processes, particularly Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable, and their integration with upstream operational systems. Working knowledge of financial controls, segregation‑of‑duties principles, access management, and audit expectations. Familiarity with end‑to‑end system lifecycles, including requirements gathering, user acceptance testing, implementation, and post‑implementation review.
hrp|17318463|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-8dee-f4a.description: As Senior Manager / Manager (Finance Transformation), you will be part of the Finance and Procurement department, which supports the accounting, finance, and procurement functions of the organisation. The Finance Transformation function plays a key role in strengthening public financial management by modernising finance systems, improving end-to-end processes, and embedding robust governance and controls.

hrp|17332512|005056a3-d347-1fe1-8a9a-836.responsibilities: He/She is responsible for the following: Governance • Ensure that the systems within HTSC are compliant to the latest policies and standards. • Conduct of timely Vulnerability Assessment (VA), Penetration Testing (PT) and RMM (Risk Management Methodology) in accordance to IM8 requirements based on system classification. • Maintain Risk Register and ensure that residual risks that cannot be remediated are accepted by the approving authority. • Ensure that all evidence and artifacts are documented and stored for audit purposes. • Propose, review and monitor existing and new KPIs. • Any other work that is required for the governance of HTSC Operations. Exercises Coordination and Development • Work closely with respective Home Team Departments (HTDs) by leading the planning, design and conduct of HTD exercise programmes to raise overall cyber readiness of the Home Team to mitigate any potential cyber-attacks. • Supervision of external consultants’ work to ensure that exercise objectives and outcomes are achieved. • Assist in the planning and coordination of various sectoral and national level exercises that are required by CSA CCoP 2.0 and GovTech IM8. • Conduct of annual Cybersecurity Exercises with HTDs • Conduct of Training Workshops for all Exercise Participants • Conduct of Crisis Communications Workshop(s) for MHA Communications Representatives Exercises Planning • Assist in the procurement of professional services for conduct of cybersecurity exercises for MHA • Co-manage the various exercise requirements across the four domains of HTSC and ensuring the vendors can deliver as per service level agreements. • Establishing engagement sessions with project management team for introduction and understanding of nominated systems. • Working with stakeholders to identify cyber risks and designing threat scenarios which are realistic and relatable, based on the emerging threats and risk assessment. • Develop the contents for enhanced e-Learning course modules. • Plan and deliver the training cycle to ensure that exercise fatigue to be kept to the minimum. • Developing and reviewing evaluation methodology for cyber exercise.
hrp|17332512|005056a3-d347-1fe1-8a9a-836.requirements: • Degree in Computer Science or IT-related equivalent. • Certifications in Cybersecurity and Networks are preferred. • Government or Home Team Ops knowledge and good understanding of their systems & networks are preferred. • Strong effective communications skills. • Good time management and organisational skills. • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills. • A team player with the ability to work autonomously. All new hires are appointed on a two-year contract in the first instance and will be assessed and considered for permanent tenure over time, based on performance. As part of the shortlisting process for this role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment. All applicants will be updated on the status of their applications within 4 weeks upon closing of the advertisement. #L1-FL1
hrp|17332512|005056a3-d347-1fe1-8a9a-836.description: The job-holder will work closely with Head (Governance & Exercises), in the governance of HTSC Operations and to ensure the crisis preparedness of Home Team Departments (HTDs) through regular training and exercises. Job-holder will be part of a closely knitted team to successfully implement the Enhanced Exercise Regime for MHA, as well as keeping HTSC Operations compliant to statutory policies and standards.

hrp|17336257|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-8aaa-2e4.responsibilities: Manage the day-to-day operations of Former Ford Factory (FFF), including overseeing cashless machines, visitor reception, closing reports, daily compound checks for defects, and content and publicity updates. Drive visitor engagement by conceptualising promotional programmes and outreach initiatives, identifying target customer segments to meet FFF visitorship KPIs, while also ensuring timely response to CRM inquiries and leading engaging tours. Elevate the visitor experience by providing comprehensive training and mentorship to volunteer docents in delivering engaging commentary, while actively monitoring their performance and gathering visitor feedback during tours. Staff management: Supervise and coordinate operations staff, liaising with manpower agencies recruitment and resignations, training, roster planning, budget tracking and requests, billing, and covering counter duty when necessary. Finance and procurement: This involves budget planning and monitoring, daily reconciliation of admission fees, and procurement of operational items for FFF. Manage inventory, fixed assets, and artefacts. This includes ensuring stocktake of assets, monitoring wear and tear of furniture and furnishings, procuring replacements, tracking inventory and return timelines, and planning yearly condition checks for collection maintenance. Provide support for building matters, such as conducting regular site visits to identify issues pertaining to infrastructure and maintenance works. Any other duties assigned.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Good command of a second language would be an added advantage. Meticulous and self-driven, with the abilities to manage operational matters especially in problem solving and meeting FFF’s operational needs. hrp|17336257|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-8aaa-2e4.description: The National Library Board (NLB) nurtures Readers for Life, Learning Communities and a Knowledgeable Nation by promoting reading, learning and history through our network of 28 libraries across Singapore, the National Library and the National Archives of Singapore. At NLB, you can look forward to a flexible, hybrid work environment with rewarding, impactful deliverables that improve the lives of the community. With caring colleagues, you will be in an ideal environment for professional development, innovation and impact. We can offer you: • A chance to Impact the Community, bridge gaps and empower everyone with the opportunity for learning and discovery. • An opportunity to Innovate and Push Boundaries. We value ideas, curiosity and a passion for innovation to transform our libraries and archives. • An organisation that Cares for your Growth and Wellbeing through investment in staff development and wellbeing in a supportive and collaborative environment. You will be part of the team responsible in overseeing the administration, operations, management and programming of the Former Ford Factory (FFF), a World War II permanent gallery, which contributes to NLB’s strategic thrust to achieve excellence in Singapore content and a nation that knows our history. Location: 351 Upper Bukit Timah Rd, Singapore 588192 Division: National Archives of Singapore / Corporate Development (Former Ford Factory)

hrp|17336259|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-8aaa-2f6.responsibilities: Duties & Responsibilities The duties and responsibilities include (but not limited to): Assist to administer and control the pre- and post-contracts management of planning and implementation of all estates management contracts of all PA properties. Assists the supervisor to implement, monitor and manage the procurement for goods and services including maintenance and construction services to ensure compliance of Governmental procurement and financial procedures. Formulate contract strategies and policies including establish good governance standards and processes. Lead the compliance management and procedures on contract to ensure effectiveness and alignment to Public Sector Standards Conditions of Contract (PSSCOC), Government Instruction Manual (IMs), PA’s policies/procedures and relevant authorities (e.g. Building & Construction Authority) requirements. Prepares, checks and reviews quotation / tender documents to ensure that the documents comply with the PSSCOC, Government IMs, PA’s policies/procedures and to meet the operational needs of the PA. Calls, evaluates and awards quotations and tenders. Tracks and processes variation orders to the contract in accordance with the PSSCOC, Government IMs, PA’s policies/procedures and contractual provisions. Attends site meetings to ensure contractual requirements are adhered to by managing agents, consultants, contractors and etc. Monitors and manages contracts/projects within approved cost/budget. Seeks funding approval for increase in project/contract costs, where required. Monitors and maintains cashflow projection of the contract/project. Checks and processes consultant/contractors’ claims to ensure accurate and timely disbursement of payments. Creates contract/project accounts, upload budget and manages virement requests and budget-related requirements in PA’s financial system. Assists in post-contract management and jointly monitors with Facilities/Projects Section on the submissions of “as-built” drawings, warranties, Operations and Maintenance manual and etc. required under the contracts. Oversees finalisation of project accounts and seeks approval for closure of project accounts. Prepares submission of Development Project In-Progress (DPIP) for closure of FY and capitalisation of fixed assets on project completion. Develops and maintains an updated and accurate contract document and records management system for the Division. Lead and oversees in audits conducted by both internal and external auditors on contracts/projects. Other Duties Other ad-hoc duties not covered under main responsibilities and duties. Covers the duties of the Assistant Director during period of absence. Provides mentorship and guidance to other colleagues. Represents in Task Forces/Committees as required. Perform other duties as and when assigned by senior officers.
hrp|17336259|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-8aaa-2f6.requirements: Knowledge & Skills The minimum education and experience profile required by the job-holder to perform on the job. Education - Professional qualifications in Building, Project Management, Construction Management, Quantity Surveying or other building related disciplines. Experience - Preferably minimum of five years of relevant experience in contract administration and management of building, facilities or estates projects and/or building maintenance. Good track record particularly in projects using PSSCOC or possess relevant experience working in government agencies or consultancy firms. Others - Proficient in MS Words, Excel, PowerPoint and other relevant computer skills. Good command of English language with strong written and presentation skill. Experince in construction procurement and familiarity with BCA’s procurement frameworks (PQM, QFM, etc). Knowledge of Government Instruction Manual is preferred. Knowledge of PSSCOC is preferred. Must have good organisational, conceptualisation, communication and inter-personal skills. Able to work independently with good time management. Effective team player, able to multi-task and prioritize daily workload. Knowledge in GeBIZ / Workday system is an advantage. Good working attitude and willing to learn. Only shortlisted candidates will be notified. Successful candidates will be given a 3-year contract.

hrp|17337514|005056a3-d347-1fe1-8ab2-918.responsibilities: The jobholder will collaborate with various teams (within HTX and across Home Teams) and is responsible to: • Develop enterprise sensemaking application with video/data analytics, AL/ML models and advance dashboarding • Lead the agile development and conducting design thinking workshops with users on story mapping, creating user stories with operational insights that address operational challenges in a proactive manner • Managing and enhancing video hub to ensure the smooth onboarding of sensor projects • Keep abreast of technological advances in Video Surveillance, Video Analytics, Big Data Technologies, database designs & architecture and government policies & recommendations, etc • Manage and execute the procurement of the system/platform in a timely manner • Evaluate and recommend the solution that best address the needs • Manage the vendors to develop and deliver the solution • Identify, manage project risks and implications to the project and to recommend mitigating measures • Manage contractual and payment matters affecting the projects and ensure that systems are operating according to service level agreements • Understand the various prevailing policies and security guidelines and to ensure the system and processes are designed to comply with these policies and guidelines The jobholder will be expected to have supervisory duties as well, in managing a small team to deliver the above tasks. hrp|17349763|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-8b81-be3.responsibilities: Strategic AI Masterplanning • Drive the strategic AI masterplan across AI domains in HTX, aligning it with MHA strategic objectives and Home Team operational needs. • Act as the central planning hub for all AI initiatives, including the review of scope, timeline and budget before approval. • Conduct strategic foresighting and scenario planning to identify emerging technology opportunities across the AI domains. Programme Management • Lead AI programmes delivery, budgeting and resource allocation; produce regular dashboards and reports on AI adoption, performance and organisational AI maturity. • Coordinate with cross-functional teams to ensure timely delivery of AI projects and initiatives. • Provide technical expertise for the procurement of AI solutions, including reviewing specifications and evaluating vendor proposals. AI Governance & Risk Management • Develop and continuously update the AI Governance strategy and playbook covering key principles such as explainability, fairness, privacy, security, accountability, robustness and sustainability. • Establish metrics, monitoring processes and KPIs and provide regular updates of AI governance key performance metrics to senior leadership. Ecosystem Development & Collaboration • Design and execute an engagement strategy to build a vibrant AI ecosystem of industry, academia and government partners. • Identify, evaluate and recommend technology and vendor solutions that meet Home Team’s AI use-case requirements. • Organise outreach events, workshops and presentations; track ecosystem engagement KPIs and produce regular status reports. Stakeholder & Cross-Agency Coordination • Liaise with Home Team Departments, Programme Management Centres, Whole-of-Government (WoG) agencies and statutory boards to align AI requirements, ensure interoperability and facilitate data sharing. • Collaborate across cross-functional teams (Solutioning, Certifications, R&D, Product Development, Platforms, Data Engineering, Infrastructure) to gather and consolidate AI inputs for AI masterplanning. Leadership & People Management • Supervise a team of AI specialists and foster a culture of innovation, collaboration and continuous learning. • Conduct presentations to senior management on AI masterplan roll-out , governance updates, programmes progress and ecosystem collaboration outcomes.
hrp|17349763|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-8b81-be3.requirements: • Post-graduate / tertiary qualification in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, AIor related quantitative/analytical fields. • Minimum 15 years of technology development in AI-related domains, with at least 8 years in senior roles that include strategic planning, ecosystem collaboration, programme management and governance; at least 3 years delivering large-scale, multi-site AI projects. • Strong understanding of AI domains not limited to Vision AI, Embodied AI, Language AI, LLM & LMM, AI Safety & Security, and Emerging AI; experience with AI/ML, data science and analytics, and knowledge of AI Governance policies and frameworks. • Demonstrated track record of driving strategic planning cycle, formulating strategic masterplans, and driving their successful implementation with clear, quantifiable impact. • Demonstrated track record of building strategic partnerships, evaluating vendor solutions, negotiating contracts and leading collaborative AI initiatives with industry, academia and government partners. • Experience in procurement, budgeting, financial tracking and resource allocation for AI programmes. • Excellent verbal and written communication; ability to provide briefings and influence senior stakeholders across HTX and Home Team departments; strong facilitation and interpersonal skills. • Understanding of Home Team departmental business and technical requirements; familiarity with homeland-security contexts. • Good strategic foresight & innovation. • Excellent cross-agency collaboration & communication. • Comfortable to travel occasionally. All new hires are appointed on a two-year contract in the first instance and will be assessed and considered for permanent tenure over time, based on performance. hrp|17349763|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-8b81-be3.description: The Deputy Director will provide strategic leadership across AI masterplanning, AI governance, and AI collaboration and programme management. For masterplanning, the Deputy Director will develop a strategic masterplan for all applied AI domains (Vision AI, Embodied AI, Language AI, large language and large multimodal models, AI safety & security, and emerging technologies). For AI governance, the Deputy Director will establish robust frameworks that embeds responsible AI practices throughout HTX’s initiatives. For AI collaboration and programme management, the role will foster strategic AI collaboration with industry, academia and other government agencies, and programme manage end to end, cross functional AI projects. Together, these efforts will deliver AI solutions that support our public safety mission, improve citizen experience, and increase operational productivity.

hrp|17355495|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-8b99-d14.responsibilities: The Lead Associate/Senior Associate/Associate (Digital Transformation) will be part of the business ops team to conceptualise, plan and execute the implementation of the new GeBIZ system. hrp|17355495|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-8b99-d14.description: The Government Procurement Function Office (GPFO) oversees the Government procurement policies, practices, systems and workforce. Among other responsibilities, it is responsible for driving transformation of the whole-of-government (WOG) procurement function, including digital transformation. MOF-GPFO is embarking on a project to refresh the current GeBIZ. GeBIZ is a WOG platform for agencies to publish their tenders and suppliers to submit their proposals.

hrp|17365052|005056a3-d347-1fe1-8bc4-641.responsibilities: The jobholder is responsible for the Governance, Risk, audit and process management of enterprise ICT infrastructure services systems (such as end-user devices, virtualised infrastructure, active directory, network, serve, etc.) that are across all MHA Home Team Departments (HTDs). Relevant certification from Microsoft and other professional bodies would be an added advantage. All new appointees will be appointed on a two-year contract in the first instance. We wish to inform that only shortlisted candidates will be notified within 4 weeks upon closing of the advertisement. As part of the shortlisting process for this role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment. #L1-FL1

Support Director to develop and formulate the overall Community & School Outreach Master Plan aligned with “One Team Singapore” and national priorities. b. Identify, develop and maintain partnerships with government agencies, schools, IHLs, corporates, grassroots and ASEAN community groups. c. hrp|17387420|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-8ccc-59e.responsibilities: 1. Sponsorship Strategy & Planning a. Support the team in developing the sponsorship framework, tiering structure, rights matrix and value proposition for cash and VIK packages. b. Consolidate sponsorship requirements from Functional Areas (FAs) into working inventories (branding assets, operational needs, VIK opportunities). c. Collaborate with Marketing and Branding FAs to ensure alignment between sponsorship packages and brand guidelines, including category exclusivity and brand protection. 2. Serve as day-to-day account lead for assigned sponsors, coordinating communications, planning meetings and managing timelines. b. Coordinate sponsor approvals for creative materials, branding and activation concepts in line with brand guidelines. 4. Corporate Hospitality Strategy & Delivery a. Support Deputy Director and provide regular reports on project status, budget allocation, expenditure and ROI.

hrp|17393713|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-8ce4-ca8.responsibilities: Responsibilities As SAD, Procurement (Central Procurement Office), you will report directly to Chief Financial Officer and be part of a dynamic team in managing AGC's procurement functions to ensure prudent spend and compliance with the Government's Instruction Manuals (IM). Your scope of work will include a range of procurement activities covering the following: • Review of AGC’s procurement to ensure compliance with the Government Instructions Manual (IM) on Procurement and internal procurement guidelines. • Review and incorporate changes to IM and other Whole-of-Government processes into AGC’s procurement processes. hrp|17416264|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-8de0-fd3.responsibilities: The scope of work includes the following: • Technology Scouting: Conduct comprehensive literature reviews, patent searches, and technology surveys to identify emerging detector technologies and commercial products capable of detecting and mitigating CBRNE threats. • Quick Proof-of-concept Trials: Conduct tests on prototypes and products to identify superior technologies or products that can bring about operational enhancements. • Technology Development & Project Management: Lead and manage multiple concurrent research and development projects, managing timelines, resources, and deliverables whilst ensuring alignment with strategic objectives and stakeholder requirements • Procurement & Budget Management: Work as a team in securing project funding, managing procurement processes, and implementing technology acquisition strategies for CBRNE detection capabilities
hrp|17416264|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-8de0-fd3.requirements: • PhD / Masters / Bachelor's Degree in Science or Engineering with demonstrated strength in Applied Physics, Physical Sciences, or related disciplines • Knowledge of sensing technologies, signal processing, and materials science and their applications for enhancing border and aviation security through more effective and efficient people, conveyance and cargo screening processes. • Strong written communication skills and proficiency with modern productivity tools • Experience working within multidisciplinary teams of scientists and engineers • Willingness to participate in field studies and trials involving CBRNE threat detection (including simulant testing) • Independent, resourceful team player with excellent communication and critical thinking abilities • Experience managing collaborative projects with industry partners • Experience in coding and the use of artificial intelligence/machine learning to enhance relevant work processes is an edge. Competencies expected: • Scientific Rigour: Ability to design robust experiments and trials, validate solutions against experimental data, and critically evaluate scientific literature. • Project Leadership: Excellent coordination skills with proven ability to manage concurrent research programmes and stakeholder relationships • Analytical Excellence: Strong problem-solving abilities with meticulous attention to technical detail and systematic approach to complex challenges • Technical Communication: Skill in translating complex technical concepts into actionable insights for both specialist and non-specialist audiences • Collaborative Leadership: Ability to work effectively with multidisciplinary teams including chemists, engineers, and operational personnel whilst driving project outcomes * All new hires are appointed on a two-year contract in the first instance and will be assessed and considered for permanent tenure over time, based on performance. hrp|17416264|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-8de0-fd3.description: HTX is the first Science and Technology Agency of its kind in the world, bringing together science and engineering capabilities across the Home Team Departments to transform Singapore's homeland security landscape. We are a statutory board under the Ministry of Home Affairs, dedicated to developing cutting-edge technologies that empower our Home Team to solve crimes, save lives, secure borders, and safeguard public spaces. As an Engineer / Lead Engineer (Sensing Applications) within the Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear and Explosives (CBRNE) Centre of Excellence, you will drive physics-based novel multimodal threat sensing technologies whilst managing stakeholder relationships and research collaborations. Your work will involve applying physics-based sensing principles to create innovative sensing approaches for detecting, identifying, and quantifying CBRNE threats. The role demands deep physics expertise and practical engineering capabilities to translate theoretical concepts into deployable solutions, strong project management skills to coordinate diverse stakeholders, and the ability to evaluate commercial sensing technologies for operational deployment. You will drive the development of new sensing capabilities that surpass current state-of-the-art systems for Singapore's homeland security applications.

hrp|17438709|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a4a1-6d9.responsibilities: Design the system architecture and formulate the technical specifications for the IDTS systems Coordinate with users to gather the operational requirements and ensure that the systems are implemented in accordance with these requirements Conduct market surveys of potential systems available in the market Seek approval from the relevant authorities to adopt the proposed system design and technical specifications Identify and mitigating risks which may impact the successful delivery of the systems Perform procurement of the systems, including its evaluation of the proposed solutions Manage IDTS systems including cyber-security implementations, as well as the design and engineering information security (e.g. authentication, perimeter security, security compliance tools), technology systems (software & hardware), and security policies/ procedures. Implement and deploy the systems with the vendors (including testing and commissioning activities). Work closely with multiple stakeholders both internal and external (including other government agencies, system suppliers, maintenance operators, operation users, IT consultants/ auditors etc.) which include coordinate, liaise, support, and conduct meetings to facilitate and validate the implementation in accordance with national and international cybersecurity standards and requirements. Coordinate, liaise, support, and conduct internal as well as external audit needs/issues including technical discussions and internal audits (e.g., scanning exercises, penetration tests). Conduct investigations into security breaches to determine the cause of the incidents and work closely with multiple stakeholders both internal and external to resolve the incidents, participate in post-incident reporting and study/implement the proposed enhancement to the systems and infrastructure to close the security gaps. Manage the maintenance team to maintain the IDTS systems in accordance the required service level
hrp|17438709|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a4a1-6d9.requirements: Training in Engineering (Computing/ Electrical/ Electronics/ Telecommunication), Information Systems Management, Information Technology, Computer Science, or equivalent Experience in implementing large-scale ICT system-of-system for the entire life cycle is preferred Knowledge of system architecture design, system administration, networking and cybersecurity preferred Candidate with relevant experiences in air traffic control related systems may be considered for higher appointment Good team player who is able to work independently and with officers of all levels Good communication, written, interpersonal, analytical, presentation and negotiation skills with positive attitude and a keen sense of details Organised and good self-disciplined to meet tight timeline Able to work outside working hours and travel overseas occasionally Your appointment designation will commensurate with your relevant work experience. Successful candidates will be offered a 3-year contract in the first instance, and may be considered for placement on a permanent tenure or subsequent contract renewal.
hrp|17438709|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a4a1-6d9.description: CAAS Next Generation Programme Office Division is looking for a strong, driven and dynamic esteemed engineer candidate to be part of the Integrated Digital Tower System (IDTS) Section. You will be part of the team overseeing the entire life cycle management of the software intensive and complex Air Navigation Services (ANS) systems related to the Air Traffic Management (ATM) tower, from its implementation in accordance with the international standards (such as ICAO and Eurocae) to its maintenance. You will play a key role in defining the architecture of the systems, formulating the technical specifications, implementing the systems and operating and maintaining the systems, thereby contributing directly to the safety and efficient management of air traffic operations within Singapore Flight Information Region (FIR). You will be exposed to a wide spectrum of areas from project management, cybersecurity to comply with CAAS and Government IM8 requirements, safety management to system management. You will work closely with various stakeholders (both internal and external), including other government agencies, consultants, operational users, maintenance teams, renowned equipment and solution providers to deliver and maintain the systems.

hrp|17438712|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9cff-257.responsibilities: Design, develop and implement IT applications, technology services and integration of application systems across different technology platforms. Conceptualize, innovate and perform feasibility study of new or improved products and services based on user requirements. Manage Proof-of-Concept and/or pilot projects involving new technologies. Work closely with users on leveraging IT to effectively support their business needs and services as well as to improve current work operations and innovation of new services, while concurrently ensuring compliance to prevailing policies and guidelines. Prepare proposal and storyboarding of IT solutions to get buy-in from users and management. Responsible for end-to-end procurement of IT services, ensuring objectivity, transparency and best value for NLB and its patrons. Manage the vendors and contracts to ensure that the performance of vendors and deliverables are in accordance with the tender and service level agreements.
hrp|17438712|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9cff-257.requirements: Degree in IT, Computer Science or Mechanical Engineering with minimum of 3 to 8 years of relevant working experience in related IT roles e.g. managing IT related products/projects, prototyping, vendor management. Those with project management certification or equivalent, familiar with government procurement process and IM8 guidelines would have an added advantage. Experience in hybrid Agile environments and leveraging mechanical automation to improve delivery outcomes. Experience in delivering and managing projects involving automated or operational systems, including hardware-software integration, process optimization, and third-party vendor management. Knowledge of new technologies including AI-enabled tools, data-driven decision-making, and cloud-based collaboration platforms is a plus. Good working knowledge of Quality Management Systems, ISO 9000 standards is a plus. Strong interpersonal and communications skills to manage relevant stakeholders. The office location is at ESR BizPark@Chai Chee. Successful candidate will be appointed on a 2-year contract.
hrp|17438712|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9cff-257.description: The National Library Board (NLB) nurtures Readers for Life, Learning Communities and a Knowledgeable Nation by promoting reading, learning and history through our network of 28 libraries across Singapore, the National Library and the National Archives of Singapore. At NLB, you can look forward to a flexible, hybrid work environment with rewarding, impactful deliverables that improve the lives of the community. With caring colleagues, you will be in an ideal environment for professional development, innovation and impact. We can offer you: • A chance to Impact the Community, bridge gaps and empower everyone with the opportunity for learning and discovery. • An opportunity to Innovate and Push Boundaries. We value ideas, curiosity and a passion for innovation to transform our libraries and archives. • An organisation that Cares for your Growth and Wellbeing through investment in staff development and wellbeing in a supportive and collaborative environment.

hrp|17443619|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-8ed3-655.responsibilities: You will be responsible for the following: Oversee the daily operations of the facility and installations, including building systems and services, landscaping, pest control, and conservancy. Ensure the proper functioning of all Mechanical and Electrical (M&E) systems, including plumbing, Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning (HVAC), lighting, and fire protection systems Supervise a team of facilities, landscaping, pest control, conservancy and other outsourced contractors to ensure works are carried out satisfactorily in accordance with contract requirements Plan and coordinate preventive and corrective maintenance works in accordance with contract requirements. Monitor maintenance schedules and ensure timely completion of all works. Plan and carry out procurement of office equipment, supplies, stationery, and other operational items. Perform administrative duties, including processing invoices for payment, managing copier rental contracts, tracking paper usage, and coordinating the provision of uniforms. Handle and manage feedback, including investigation and follow-up actions. Ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and maintain safety standards within the facility. Respond to and investigate any building-related incidents and coordinate with relevant authorities and internal stakeholders, even after office hours. Participate in major events such as Qing Ming Festival, scheduled fire emergency exercises, annual shutdown servicing and any other organisational level events, including on weekends and public holidays. Perform any other duties as assigned by the supervisor.

hrp|17443619|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-8ed3-655.description: We are looking for a service-oriented individual to join the Memorial Services and Operations Division which oversees the operation and maintenance of Government cemeteries, crematoria and columbaria. Creative Concept Development Develop innovative concepts and programming for public, corporate, and island-wide events that enhance visitor experiences and promote the Sentosa brand. Government Procurement & Tender Management Oversee full procurement lifecycle—including tender preparation, qualification, evaluation, and award—in compliance with government and statutory requirements. Permits & Regulatory Compliance Coordinate licensing, permits, insurance, and agreements with authorities for seamless event delivery. Reporting & Performance Measurement Track KPIs such as attendance, satisfaction, financial performance, and ROI; produce post-event analysis with recommendations for improvement.

hrp|17461791|005056a3-d347-1fe1-8f9e-cce.responsibilities: Supply Operations (Post-Deal) Collaborate with the Director of Procurement to manage counterparties and ensure timely delivery of SAF cargos. Oversee operational execution of supply agreements, including scheduling, logistics, and compliance. Monitor and resolve delivery issues, ensuring counterparties meet contractual obligations. Coordinate with finance teams to ensure accurate and timely payment flows linked to supply contracts. Sales Operations (Post-Sales) Partner with the Director of Business Development to manage execution of sales agreements. Work with airlines, corporate buyers, and other stakeholders on Environmental Attribute (EA) post-sales operations. Ensure smooth customer onboarding, order fulfilment, and reporting of SAF usage and EA allocations. Provide operational insights to support customer satisfaction and repeat business. Cross-Functional Support & Capability Building Act as the operational bridge between supply and sales functions, ensuring alignment across teams. Work closely with sustainability, finance, and legal teams within SAFCo and CAAS to ensure procurement strategies are operationally executable and aligned with SAFCo’s mission. Participate in monthly and quarterly supplier meetings to review fuel pricing, delivery performance, and reconciliation issues. Support risk management, compliance, and business continuity planning. Contribute to process improvements and system development to enhance SAFCo’s operational agility. Engage with external stakeholders to strengthen SAFCo’s credibility and transparency in the SAF ecosystem. Tender Operations & Management Support the setup and implementation of procurement systems (e.g. SAP, Oracle or esourcing tools), ensuring system integrity, user access control, and audit readiness. Support the execution the end-to-end tender lifecycle for SAF procurement, including RFI/RFP/RFQ processes, bid evaluations, contract finalization and post-award management. Provide support on maintenance of procurement dashboards and reporting tools to track KPIs such as supplier performance, contract milestones, fuel volumes and pricing benchmarks Ensure accurate input and reconciliation of fuel prices in procurement systems, including monthly invoicing, rolling buffers, and despite resolution with vendors.
hrp|17461791|005056a3-d347-1fe1-8f9e-cce.requirements: 8–12 years in supply chain, operations, or sales operations, ideally within energy, aviation, or related industries. Proven experience managing counterparties and executing complex post-deal/post-sales operations. Strong stakeholder management and negotiation skills. Excellent organizational and problem-solving abilities. Familiarity with regulated industries and contractual execution frameworks. Self-starter with a strong sense of ownership and accountability. Comfortable multi-hatting in a lean, fast-paced start-up environment. Growth-oriented, eager to expand beyond traditional operations into strategic responsibilities. Why Join SAFCo? Be part of a pioneering team shaping Singapore’s sustainable aviation future. Grow your career in a dynamic, purpose-driven startup. Work closely with leadership and contribute to high-impact initiatives.
hrp|17461791|005056a3-d347-1fe1-8f9e-cce.description: The Singapore Sustainable Aviation Fuel Company (SAFCo) is a mission-driven entity supporting Singapore’s national SAF (Sustainable Aviation Fuel) policy. SAFCo manages SAF levy collection, procures SAF to meet regulated demand, and develops the voluntary SAF market. As a lean and agile startup, SAFCo is building foundational capabilities to ensure operational excellence, transparency, and credibility in the SAF ecosystem. Role overview The Senior Supply & Sales Operations Manager will work closely with the Director of Business Development on post-sales operations and the Director of Procurement on post-deal operations. This role ensures seamless execution after contracts are signed — from coordinating counterparties for timely cargo delivery and payment, to managing customer and partner interactions on post-sales execution. It is ideal for an experienced operator who thrives in a dynamic start-up environment and can bridge supply reliability with commercial success.

hrp|17461798|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9fac-beb.responsibilities: As a member of Integrated Outreach team overseeing Workplace Outreach, you will: Support the development of HPB’s new strategy to engage and partner companies to support worker health; Oversee the procurement of Project Manager services to implement HPB’s new strategy at scale; Support the planning and development of operational workflows for HPB to work with appointed Project Managers; Work with HPB’s corporate marketing team to oversee the design and publication of marketing materials for the implementation of HPB’s new strategy.

hrp|17479409|005056a3-d347-1fe1-8fdf-cc5.responsibilities: ICT Operations and Support • Manage day-to-day ICT operations for assigned departments and zones. • Provide comprehensive IT support services including hardware troubleshooting, software installations, and technical guidance to end users. • Oversee provision and management of basic ICT equipment including EUSS, notebooks, peripherals, and mobile devices. • Coordinate and execute tech refresh exercises, including planning, implementation, and post-deployment support. • Monitor and maintain ICT equipment performance, conducting preventive maintenance and addressing technical issues promptly. • Support remote access solutions and ensure secure connectivity. • Oversee ad hoc software licensing and portable storage media management in accordance with security policies. Cybersecurity and Risk Management • Personally oversee phishing email exercises, cybersecurity related areas and awareness programmes, and staff training completion. • Lead comprehensive ICT incident response, investigation, and management across the Group. • Manage IM8 and MND Third-Party Risk Management programmes, ensuring compliance and risk mitigation. Asset and Service Management • Oversee provision and management of basic ICT equipment including EUSS, notebooks, peripherals, and mobile devices. • Manage specialised ICT services such as telephony systems, managed print services, and wireless network infrastructure. • Coordinate SG-mails and SGEPP management, ensuring proper access controls and user support. • Handle procurement processes for ICT assets, including vendor coordination, approval workflows, and delivery management. • Maintain accurate asset registers and conduct regular audits to ensure compliance and optimal resource utilisation. Security and Compliance • Support Category 2 Security Clearance processes, ensuring proper documentation and compliance. • Ensure compliance with WOG/HDB security policies. ICT Coordination and Engagement • Coordinate onboarding and offboarding processes for staff, ensuring proper ICT access provisioning and asset recovery. • Serve as secretary/coordinator for engagement with Department/ Zone Administrative Managers. • Heighten awareness of new work productivity tools and technologies, promoting adoption of innovative solutions to improve operational effectiveness. • Champion adoption of new ICT work tools through awareness campaigns, training sessions, and user support. • Coordinate ICT-related meetings and stakeholder engagements, including agenda preparation and follow-up actions. Additional Portfolio - Department Administrative Manager • Manage the Administrative team, providing guidance and support for administrative operations. • Supervise end-to-end procurement and asset management processes. • Manage department budgets and resources efficiently, including financial planning and expenditure monitoring. • Coordinate with various stakeholders on department renovation works and facility management. • Coordinate HR-related matters including staff welfare, leave management, and personnel administration. • Champion department procurement matters, ensuring compliance with procurement policies and procedures. • Cascade administrative communications and policies to department staff. • Manage office administration including coordination of department events, meetings, and official functions. • Maintain department records and documentation systems. • Liaise with corporate services on administrative matters affecting the department.
hrp|17479409|005056a3-d347-1fe1-8fdf-cc5.requirements: • Background in in Information Technology, Computer Science, or related technical field. • Minimum 3-5 years of experience in ICT operations, or related roles. • Experience with cybersecurity principles and IT governance frameworks preferred. • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills with ability to work effectively with diverse stakeholders. • Strong organisational and project coordination abilities. • Experience in government, public sector, or large organisation ICT environments advantageous. • Administrative management experience preferred for the additional portfolio responsibilities. Successful candidates will be offered 1-yr contract at the first instance. Find out more about a career with HDB at www.hdb.gov.sg/cs/infoweb/about-us/careers All applicants will be notified on whether they are shortlisted for the position within 4 weeks of the closing date of this job posting.

hrp|17497107|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-90ce-d2a.responsibilities: Key responsibilities include: Lead and manage the ATM support systems related projects, which include replacement of existing systems, perform enhancement works and tech refresh upgrades. Ensure the projects are delivered on time, within scope, and meet defined operational requirements. Design the system architecture and develop the technical specifications for the ATM support systems, which are being deployed both on-site and on cloud platforms. Work with users and stakeholders to formulate the operational, technical, and cybersecurity requirements. Ensure that the replacement systems, enhancements, and upgrades are implemented in accordance with these requirements. Seek approval from the relevant authorities to adopt the proposed system design and technical specifications Formulate the budget required for the projects and devise the system implementation plans. This includes Identifying and mitigating risks which may impact the successful delivery of the systems Perform procurement activities for the enhancement works and technology refresh upgrades, including evaluating proposed solutions. Implement and deploy the ATM support systems with the vendors (including testing and commissioning activities). Support the operation and maintenance activities of the ATM support systems, such as preventive and corrective maintenance. You are also required to ensure that the ATM support systems are implemented in accordance with the international standards (such as ICAO and Eurocae), as well as applicable governance regulations (such as cyber security requirements). These systems are software intensive, complex and requires high availability. You will need to work closely with multiple stakeholders (both internal and external), including other government agencies, system suppliers, maintenance operators, operation users, IT consultants etc. to ensure the system(s) meets the required standards and requirements. Stakeholder management is critical, and you are expected to coordinate and liaise with the respective stakeholders.

hrp|17497631|005056a3-d347-1fe1-90d4-b5e.responsibilities: We are looking for a pro-active and dynamic individual to be part of our Logistics Team. You will need to be a meticulous person with a sharp eye for numbers and always plan ahead to ensure sufficient supplies of all required inventories/logistics and continuity of all procured services to maintain buildings, infrastructures and operations. With a quick-thinking mind, you learn to identify, flag and resolve potential issues to ensure procurements are conducted in a fair, transparent and value-for-money manner. You shall be self-motivated and use initiative to improve and streamline work processes to improve work quality. You will ensure effective and efficient execution of various processes within Logistics section. You shall provide services for internal customers by providing prompt and accurate responses to requests and enquiries from officers and supervisors. You will assist in reviewing existing procedures and current state of procurement processes and contract management for improvement. You shall ensure the compliance of procedures, propose improvements to enhance efficiency and productivity, and implement preventive measures to minimise any procurement, contract management and supply risks.
hrp|17497631|005056a3-d347-1fe1-90d4-b5e.requirements: • Relevant Background • Possess strong analytical, effective interpersonal and communication skills • Meticulous and independent worker • Possess high drive and pleasant personality with strong teamwork belief • Able to adapt in high intense operations environment • Good time management and be able to meet tight deadlines • Good knowledge of Microsoft Office suite (e.g., Microsoft Excel, Work and PowerPoint). Knowledge of SAP would be an added advantage. Application: To be part of our team, please submit an online application via www.careers.gov.sg. Short-listed candidates will be notified within two weeks after the closing date for applications.
hrp|17497631|005056a3-d347-1fe1-90d4-b5e.description: Are you looking for a challenging career that allows you to be part of police operations in keeping Singapore safe and secure? Join us and be part of our team at the Singapore Police Force (SPF). SPF plays a critical role in keeping Singapore safe and secure with our mission to prevent, deter and detect crime. Special Operations Command (SOC) is the lead tactical arm of SPF to provide highest level of tactical option to combat crime, terrorism and public disorder. We seek to constantly explore, innovate and adapt cutting-edge technology to support our officers to enhance policing efforts for crime fighting. As a Logistics Officer in the SOC, you play a critical part in the supply chain operations, manage established contracts and handle procurement of goods and services using the Integrated Logistics Management System (iLMS) to support SOC’s mission and continuity of all operations. You will become part of the logistics fraternity where you get to learn and be au fait with the Government Instruction Manuals (IM) on procurement and finance and be equipped with knowledge to advise and guide officers on procurement procedures. You will work with various logistics departments in MHA and Police HQ.

hrp|17497877|005056a3-d347-1fe1-92db-72a.requirements: • Professionals with experience in one or more of the following areas - procurement, implementing organisational systems, digital transformation, project management. • Ability to look at issues from a WOG perspective, review the status quo and integrate procurement policy considerations and operational requirements with what is technologically feasible. • Have a dare-to-do attitude and not afraid to challenge the status quo. • Self-driven and committed individual able to work independently and within teams. • Strong critical thinking, analytical and project management skills. • Strong communication skills and ability to work collaboratively with internal and external stakeholders. • Excellent writing ability and presentation skills. • Entry-level positions available for candidates with demonstrated interest in procurement and/or digital transformation.
hrp|17497877|005056a3-d347-1fe1-92db-72a.description: The Government Procurement Function Office (GPFO) oversees the Government procurement policies, practices, systems and workforce. Among other responsibilities, it is responsible for driving transformation of the whole-of-government (WOG) procurement function, including digital transformation. MOF-GPFO is embarking on a project to refresh the current GeBIZ. GeBIZ is a WOG platform for agencies to publish their tenders and suppliers to submit their proposals.

hrp|17498012|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-90d5-88f.responsibilities: Strategic AI Masterplanning • Drive the strategic AI masterplan across AI domains in HTX, aligning it with MHA strategic objectives and Home Team operational needs. • Act as the central planning hub for all AI initiatives, including the review of scope, timeline and budget before approval. • Conduct strategic foresighting and scenario planning to identify emerging technology opportunities across the AI domains. Programme Management • Lead AI programmes delivery, budgeting and resource allocation; produce regular dashboards and reports on AI adoption, performance and organisational AI maturity. • Coordinate with cross-functional teams to ensure timely delivery of AI projects and initiatives. • Provide technical expertise for the procurement of AI solutions, including reviewing specifications and evaluating vendor proposals. AI Governance & Risk Management • Develop and continuously update the AI Governance strategy and playbook covering key principles such as explainability, fairness, privacy, security, accountability, robustness and sustainability. • Establish metrics, monitoring processes and KPIs and provide regular updates of AI governance key performance metrics to senior leadership. Ecosystem Development & Collaboration • Design and execute an engagement strategy to build a vibrant AI ecosystem of industry, academia and government partners. • Identify, evaluate and recommend technology and vendor solutions that meet Home Team’s AI use-case requirements. • Organise outreach events, workshops and presentations; track ecosystem engagement KPIs and produce regular status reports. Stakeholder & Cross-Agency Coordination • Liaise with Home Team Departments, Programme Management Centres, Whole-of-Government (WoG) agencies and statutory boards to align AI requirements, ensure interoperability and facilitate data sharing. • Collaborate across cross-functional teams (Solutioning, Certifications, R&D, Product Development, Platforms, Data Engineering, Infrastructure) to gather and consolidate AI inputs for AI masterplanning. Leadership & People Management • Supervise a team of AI specialists and foster a culture of innovation, collaboration and continuous learning. • Conduct presentations to senior management on AI masterplan roll-out , governance updates, programmes progress and ecosystem collaboration outcomes.
hrp|17498012|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-90d5-88f.requirements: • Post-graduate / tertiary qualification in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, AIor related quantitative/analytical fields. • Minimum 15 years of technology development in AI-related domains, with at least 8 years in senior roles that include strategic planning, ecosystem collaboration, programme management and governance; at least 3 years delivering large-scale, multi-site AI projects. • Strong understanding of AI domains not limited to Vision AI, Embodied AI, Language AI, LLM & LMM, AI Safety & Security, and Emerging AI; experience with AI/ML, data science and analytics, and knowledge of AI Governance policies and frameworks. • Demonstrated track record of driving strategic planning cycle, formulating strategic masterplans, and driving their successful implementation with clear, quantifiable impact. • Demonstrated track record of building strategic partnerships, evaluating vendor solutions, negotiating contracts and leading collaborative AI initiatives with industry, academia and government partners. • Experience in procurement, budgeting, financial tracking and resource allocation for AI programmes. • Excellent verbal and written communication; ability to provide briefings and influence senior stakeholders across HTX and Home Team departments; strong facilitation and interpersonal skills. • Understanding of Home Team departmental business and technical requirements; familiarity with homeland-security contexts. • Good strategic foresight & innovation. • Excellent cross-agency collaboration & communication. • Comfortable to travel occasionally. All new hires are appointed on a two-year contract in the first instance and will be assessed and considered for permanent tenure over time, based on performance. As part of the shortlisting process for this role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment. All applicants will be updated on the status of their applications within 4 weeks upon closing of the advertisement. #LI-CW1
hrp|17498012|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-90d5-88f.description: The Deputy Director will provide strategic leadership across AI masterplanning, AI governance, and AI collaboration and programme management. For masterplanning, the Deputy Director will develop a strategic masterplan for all applied AI domains (Vision AI, Embodied AI, Language AI, large language and large multimodal models, AI safety & security, and emerging technologies). For AI governance, the Deputy Director will establish robust frameworks that embeds responsible AI practices throughout HTX’s initiatives. For AI collaboration and programme management, the role will foster strategic AI collaboration with industry, academia and other government agencies, and programme manage end to end, cross functional AI projects. Together, these efforts will deliver AI solutions that support our public safety mission, improve citizen experience, and increase operational productivity.

hrp|17500164|005056a3-d347-1fe1-90db-942.responsibilities: We are seeking a proactive and passionate individual to lead the development and implementation of central policies that elevate leadership and workforce excellence across the Government Procurement function. This pivotal role will shape talent strategies, design leadership development programs, and drive workforce engagement initiatives in collaboration with both internal and external stakeholders to build a future-ready procurement workforce and strengthen capabilities across government. Key Responsibilities Leadership and Talent Development • Drive the implementation of leadership and talent development strategies for the Government Procurement function, including leadership rotations, succession planning, and talent engagement initiatives to build a strong leadership pipeline across agencies. • Serve as the secretariat for the Joint Finance and Procurement Talent Development Committee and act as the primary liaison with HR counterparts across agencies to coordinate and implement talent initiatives effectively. Career Development and Mobility • Partner with government agencies to design and facilitate cross-agency learning experiences such as Structured Job Rotations (SJR), GIG Projects, Short-Term Immersion Programmes (STIP), and Private Sector Attachment Programmes. • Leverage the One Talent Gateway (OTG) portal to promote transparency and accessibility of career opportunities within the Procurement community. Stakeholder Engagement and Strategic Partnerships • Maintain strong engagement with HR teams across agencies through regular consultations to align development initiatives with agency needs. • Collaborate with private sector and industry partners to co-create impactful attachment opportunities and assess their effectiveness and value. • Work closely with procurement leaders to design developmental initiatives that promote continuous learning and career growth within the procurement workforce. • Foster a vibrant and connected procurement community through networking events and community-building activities. • Provide data-driven insights and performance reporting to senior management to track the effectiveness and outcomes of workforce development efforts.
hrp|17500164|005056a3-d347-1fe1-90db-942.requirements: What We Look For: • Collaborative Spirit: Strong interpersonal skills to engage effectively with diverse stakeholders and foster productive partnerships. • Transformative Mindset: Passion for driving transformation in public service procurement • Communication: Excellent written and verbal communication skills. • Adaptability: Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment, manage multiple priorities, and embrace change. • Experience: 3-5 years of relevant experience in workforce planning, leadership and talent development, human resources, or a related field.

hrp|17500167|005056a3-d347-1fe1-90db-98f.description: The Government Procurement Function Office (GPFO) leads procurement transformation across the Singapore Public Service. We develop policies, drive technological innovation, foster Whole-of-Government resource optimisation, and build workforce capabilities to enable effective government procurement while maintaining strong governance. We are looking for a proactive and passionate candidate to manage the Procurement Professional Programme (P3) – GPFO’s flagship initiative to build a strong pipeline of procurement professionals for the Public Service. This role is pivotal in shaping procurement capabilities while supporting the career development of young talents. You will also spearhead outreach and recruitment initiatives to attract high-potential candidates to the programme.

hrp|17531147|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9286-c75.responsibilities: • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to develop and implement project plans, budgets and funding for new and Addition & Alteration (A&A) facilities • Oversee end-to-end delivery of projects from Invitation to Quotes (ITQs)/Tenders award to project close-out and defect management, ensuring timely, within-budget and quality outcomes. • Track project expenditures, identify trends and provide insights for cost optimization and future planning, ensuring effective resource allocation. • Foster strong relationships with project stakeholders, including architects, engineers, contracts and building occupants to ensure effective communication and issue resolution. • Assist in preparing project, expenditure and resource reports for Management and maintain accurate up-to-date project records, including drawings, specifications and other relevant documents. • Liaise with internal and external stakeholders to ensure seamless project execution, issues resolution and provide project updates.

hrp|17531147|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9286-c75.description: The Internal Security Department (ISD) confronts and addresses threats to Singapore’s internal security and stability. For over 75 years, ISD and its predecessor organisations have played a central role in countering threats such as those posed by foreign subversive elements, spies, racial and religious extremists, and terrorists. A fulfilling and rewarding career awaits those who want to join in ISD’s critical mission of keeping Singapore safe, secure and sovereign for all Singaporeans. The officer supports the implementation of building infrastructure projects by assisting in the coordination of design, procurement, and construction activities in line with approved scope, budget and timelines. The role monitors contractor and consultant performance, tracks risks and project controls, makes administrative submissions, prepares reports and documentation to support the development, commissioning and handover processes of a Building & Infrastructure (B&I) project so as to ensure the smooth conduct and transition to operations.

Fresh graduates will be considered. Job Requirements: Pleasant personality; mature, independent and resourceful; highly self-motivated; patient and resilient; adaptable to diverse work scopes Integrity and good interpersonal and presentation skills Analytical with good writing, communication and problem solving skills Ability to lead, interact and foster team work Proficient in Microsoft Office As part of the shortlisting process for this role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment.
hrp|17535777|005056a3-d347-1fe1-99ba-652.description: The Tuas South Incineration Plant (TSIP) is responsible for the incineration of waste and the heat generated from the incineration process is recovered to produce electricity. hrp|17535785|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9298-0fc.requirements: Degree in IT, Computer Science or equivalent. At least 4 - 8 years of relevant working experience in IT environment. hrp|17565129|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-97cb-b5a.description: The Municipal Services Office (MSO) was set up in 2014 to improve the coordination, delivery and quality of municipal services by the Government and Town Councils. These services include the upkeep and improvement of common areas in public and private housing estates, and the upgrading or provision of neighbourhood infrastructure. Having reaped these early, low-hanging fruits, MSO and our partner agencies are now on a multi-year effort to more fundamentally integrate and optimise decision-making and ground operations across the sector. We are transforming the way works are scheduled and manpower deployed on the ground, multi-skilling workers to perform several adjacent job functions and deploying operations-technology meaningfully. We piloted this new integrated operations service delivery model, which delivered promising outcomes. The MSO Integrated Operations (IO) team is now working with agencies and industry on the next phase, to scale the integrated operations to more towns, reaping even greater benefits for residents, industry and Government. We are looking for experienced Procurement officers to join the IO team, for this exciting journey to scale up the integrated operations.

hrp|17567269|005056a3-d347-1fe1-97df-672.responsibilities: [Procurement] Shape and drive the strategic direction of end-to-end procurement for IO related projects, from industry engagement and tender specification development through to evaluation and contract award. You will establish and uphold procurement standards in full compliance with the IM on Procurement and agency-level requirements, while forging substantive partnerships with industry players, vendors, and relevant agencies (e.g. JTC, HDB, NEA, NParks) to assess industry readiness and surface best practices across targeted sectors, with a focus on facilities management disciplines such as cleaning, landscaping, and infrastructure maintenance. You will also strategise and lead negotiations to secure favourable terms, pricing, and service levels for the Government, while preserving sufficient commercial headroom for suppliers to invest in and grow their capabilities. [Contract Management] Define and champion a robust contract governance framework across the full contract management lifecycle alongside the operations team, covering all key milestones such as variations and renewals through to payments, security deposits, and insurance. You will lead the team to work with MSO operations team for the accounting of contractor performance against agreed indicators, present performance reports to Senior Management and steering dispute resolution as required. This includes driving regular contract reviews and risk assessments to surface improvement opportunities, review contractors’ audited reports where applicable , and ensuring all submissions are properly documented and processed. [Finance] Work with Finance Business Partner Team to provide guidance to the team on IO financial resourcing and end-to-end functions from procurement to payment. This includes driving the coordination of resourcing proposals (e.g. Reinvestment Fund), work collaboratively with other Ministries and agencies on budget cutover and top-ups, ensure good budget marksmanship, and governance etc. You will also take charge of the designing and delivering of Programme Evaluation (PE) for IO projects, including developing theories of change and evaluation plans, and partnering with line departments on data collection and reporting.
