hrp|17567269|005056a3-d347-1fe1-97df-672.description: The Municipal Services Office (MSO) was set up in 2014 to improve the coordination, delivery and quality of municipal services by the Government and Town Councils. These services include the upkeep and improvement of common areas in public and private housing estates, and the upgrading or provision of neighbourhood infrastructure. Having reaped these early, low-hanging fruits, MSO and our partner agencies are now on a multi-year effort to more fundamentally integrate and optimise decision-making and ground operations across the sector. We are transforming the way works are scheduled and manpower deployed on the ground, multi-skilling workers to perform several adjacent job functions and deploying operations-technology meaningfully. We piloted this new integrated operations service delivery model, which delivered promising outcomes. The MSO Integrated Operations (IO) team is now working with agencies and industry on the next phase, to scale the integrated operations to more towns, reaping even greater benefits for residents, industry and Government. We are looking for experienced Procurement officers to join the IO team, in this exciting journey to scale up the integrated operations.

hrp|17575674|005056a3-d347-1fe1-93fa-4f2.description: About EDB The Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB), a government agency under the Ministry of Trade and Industry, is responsible for strategies that enhance Singapore’s position as a global centre for business, innovation, and talent. We undertake investment promotion and industry development, and work with international businesses, both foreign and local, by providing information, connection to partners and access to government incentives for their investments. Our mission is to create sustainable economic growth, with vibrant business and good job opportunities for Singapore. For more information on EDB, please visit www.edb.gov.sg About FRAP As part of EDB’s continuous efforts to develop the suite of industries in Singapore, the Finance, Risk & Assurance and Procurement (FRAP) division is an imperative business partner to our officers in the industry and policy groups. As a FRAP business partner, you will be responsible for providing advisory on the procure to pay value chain. You will also be part of a team that is responsible for the data management and implementation of FRAP systems, which is critical in ensuring that EDB has access to accurate and relevant data at all times from a single point of access to help drive operational decision-making, policy-making and strategic planning by Corporate Management and line divisions within EDB. As this role requires extensive cross-functional partnership with various stakeholders, you will also get to learn about EDB’s business from the line divisions directly and gain better understanding on policy considerations. This is an excellent opportunity for a Finance and/or Procurement professional looking to build their competencies and work alongside a fun and passionate team that greatly emphasizes on teamwork, open communication and diversity of perspectives.

hrp|17575978|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-93ff-76e.responsibilities: Corporate Finance & Treasury • Lead funding and treasury strategies and operations to ensure sufficient liquidity and cost effective financing to support operating and development needs. • Advise senior management on capital structure, and financing strategies and options, considering market conditions and financial risks. • Oversee cashflow forecasting and planning, foreign currency exposure and the investment of surplus funds within approved parameters. Financial Risk Management and Stewardship • Oversee insurance arrangements for property and public liability risks, working with internal stakeholders and insurance brokers to ensure adequate and cost effective coverage. • Review and strengthen governance, controls, policies, procedures and risk management practices across corporate finance and treasury activities. • Ensure that the financial control framework in the Financial Manual remains relevant and up-to-date. Revenue Collection & Contract Management • Lead cross-department collaboration for contractual management of outsourced billing and collection arrangement for major revenue streams, including procurement of the billing and collection services provider. • Ensure accuracy of billing, timely remittance of collections and effective management of arrears, including escalation of material issues for senior management or Board approval where required. • Ensure revenue accounting practices comply with relevant Statutory Board Financial Reporting Standards (SB-FRS) and Government policies and guidelines. People Leadership & Digital Business Transformation • Lead, mentor and develop the corporate finance & treasury team to build strong professional capability and foster a culture of integrity, teamwork, continuous learning and innovation. • Provide leadership and guidance to build officers’ digital capabilities and in the development and adoption of digital and AI solutions to streamline, automate and transform operations, and produce management insights.
hrp|17575978|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-93ff-76e.requirements: • Degree in Finance, Accountancy, Economics, Business or a related discipline. • Professional qualifications (e.g. CA, CFA) are an advantage. • Proven track record and senior level experience in corporate finance and/or treasury, with exposure to debt capital markets, green financing, treasury operations, investments, contract management, financial controls and financial risk management. Key Attributes • Strong analytical judgement and ability to balance detail with broader organisational considerations. • High standards of integrity and professionalism, especially in dealings with banks, advisors and service providers. • Clear communicator, able to explain complex financial issues to senior stakeholders and translate financial and market information into clear, practical recommendations to support decision making. • Proven people leadership experience, with a track record in developing finance professionals and strong ability to assess competency gaps, uplift skills, and guide officers towards higher proficiency.
hrp|17575978|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-93ff-76e.description: You will lead the Corporate Finance & Treasury function to ensure strong financial stewardship and sustainability for PUB. This includes managing financing and liquidity, investing surplus funds prudently, overseeing revenue collection arrangements and mitigating financial risks. This is a finance leadership role requiring strong technical expertise, effective people and partner management skills, and a keen interest in digitalisation and business process transformation. You will oversee a team of six and report to the Chief Financial Officer. You will work closely with senior management and external partners to support sound financial decision making in a complex and evolving operating environment.

hrp|17576545|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9487-3e5.responsibilities: The temporary staff member will work closely with the Team and key stakeholders to implement, monitor, and evaluate sport programmes and initiatives designed to enhance the lives of underprivileged and at-risk children and youth in our community, in line with SportCares/SportSG vision and mission to change lives through sport. Job Responsibilities: • Support the implementation, recruitment, monitoring, and evaluation of sport programmes such as Saturday Night Lights (SNL) and SportCares HEARTS Football League, and initiatives designed to impact underprivileged and at-risk youth, including facilitating their participation in development programmes, volunteering activities, and competitions. • Assist in coach recruitment and assessment, programme quality assurance, and develop indicators and reporting measures to demonstrate programme effectiveness and outcomes. • Oversee the comprehensive design, execution, monitoring, and evaluation of programme categories while collaborating with internal and external stakeholders to ensure seamless operations and strong partnership relationships. • Manage procurement activities within approved budgets and timelines, including supplier evaluation, vendor relationship management, and ensuring compliance with government procurement guidelines. • Assist in managing the Community Futsal Programme (CFP) database, facilitating participant opportunities in development programmes and competitions, and collaborating with coaches to coordinate and execute events, workshops, and competitions.
hrp|17576545|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9487-3e5.requirements: We are looking for self-motivated individuals who value integrity, teamwork and take pride in going the extra mile to provide excellent service to stakeholders and the community. This individual should be a sport advocate through living an active lifestyle and staying active. In addition, an ideal candidate should possess the following: • Some experience in organising and implementing programmes or outreach initiatives for vulnerable children, youth, and families (not necessarily sports-related). • Some experience in programme design, monitoring, and evaluation. • Familiarity with Singapore's sporting ecosystem and social service landscape. • Prior experience managing a variety of programmes and working within the social service sector would be an advantage. • A genuine interest in youth development, sports, or the social service sector is a plus. • Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to engage stakeholders across diverse backgrounds. • Organised, self-motivated, and able to work independently as well as collaboratively in a team. • Empathetic, with a passion for sports and a commitment to making a positive impact.
hrp|17576545|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9487-3e5.description: At Sport Singapore, we aspire to transform the nation through an active lifestyle designed around innovative, fun, and meaningful sporting experiences. Sport has the unique ability to bring people together through play, regardless of age, gender, race, ability, or social status. It imparts life values, nurtures character and builds resilience. It inspires and evokes the Singapore spirit through shared experiences and strengthens our national identity. We help Singaporeans Live Better Through Sport. Sport Singapore is constantly on the lookout for individuals who are passionate about what they do. Anchored in our values of Passion for Sport, Strength through Teamwork and Care for People, we believe in working and playing, not just as a team, but as a family. The level of offer will commensurate with applicants’ experience and track records. Successful candidates will be offered a 12-months Full-time contract. Only shortlisted applicants will be notified.

hrp|17576545|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-94e5-ba2.description: At Sport Singapore, we aspire to transform the nation through an active lifestyle designed around innovative, fun, and meaningful sporting experiences. Only shortlisted applicants will be notified.

hrp|17579898|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9493-70a.description: The Environmental Monitoring & Modelling Division (EMMD) puts in place and manage a comprehensive air and water quality monitoring programme to ensure effective monitoring of the air and water quality and enable policies to be formulated to improve air and water quality. You will be leading the Modelling & Instrumentation Department (MID) in EMMD. MID consists of two branches – 1) Environmental Monitoring instrumentation Branch and 2) Modelling and Research Branch. The Environmental Monitoring Instrumentation Branch is responsible for ensuring that the various air and water quality monitoring systems operates smoothly to continuously provide accurate and timely air and water quality data, as well as ensure maintenance, upgrades and IT security compliance of the systems. The Branch is also responsible for development projects such the expansion of existing monitoring networks, setting up of new specialised monitoring systems, and conducting test-bedding and field trials of emerging environmental monitoring technologies. The Modelling and Research team is responsible for carrying out air dispersion and water quality modelling studies to assess and quantify the impact of policies and developmental projects on air and water quality. The team also drives air and water quality research projects, data analysis and studies to better understand air and water quality issues in Singapore.

hrp|17585230|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-94c1-e80.responsibilities: The jobholder is responsible for the Governance, Risk, audit and process management of enterprise ICT infrastructure services systems (such as end-user devices, virtualised infrastructure, active directory, network, serve, etc.) that are across all MHA Home Team Departments (HTDs). hrp|17590662|005056a3-d347-1fe1-94de-e37.responsibilities: Develops strategic procurement plan in partnership with stakeholders to meet NLB’s strategic objectives, including establishing demand aggregation opportunities; provides advice to divisions in procurement decisions especially for complex purchases; manage stakeholders and resolve identified issues with the stakeholders in a timely manner. Provides guidance to procurement account managers to support divisions on their purchase requirements and propose appropriate sourcing strategies that best meet the divisions’ business needs; undertakes the role of business partners in supporting the divisions’ procurement needs where required. Develops and build capability of the project managers and the procurement account managers to equip them with the required competencies; review and refresh the procurement competency framework for project managers and approving officers. Directs the efforts of Incident Reporting relating to procurement, including the reporting framework/SOP, review and analysis of reports for submissions to Senior Management and Sub-Board. Streamlines processes/SOPs and assists in the deployment of technology to improve the efficiencies of work processes; prepares policy papers/reports and makes presentations during Senior Management and Main Board/Sub-Board meetings. Provides guidance on data analytics, internal and external audit matters; develop and follow-up on the implementation of various measures/initiatives. Assists in the strategic planning for the department workplans/other initiatives and lead the efforts in implementation.
hrp|17590662|005056a3-d347-1fe1-94de-e37.requirements: Preferably at least 8 years of relevant experience in public sector procurement, and at least 5 years’ experience in a leadership position Strong interpersonal and communication skills (written & spoken) Strong leadership skills Meticulous and attentive to details Able to work in a fast-paced environment and deliver results under tight timelines The successful candidate will be appointed on a 2-year contract at the first instance.
hrp|17590662|005056a3-d347-1fe1-94de-e37.description: The National Library Board (NLB) nurtures Readers for Life, Learning Communities and a Knowledgeable Nation by promoting reading, learning and history through our network of 28 libraries across Singapore, the National Library and the National Archives of Singapore. At NLB, you can look forward to a flexible, hybrid work environment with rewarding, impactful deliverables that improve the lives of the community. With caring colleagues, you will be in an ideal environment for professional development, innovation and impact. We can offer you: • A chance to Impact the Community, bridge gaps and empower everyone with the opportunity for learning and discovery. • An opportunity to Innovate and Push Boundaries. We value ideas, curiosity and a passion for innovation to transform our libraries and archives. • An organisation that Cares for your Growth and Wellbeing through investment in staff development and wellbeing in a supportive and collaborative environment. As an Assistant Director, you play a critical role in the planning and execution of the procurement functions of the department. You will work closely with various stakeholders in reviewing NLB’s policies and the strategic planning for the divisions’ procurement needs. Your key responsibilities include the following:

hrp|17590665|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9be8-2a0.responsibilities: Key duties and responsibilities that need to be performed to meet the primary objective of the job. This will include the important result areas (what) along with the rationale (why). Liaise with other project sections within the Division to ensure timely procurement of contracts for PA’s development projects. Translate requirements into quotation/ tender documents, manage the Invitation to Quote (ITQ)/ Invitation to Tender (ITT) from preparation, calling, evaluation, providing recommendation for all procurements up to contract award for all PA’s development projects. Liaise with co-users on the requirements for integrated CCs projects includes seeking release of funds from co-users for integrated CCs projects. Assist in budgetary forecasts, data collection and analytic, and to set up backend data base. Ensures compliance with appropriate tendering and procurement procedures in accordance with Government procurement & financial procedures and PA’s policies/procedures. Assists to liaise with audits conducted by both internal and external auditors on tenders/ projects. Support the Section in improving internal systems including processes and procedures for greater efficiency. Implement procurement strategies to enhance governance, results and increase operational efficiencies.

hrp|17599440|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-958a-411.responsibilities: You will: • Conduct cost benefit analysis to develop cost-effective proposals, and prepare presentations, and funding papers. • Engage Senior Management and key stakeholders for buy-in on the proposals. • Formulate and operationalise the ministry’s security policy, emergency plans, and business continuity plan with the latest requirements, threats consideration, and operating environment. • Oversee facility programs and contracts, including the procurement of related services/ works/ goods. • Support key development projects in the security, mechanical & electrical engineering, or procurement scope. • Engage the MOH workforce to obtain feedback, and champion change management.
hrp|17599440|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-958a-411.requirements: • Degree in security studies / public safety, project & facility management, contract/ procurement management, mechanical /electrical engineering, information technology, or related fields • Good written, presentation, and people skills, with the ability to engage and influence stakeholders • Good analytical and time management skills • Enjoy working in a team setting and fast-paced environment • Preferably 5 years of relevant work experience Ideal candidate should also possess the following key competencies: • Thinking Clearly & Making Sound Judgements – Strong analytical and critical thinking abilities to support the crafting of sound policy recommendations; ability to grasp timelines, operating context and ground realities. • Learning & Putting Skills into Action - Possesses the drive and curiosity to learn and apply new skills, knowledge and new ways of working. • Improving & Innovating – Ability to seek continual improvements, and to innovate and experiment while managing the risks involved. • Working Effectively with Stakeholders – Ability to mobilise and rally partners and stakeholders towards a collective purpose. As part of the shortlisting process for this role, candidates may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment.
hrp|17599440|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-958a-411.description: You will be responsible for the security and facility programs that support the ministry’s operations and emergency responses. You will be responsible for the formulation and implementation of the ministry’s security policy on classified information and physical infrastructure, emergency response plans, and business continuity plans. You may be rotated across various facility programs covering tenancy management, mechanical & electrical engineering, or security services. You would also have the opportunity to be involved in key infrastructure development projects. You will be working in a fast-paced and dynamic environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders at the same time. To excel in this role, you must possess good written, analytical, and presentation skills. Familiarity with government’s security policy/ framework and operating environment is essential. Experience in security, tender, contract, or construction management, will be advantageous.

hrp|17606892|005056a3-d347-1fe1-95b3-164.responsibilities: This role offers a meaningful opportunity to strengthen the risk management frameworks underpinning national family support schemes. You will play a key role in identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks across the GPLS, working closely with internal and external stakeholders to uphold the integrity of public schemes. The key responsibilities are as follows. (a) Risk Management and Framework Development You will be responsible for the development, review, and continuous improvement of risk management frameworks and controls for the GPLS. This includes monitoring emerging risk trends, evaluating the effectiveness of existing controls, and recommending enhancements to risk detection and mitigation strategies. You will also contribute to risk reporting and maintain documentation that supports sound governance and accountability. (b) Risk Assessment and Appeals You will manage the risk assessment phase of the GPLS claims process, reviewing and adjudicating appeals from claimants flagged by the risk detection model. This requires careful evaluation of each case on its merits, sound judgement in determining outcomes, and thorough documentation to ensure decisions are well-supported and defensible. (c) External Audit Oversight You will be responsible for managing appointed external auditors engaged to review the GPLS, ensuring the audit process is conducted effectively and that findings are properly addressed. This includes overseeing procurement, liaising with auditors, and working with stakeholders to address audit observations in a timely manner. (d) Case Management and Follow-up You will manage GPLS cases referred to RMI, reviewing case details and coordinating with the GPLS operations team and other relevant stakeholders to determine and follow through on the appropriate course of action.
hrp|17606892|005056a3-d347-1fe1-95b3-164.requirements: • We are looking for someone who is analytical, meticulous, and driven, with a strong foundation in risk management principles and the ability to assess complex situations and exercise sound judgement. • Experience in risk management, audit, or compliance would be advantageous. • You should be comfortable working both independently and collaboratively and be able to engage effectively with internal and external stakeholders across the public sector. • Strong written and communication skills are essential. Work location is in Bishan. Only shortlisted candidates will be notified within 4 weeks from the closing date of this position.
hrp|17606892|005056a3-d347-1fe1-95b3-164.description: At Family Life Group (FLG), our mission is to build strong and resilient families and support them through all stages of life, towards the vision of making Singapore a great place for families. The Services Division administers Government services and schemes that enable and encourage family formation. The Risk Management and Investigation (RMI) Branch safeguards the integrity of the Government-Paid Leave and Benefits Schemes (GPLS) and Baby Bonus Schemes by developing and maintaining robust risk management frameworks, including investigations and ensuring that claims under the Child Development Co-Savings Act (CDCA) are administered with integrity and accountability.

hrp|17621480|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-969c-315.responsibilities: We are seeking a proactive and passionate individual to lead the development and implementation of central policies that elevate leadership and workforce excellence across the Government Procurement function. hrp|17629561|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-96d0-2c9.responsibilities: Responsibilities You will be the Procurement Officer reporting to the Deputy Director, Procurement. In this role, you will be part of the team to partner business units to deliver efficient and timely procurement operations while ensuring assurance through understanding business needs and the operating environment, leveraging on technology to enhance users’ experience. In this role, you will, • Support Business Units in their procurement process and partner project officers to: - Plan the project’s procurement needs while ensuring alignment to SportSG Procurement Regulations and the IM. - Develop procurement timeline and milestones based on their specific needs. • Manage the calling of Quotations and Tenders. • Provide advice to project teams on post contract management. • Implement policies and process and review process with outsourced vendor and internal stakeholders to enhance efficiency and achieve value-for-money procurement. • Manage and ensure timely execution of all the following GeBIZ procurement processes for Quotations and Tenders.
hrp|17629561|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-96d0-2c9.requirements: Requirements We are looking for self-motivated individuals who value integrity, teamwork and take pride in going the extra mile to provide excellent service to stakeholders and the community. This individual should be a sport advocate through living an active lifestyle and staying active. In addition, an ideal candidate should possess the following: • Minimum 2 years of relevant working experience in procurement. • Excellent written, communication, and interpersonal skills. • Strong analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving abilities. • Organised, meticulous, proactive, and resourceful. • Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a team. • Knowledge in GeBIZ, data analytics, RPA would be advantageous. The level of offer will commensurate with applicants’ experience and track records. Successful candidates will be offered a 3-year contract in the first instance.

It inspires and evokes the Singapore spirit through shared experiences and strengthens our national identity. We help Singaporeans Live Better Through Sport. Sport Singapore is constantly on the lookout for individuals who are passionate about what they do. Anchored in our values of Passion for Sport, Strength through Teamwork and Care for People, we believe in working and playing, not just as a team, but as a family.

hrp|17629561|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a6d4-361.responsibilities: Responsibilities You will be the Procurement Officer reporting to the Deputy Director, Procurement. In this role, you will be part of the team to partner business units to deliver efficient and timely procurement operations while ensuring assurance through understanding business needs and the operating environment, leveraging on technology to enhance users’ experience. In this role, you will, • Support Business Units in their procurement process and partner project officers to: - Plan the project’s procurement needs while ensuring alignment to SportSG Procurement Regulations and the IM. - Develop procurement timeline and milestones based on their specific needs. • Manage the calling of Quotations and Tenders. • Provide advice to project teams on post contract management. • Implement policies and process and review process with outsourced vendor and internal stakeholders to enhance efficiency and achieve value-for-money procurement. • Manage and ensure timely execution of all the following GeBIZ procurement processes for Quotations and Tenders.
hrp|17629561|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a6d4-361.requirements: Requirements We are looking for self-motivated individuals who value integrity, teamwork and take pride in going the extra mile to provide excellent service to stakeholders and the community. This individual should be a sport advocate through living an active lifestyle and staying active. In addition, an ideal candidate should possess the following: • Minimum 2 years of relevant working experience in procurement. • Excellent written, communication, and interpersonal skills. • Strong analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving abilities. • Organised, meticulous, proactive, and resourceful. • Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a team. • Knowledge in GeBIZ, data analytics, RPA would be advantageous. The level of offer will commensurate with applicants’ experience and track records. Successful candidates will be offered a 3-year contract in the first instance.
hrp|17629561|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a6d4-361.description: At Sport Singapore, we aspire to transform the nation through an active lifestyle designed around innovative, fun and meaningful sporting experiences. Sport has the unique ability to bring people together through play, regardless of age, gender, race, ability or social status. It imparts life values, nurtures character and builds resilience. It inspires and evokes the Singapore spirit through shared experiences and strengthens our national identity. We help Singaporeans Live Better Through Sport. Sport Singapore is constantly on the lookout for individuals who are passionate about what they do. Anchored in our values of Passion for Sport, Strength through Teamwork and Care for People, we believe in working and playing, not just as a team, but as a family.

hrp|17630635|005056a3-d347-1fe1-96df-700.responsibilities: Responsibilities • Manage effective and timely end-to-end processing of agency’s purchase requests, quotations and tenders, including calling, evaluation and award. • Support and provide timely procurement advice to users as Business Partner to ensure compliance with procurement policies and processes. • Assess the potential pitfalls and risks related to procurement, contractual and supplier management, and recommend appropriate mitigation plans to minimize potential disruption to CSA’s operations. • Oversee agency’s procurement systems and provide administration support to meet operational and regulatory requirements • Implement innovative procurement solutions to improve productivity and manage rapid technological changes and evolving cyber-related risks/threats. • Perform data analytics and generate insights for procurement to drive evidence-based decision making and improve efficiency of procurement processes. • Improve outreach, conduct training and facilitate dialogue among the community within the agency. • Other administrative tasks as assigned.
hrp|17630635|005056a3-d347-1fe1-96df-700.requirements: Requirements • A tertiary qualification in any discipline; a background in Business, Supply Chain Management, Information Technology, or Cybersecurity is an advantage. • Preferably with at least 3 years of experience in Procurement, Contract Management or a related field; • Good interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to engage and advise stakeholders at various levels; • A proactive, self-motivated disposition with the ability to work in a fast-paced and dynamic environment; • The ability to work independently as well as collaboratively as a team player. • A positive mindset and willingness to go beyond the scope of procurement work to support the agency’s broader mission. If you share our passion to make a difference in the cyber security landscape, take up the challenge and apply now. All applicants will be notified of whether they are shortlisted or not within four weeks of the closing date of this job posting. For any issues with the application, you may drop your resume with us at csa_recruit@csa.gov.sg
hrp|17630635|005056a3-d347-1fe1-96df-700.description: About CSA Established in 2015, the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA) seeks to keep Singapore’s cyberspace safe and secure to underpin our Nation Security, power a Digital Economy and protect our Digital Way of Life. It maintains an oversight of national cybersecurity functions and works with sector leads to protect Singapore’s Critical Information Infrastructure. CSA also engages with various stakeholders to heighten cyber security awareness, build a vibrant cybersecurity ecosystem supported by a robust workforce, pursue international partnerships and drive regional cybersecurity capacity building programmes. CSA is part of the Prime Minister’s Office and is managed by the Ministry of Digital Development and Information. For more news and information, please visit www.csa.gov.sg

hrp|17647039|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9afc-a5e.responsibilities: You will: • Manage and review preventive and cyclical maintenance of MOH infrastructure and mechanical & electrical systems. • Oversee facility programs and contracts, including the procurement of related services/ works/ goods. • Champion MOH’s sustainability effort and engage the MOH workforce to obtain feedback, and champion change management. • Prepare and submit re-certification of MOH premises for Green Mark Platinum/ Platinum Super Low Energy certification. • Conduct cost benefit analysis to develop cost-effective proposals, and prepare presentations, and funding papers. • Engage Senior Management and key stakeholders for buy-in on the proposals.
hrp|17647039|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9afc-a5e.requirements: • Training in mechanical & electrical engineering, sustainability & facility management, or related fields • Good written, presentation, and people skills, with the ability to engage and influence stakeholders • Good analytical and time management skills • Enjoy working in a team setting and fast-paced environment • Preferably at least 3 years of relevant work experience Ideal candidate should also possess the following key competencies: • Thinking Clearly & Making Sound Judgements – Strong analytical and critical thinking abilities to support the crafting of sound policy recommendations; ability to grasp timelines, operating context and ground realities. • Learning & Putting Skills into Action - Possesses the drive and curiosity to learn and apply new skills, knowledge and new ways of working. • Improving & Innovating – Ability to seek continual improvements, and to innovate and experiment while managing the risks involved. • Working Effectively with Stakeholders – Ability to mobilise and rally partners and stakeholders towards a collective purpose. As part of the shortlisting process for this role, candidates may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment.
hrp|17647039|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9afc-a5e.description: You will be responsible for the facility management and maintenance of mechanical & electrical plants and systems within the MOH HQ premises. This involves overseeing the full spectrum of building maintenance and engineering works that support the ministry’s operations and emergency responses. You will be the appointed as the ‘Sustainability Manager’ for the ministry, playing the key role in championing MOH’s environmental sustainability efforts. You will ensure that MOH continually achieves the WoG sector sustainability targets through resource-efficient facility operations and practices. You will be involved in reviewing mechanical and electrical designs and requirements for infrastructure development / enhancement projects within MOH HQ premises. You may be rotated to oversee various facility programs or building-related services and have the opportunity to be involved in development projects. You will be working in a fast-paced and dynamic environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders at the same time. To excel in this role, you must possess good written, analytical, and presentation skills. Familiarity with GreenGov.SG and Green Mark requirement are essential. Experience in budget, procurement or construction management, will be advantageous.

hrp|17654480|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-97f1-35c.responsibilities: Maintain the security posture and system hardening for both on-premises endpoints and cloud IT infrastructure (e.g. AWS, Azure), including the management of Government security monitoring services such as the Government Cyber Security Operations Centre (GCSOC) and Automated Baseline Log Review (ABLR). Maintain and support IT endpoint and infrastructure security tools, including Microsoft Defender, Secure Service Edge, firewalls, and related technologies. Ensure that critical platforms are reliable, scalable, observable, and maintainable; this includes implementing monitoring and observability tools, and leading incident response and root cause analysis to minimise downtime and prevent recurrence. Develop scripts, Infrastructure as Code (IaC), and internal tools to reduce manual intervention and improve operational efficiency and recovery times. Act as a point of contact with the internal security team on security alerts arising from Security Information and Event Management (SIEM), ABLR, and GCSOC, and represent the team in security-related discussions. Participate in infrastructure cyber hygiene reviews with relevant teams and ensure systems comply with recognised standards such as the Centre for Internet Security (CIS), National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), and Government Technology Agency Instruction Manual for ICT & SS Management. Support regular security assurance activities, including IT audits, penetration testing, and vulnerability assessments, and ensure timely remediation of identified findings. Collaborate across teams to implement security policies and controls, ensuring secure, scalable, and repeatable deployment of IT infrastructure. Manage procurement, projects, and the lifecycle of platform services, including upgrades, maintenance, and deployment of new infrastructure, ensuring security considerations are embedded throughout. Conduct regular reviews of existing on-premises and cloud infrastructure, and provide recommendations to enhance security, performance, and resilience.
hrp|17654480|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-97f1-35c.requirements: Qualifications in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related discipline. At least 5 years of relevant experience in platform reliability engineering and infrastructure security operations, with familiarity in AWS and Azure cloud architecture. Strong communication skills, with the ability to articulate complex security concepts and issues to non-technical stakeholders. Professional certifications such as CISSP, CEH, AWS, Azure, or other relevant certifications in cybersecurity and platform reliability are advantageous.

hrp|17654490|005056a3-d347-1fe1-9f93-af1.description: At the Energy Market Authority (EMA), we do more than keep the lights on. As Singapore's energy landscape evolves, delivering excellent public service is increasingly important in building trust and confidence with our stakeholders. What the Role is As part of the Digital Communications and Customer Experience Department, you will play a key role in advancing EMA's Service Excellence agenda by driving organisation-wide initiatives that strengthen customer-centricity and improve service delivery. You will partner stakeholders across the agency to identify opportunities for service redesign, capability building and continuous improvement. The role also oversees customer operations and case management, ensuring operational insights and digital solutions are leveraged to enhance service quality and customer experience.

hrp|17659179|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-988a-66b.responsibilities: Digital experience development : You will support the development of digital experience for the permanent exhibition, while managing the development and setup of the experience for special exhibitions, contributing to an integrated indoor-outdoor experience of the Memorial. This includes two key areas: Pre- and post- visit experience of the Founders’ Memorial : You will work across teams – including Visitor Experience, Marketing and Communication and Information and Technology – to plan and implement a seamless visitor journey across various digital channels and devices such as social media, online ticketing platforms and digital wayfinding . You will also work with these teams to conduct evaluations and father audience insights into the visitor experience to inform ongoing improvements. Digital brief development: You will collaborate with the Curatorial and Education teams to develop the digital experience brief – comprising technical requirements, desired user experience and suitable digital intervention s – for special exhibitio ns and supporting the development of the digital interactives for the permanent exhibition . Project management: You will manage the development and setup of digital experience for special exhibitions, including budgeting, managing the procurement, user testing and coordinating with the relevant NHB departments to organise the security testing to ensure that the digital system is robust. Additionally, you will also need to work closely with the Curatorial and Exhibitions teams to develop the feedback mechanism / data collection to track visitors’ responses to the exhibition content and experience, liaising with the appointed vendor and analysing the data collected. Data management: You will work as a team to tag, organise and store citizens’ stories that are collected through the “Project Citizens” public call , for eventual display at the FM. “Project Citizens” was a campaign launched by the FM in 2025. Since 2025, the Memorial has been collecting stories of the founding generation of citizens through a senior engagement programme which is part of “Project Citizens”. These stories are currently being processed by the Education and Digital officers at the Memorial. You will be part of this project team to process the stories to be presented in the permanent exhibition, while working on the content management system and data management of the stories.
hrp|17659179|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-988a-66b.requirements: Relevant qualifications or equivalent professional experience in digital media, interaction design, UX/UI design, or a related field. An interest or appreciation of Singapore’s history is an advantage . Digital Design & Management - Demonstrated experience in digital media design – including content strategy, art direction, UX/ UI design, wireframing – and developing digital experiences in exhibitions. Basic knowledge of web and frontend technologies, familiarity with the use of platforms such as Matterport 3D and immersive technologies such as AR/VR/MR tools is advantageous . Good project management, analytical and problem-solving skills . A collaborative team player with excellent interpersonal and stakeholder management skills , and able to work well independently . As the FM is an institution being built from the ground-up, the candidate should be able to navigate changes , multiple stakeholders and a fast-moving environment wh ere processe s are still being established . Familiarity with or willingness to learn government tools and procurement guidelines will also be essential . Some weekend and after-work hours engagements might be required – candidates should be prepared to exercise some flexibility in the work schedule .
hrp|17659179|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-988a-66b.description: Do you love Singapore for punching above its weight as a Little Red Dot? Can you identify with the grit exhibited by our founding leaders and generation as they worked hard to build Singapore to what it is today? Are you keen to explore ideas, leveraging technology to support storytelling and enhance the visitor experience of a Singapore museum? If the answer is "yes", join us at the Founders' Memorial (FM)! At the FM, we are creating a brand-new garden-museum experience for Singaporeans, by Singaporeans. A national landmark at the heart of our garden city, uncovering the story of how independent Singapore came to be, and bringing Singaporeans across generations together to reflect and have bold conversations about what our founding values mean today and for our future. The FM is seeking a suitable candidate to join the Digital team to develop interactive digital experiences and content for the Founders’ Memorial, across our exhibitions and website, leveraging the potential of digital technology to create compelling, accessible and engaging experiences for our diverse audiences. You will work collaboratively with the Curatorial and Exhibitions teams, and with creatives to present the story of how Singapore came to be, through multi-sensory, emotive and immersive experiences! With the Visitor Experience and Marketing and Communications team, you will leverage digital channels and devices to support a seamless, end-to-end visitor journey of the Founders’ Memorial. Look forward to being a part of creating a living Memorial that unites, challenges and inspires Singaporeans of all generations towards a brighter future!

hrp|17659189|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-988a-69f.responsibilities: Budget t racking and r eporting : You will support the team lead in tracking and reporting on FM's budget utilisation, including the usage of grants and donations. This includes maintaining up-to-date records of expenditure, preparing regular budget reports, and identifying opportunities to reallocate funds where they are needed most – ensuring healthy and effective utilisation of FM's overall budget. Corporate services : Working as a team, you will coordinate annual workplan and budgeting exercise and track the Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) on a quarterly basis. You will be required to provide historical benchmarks of the budget and KPIs for future planning and coordinate across the different work teams to conduct evaluation and analysis , to report the key insights as part of the annual KPI reporting. Finance and a dministrative s upport On the finance side, you will develop the standard operating procedures for F M ’s cash collection and transfer to banks, and work with officers to resolve budget and payment issues. You will play a key role in ensuring that payments to FM's vendors are processed accurately and in a timely manner . On the administrative side, you w ill manage the setup of the FM office at Bay East Garden – from developing the requirement specifications to managing the procurement for the office move and setup in 2027, and coordinating the office move in late 2027 or early 2028. You will also provide scheduling and admin istrati ve support to the Director and support to the VIP visits to the Memorial on an ongoing basis and oversee the day-to-day administrative needs of the F M ’s office. You will also wor k with the Board Secretariat and provide support for FM's C ommittee /Board meetings, which are held every qu arter . This includes managing RSVPs, preparing meeting materials for circulation arranging refreshments, and ensuring the smooth running of each meeting.
hrp|17659189|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-988a-69f.requirements: Relevant qualifications or equivalent professional experience in finance, business administration, or a related field. Preferably a t least 3 years of experience in a related role, preferably in a public sector or institutional setting. Budget Planning & Admin - Ability to execute activities relating to short term and long - term budget planning and administration to support the operations and strategic outcomes of the division . Corporate Performance Management - Ability to develop and implement performance management frameworks and track key performance indicators (KPIs) to drive achievement of the division's strategic priorities . Highly organised and meticulous, with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple workstreams concurrently. Strong interpersonal, communication, and written skills, with the ability to work effectively across teams and with external stakeholders. Proficient in Microsoft Excel, with good knowledge of its functionalities and tools to support data management and budget tracking. Knowledge of government budget tracking systems is advantageous . As the FM is an institution being built from the ground up, the candidate should be able to navigate change, multiple stakeholders, and a fast-moving environment where processes are still being established . Familiarity with or willingness to learn government tools and procurement guidelines will also be essential. Candidates should be prepared to exercise flexibility in their work schedule, as some weekend and after-hours engagements may be required .

hrp|17659439|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-988f-835.description: The Deputy Director will provide strategic leadership across AI masterplanning, AI governance, and AI collaboration and programme management. For masterplanning, the Deputy Director will develop a strategic masterplan for all applied AI domains (Vision AI, Embodied AI, Language AI, large language and large multimodal models, AI safety & security, and emerging technologies). For AI governance, the Deputy Director will establish robust frameworks that embeds responsible AI practices throughout HTX’s initiatives. For AI collaboration and programme management, the role will foster strategic AI collaboration with industry, academia and other government agencies, and programme manage end to end, cross functional AI projects. Together, these efforts will deliver AI solutions that support our public safety mission, improve citizen experience, and increase operational productivity.

hrp|17697397|005056a3-d347-1fe1-9a8c-45b.responsibilities: We are seeking a proactive and passionate individual to lead the development and implementation of central policies that elevate leadership and workforce excellence across the Government Procurement function. This pivotal role will shape talent strategies, design leadership development programs, and drive workforce engagement initiatives in collaboration with both internal and external stakeholders to build a future-ready procurement workforce and strengthen capabilities across government. Key Responsibilities Leadership and Talent Development • Drive the implementation of leadership and talent development strategies for the Government Procurement function, including leadership rotations, succession planning, and talent engagement initiatives to build a strong leadership pipeline across agencies. • Serve as the secretariat for the Joint Finance and Procurement Talent Development Committee and act as the primary liaison with HR counterparts across agencies to coordinate and implement talent initiatives effectively. Career Development and Mobility • Partner with government agencies to design and facilitate cross-agency learning experiences such as Structured Job Rotations (SJR), GIG Projects, Short-Term Immersion Programmes (STIP), and Private Sector Attachment Programmes. • Leverage the One Talent Gateway (OTG) portal to promote transparency and accessibility of career opportunities within the Procurement community. Curate and develop engaging content to help officers better understand various career pathways and growth opportunities. Stakeholder Engagement and Strategic Partnerships • Maintain strong engagement with HR teams across agencies through regular consultations to align development initiatives with agency needs. • Collaborate with private sector and industry partners to co-create impactful attachment opportunities and assess their effectiveness and value. • Work closely with procurement leaders to design developmental initiatives that promote continuous learning and career growth within the procurement workforce. • Foster a vibrant and connected procurement community through networking events and community-building activities. • Provide data-driven insights and performance reporting to senior management to track the effectiveness and outcomes of workforce development efforts.

hrp|17718487|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9b95-733.responsibilities: • Ensure compliance and implementation of property management policies and processes across all overseas missions for acquisition, disposal and leasing. • Assist Deputy Chief Properties to coordinate and staff high-level property assessment visits. Provide first-cut analytical insights and recommendations for potential acquisition of overseas properties. • Plan, Review and Implement the Master Programmes for acquisition and disposal of Government-owned properties, relocation of rented office (inclusive of office fit-out works) and new office set-up. • Gather research information and analyse relevant data for policy reviews, including housing policies (e.g., rentals) for MFA staff overseas. • Provide technical and contractual advice (in consultation with legal experts) to overseas missions on property transactions, negotiations on sales/purchase agreements and tenancy agreements to ensure value-for-money while balancing operational needs. • Assist Deputy Chief Properties to design and implement relevant frameworks for new mission establishment. • Conduct reviews establish the rentals of housing accommodation of MFA staff overseas. • Evaluate requests to acquire, lease and dispose properties and make recommendations to relevant Approving Authorities. • Conduct periodic review of the rental budget allocated for all rented offices and housing accommodation overseas. • Compile and upkeep databases/documents for all properties and prepare all returns related to land and buildings under the purview of MFA for different types of submissions. • Compile and Compute Right-of-Use (ROU) assets for all leased properties based on prevailing lease accounting principles. • Conduct procurement for all related services for the Section (e.g. valuation, property agents, property consultants, conveyancing lawyers, office fit-out companies, etc.) Ensure all related procurements adhere to Singapore Government guidelines. Number of years of experience required: • Around 10 years’ of working experience with at least 5 years’ of experience in the property administration or real estate industry focusing on either leasing or acquisitions.

hrp|17751825|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9c9a-743.responsibilities: Perform food radioactivity testing and all related functions to support SFA food safety monitoring and surveillance programs. Develop, validate and implement analytical methods for determination of natural/artificial alpha, beta and gamma emitting radionuclides. Lead the design, planning and implementation of radiological monitoring programs to establish representative baseline radioactivity levels in food. Develop and implement advanced data analytics approaches, including statistical modelling and exploratory artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques, to support trend analysis, anomaly detection, and predictive insights from radiological monitoring data. Develop data visualization tools, dashboards, and automated workflows to facilitate data interpretation and decision-making to support food safety surveillance and preparedness. Implement laboratory quality assurance programs to ensure that laboratory practices are in full compliance with ISO/IEC 17025:2017 standards. Prepare method and equipment SOPs and quality documents to be used by the team. Procurement of lab supplies and equipment to support operations of the laboratory. Prepare technical reports, scientific publications, project updates, and presentations for management and other stakeholders. Conduct technical trainings and organize proficiency testing programs for ASEAN participants and commercial laboratories to strengthen radionuclide testing capability in Singapore and ASEAN region.
hrp|17751825|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9c9a-743.requirements: The candidate should have a BSc, MSc or PhD in Chemistry, Radiochemistry, or other related scientific fields. Good knowledge and experience in radionuclide analysis, radiochemical separations, and low-level radioactivity measurements will be an advantage. Experience with radioanalytical instrumentation (alpha spectrometer, liquid scintillation counter, gamma spectrometer) and Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometer will be an advantage. Experience in method development and method validation, preferably in food matrices. Knowledge of data science, statistical analysis, machine learning, artificial intelligence, and scientific programming languages (e.g. Python or R). Experience in developing data visualization tools, dashboards, or analytics platforms to support scientific decision-making. Experience in implementing ISO/IEC 17025:2017 laboratory quality standards. Experience in managing multidisciplinary scientific projects and coordinating stakeholders. Strong scientific writing, communication and stakeholder engagement skills. Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills. Highly motivated and proactive, with a strong sense of ownership and accountability. Self-driven and capable of working independently and collaboratively. Work Location National Centre for Food Science, 7 International Business Park, Singapore 609919.
hrp|17751825|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9c9a-743.description: The mission of SFA is to ensure and secure a supply of safe food for Singapore. The National Centre for Food Science (NCFS) supports SFA’s vision of ensuring safe food for all by being a national reference laboratory on food science, conducting food safety monitoring to generate scientific data for enforcement of food regulations, support of risk assessment and protection of consumer health. NCFS oversees the application of science and technology to enable an evidence-based approach for ensuring food safety in partnership with stakeholders across the entire food chain and research institutions to address emerging food safety and security concerns. You will be part of a dynamic team of the Food Science Rapid Response Department (FSRRD) under NCFS to provide support to SFA’s food safety regulatory testing and market monitoring programs. This is a fantastic opportunity for you to learn and apply a wide range of cutting-edge testing and diagnostic techniques to solve real world problems and safeguard the food safety for Singaporeans. The Specialist Teams under FSRRD strive to continue developing our scientific knowledge and testing capabilities to keep pace with the challenges of emerging foodborne chemical, radiochemical and biological hazards. We collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to enhance food safety standards in the region, and support food security initiatives such as high-tech farming and novel food innovation. You will be deployed to the Food Radioactivity Specialist Team under FSRRD, playing a key role in developing new analytical methods for strengthening and broadening the testing capabilities and for enabling risk assessment to support SFA’s operation needs for food safety regulatory function and market monitoring programs.

hrp|17765796|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9cef-929.description: The Home Team Science and Technology Agency (HTX) is a statutory board of the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), and also the Singapore public sector’s first Science and Technology agency that works at the forefront of science and technology to amplify, augment and accelerate the Home Team’s advantage and secure Singapore’s frontline of security. HTX integrates a diverse range of scientific and engineering capabilities to innovate and deliver transformative and operationally ready solutions for homeland security. The successful job holder will be a member of the Procurement Plans team to develop and deliver reports and strategic updates to Senior Management, drive internal and external change management initiatives, and contribute to the Central Procurement Office (CPO)’s transformation through data-driven insights and stakeholder engagement.

hrp|17766550|005056a3-d347-1fe1-9d8b-5b9.responsibilities: As an Executive in the Outreach & Engagement Branch in CPS, your roles and responsibilities include: • Collaborating on capability development initiatives with strategic partners. • Developing and implementing CPS’s stakeholder engagement plan. • Co-developing and delivering security/outreach initiatives across various industries by working with Ministry of Home Affairs Headquarters and Home Team Departments on National Programmes such as SGSecure training, SaferSG outreach and counter-terrorism seminars. • Engaging private sector stakeholders on security issues and conducting training needs analysis to deliver appropriate solutions. • Collaborating with protective security community and industry stakeholders to educate public on security initiatives and raise the profile of the security industry. • Growing Communities of Practitioners through outreach and engagement of stakeholders to facilitate exchange of expertise and information with industry partners. • Promoting best practices in procurement of security services for public and private sector buyers. • Driving public and internal communications for CPS. • Developing and administering a new service excellence system for management of CPS related queries and feedback, in accordance with SPF’s service delivery standards.
hrp|17766550|005056a3-d347-1fe1-9d8b-5b9.requirements: • Experience with industry-standard design tools like Adobe Creative Cloud or Canva is preferred. • Prior work experience in training, community engagement or communications is an advantage. • Some work experience in Protective Security, Infrastructure Protection or Risk Management would be ideal. • Resilient, able to work effectively in a dynamic environment and able to adapt quickly to shifting priorities. • Strong communication and writing skills. • Good interpersonal skills with the ability to engage people at all levels and ability to work independently are essential. • The officer must be a strong team player in collaborating and contributing beyond one's immediate scope to achieve shared outcomes for the team. • Possess a can-do attitude and willingness to take on diverse tasks to support the team's objectives. Short-listed candidates will be contacted within two weeks of the application closing date.
hrp|17766550|005056a3-d347-1fe1-9d8b-5b9.description: This role is part of MHA’s Civilian Generalist career track. Learn more: https://go.gov.sg/civiliangeneralist The Singapore Police Force (SPF) plays a critical role in keeping Singapore safe and secure with our mission to prevent, deter and detect crime. The Centre for Protective Security (CPS) was operationalised to support the implementation of the Infrastructure Protection Act (IPA) and support the transformation of the security industry. The key functions of CPS are Infrastructure Protection Regulation, Capability Development and Protective Engineering. In addition, CPS collaborates with various public and private stakeholders to reinforce the IPA and synergise efforts to improve the security industry. The Outreach & Engagement Branch collaborates with strategic partners on capability development initiatives, carries out security/outreach initiatives, promotes best practices in security services procurement as well performs the public communications function for CPS-related queries/feedback/requests, to support MHA in implementing policies and establishing standards to build a competitive security industry. As an Executive, Outreach & Engagement, you play an important role in developing and implementing sustained engagement with CPS stakeholders to propagate Protective Security (PS) knowledge and performing the public communications function. You will be placed under the Management Executive Scheme.

hrp|17770195|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9cff-241.responsibilities: This role covers the end-to-end planning, coordination and execution of regional and international meetings, with a primary focus on logistical, administrative and operational support. Responsibilities include coordinating meeting schedules and requirements, liaising with internal stakeholders and external partners, managing venue and on-site arrangements, supporting procurement and vendor coordination, facilitating claims processing and payments, preparing administrative submissions and documentation, and ensuring the smooth delivery of meeting-related services. The role also requires sound knowledge of procurement processes and the ability to manage procurement activities, including preparing specifications, evaluating quotations, coordinating with vendors, and ensuring compliance with organisational procedures. The selected candidate may also be required to support cross-agency committees and working groups, and to work closely with a broad range of stakeholders to ensure that meetings and events are delivered professionally, efficiently and in accordance with organisational requirements.
hrp|17770195|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9cff-241.requirements: Preferably with at least 8 years of relevant experience in event management. Strong interest in event management, with a well-organised, meticulous and resourceful approach. Self-motivated and able to perform effectively in a fast-paced and dynamic environment. Able to work both independently and collaboratively as part of a team. Willing to work beyond regular office hours and on weekends, where required. Strong verbal and written communication skills. Strong interpersonal and stakeholder management skills. Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel and PowerPoint. This contract will end in November 2027. As part of the shortlisting process for this role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment. All applicants will be notified on whether they are shortlisted or not within 4 weeks of the closing date of this job posting.

hrp|17781935|005056a3-d347-1fe1-9db8-388.responsibilities: The jobholder is responsible for the Governance, Risk, audit and process management of enterprise ICT infrastructure services systems (such as end-user devices, virtualised infrastructure, active directory, network, serve, etc.) that are across all MHA Home Team Departments (HTDs). hrp|17781935|005056a3-d347-1fe1-9db8-388.requirements: • Tertiary qualification in Electronics/ Electrical Engineering, Computer Studies, or related disciplines such as ICT Technology or Cyber Security. • Minimally 1 year working experience in cyber security related programs such as audits support, risk assessments, audit findings remediation and cyber security compliance management. • In-depth understanding of desktop clients/servers, cloud infrastructure and networks, working knowledge/skills in system administration such as Microsoft Windows Server and Active Directory. hrp|17781935|005056a3-d347-1fe1-9db8-388.description: HTX is the world’s first Science and Technology agency that integrates a diverse range of scientific and engineering capabilities to innovate and deliver transformative and operationally ready solutions for homeland security. As a statutory board of the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and integral to the Home Team, HTX works at the forefront of science and technology to empower Singapore’s frontline of security. Our shared mission is to amplify, augment and accelerate the Home Team’s advantage and secure Singapore as the safest place on planet earth. You play an important role in the implementation and maintenance of ICT end-user devices, networks and infrastructures for a Home Team Department (e.g. Singapore Police Force, Singapore Civil Defence Force, Singapore Prison Service, Immigration & Checkpoints Authority, etc.), ensuring their operational readiness at all times.

hrp|17790268|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9ec8-4ab.responsibilities: Key roles and responsibilities: Strategic Oversight of Contract Management: Oversee all CC development contracts across the full project lifecycle, covering pre-construction design stage engagement through construction administration and post-construction final account closure, ensuring contracts are administered in accordance with PA policies, government IMs, and relevant authorities’ requirements. Establish Governance Frameworks: Develop and maintain contract administration, including variation order management, extension of time assessments, loss and expense claims, and final account negotiations, to protect PA's contractual and financial interests and ensure all records are properly maintained and audit-ready. Provide Expert Contractual Advice: Advise senior management on complex or contentious contract matters, including dispute resolution and claims management, to achieve timely and cost-effective outcomes. Monitor Contract Performance: Track key milestones, financial commitments, and contractor performance across the development portfolio to identify risks early and implement appropriate mitigation measures. Manage Stakeholders and Contracting Parties Relationships: Build and maintain effective working relationships with project divisions, consultants, and contracting parties, ensuring PA's positions are clearly communicated,appropriately documented and consistently upheld. Develop Cost Intelligence: Lead development of construction cost database and analytics to support benchmarking, planning, and decision-making across the development portfolio. Align Project Cost Planning, Budgeting, and Financial Submissions with Corporate Finance Division requirements. Drive Continuous Improvement: Identify opportunities to streamline contract management workflows, strengthen governance controls, and leverage technology to enhance efficiency, transparency and audit readiness. Build Team Capability and Manage Resources: Lead capability development across the unit, building team competencies in contract administration and governance, while managing budget, manpower planning, and workplan development to ensure the unit operates sustainably and delivers on its mandate.
hrp|17790268|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9ec8-4ab.requirements: Professional Qualification: Relevant professional qualification in building, construction management, quantity surveying, or a related field. Professional certificates such as Singapore Institute of Surveyors & Valuers, Quantity Surveyor’s accreditation is an added advantage. Experience: Minimum 15 years working experience in the infrastructure/building field and with experience leading a team. Prior experience in procurement and/or contracts management in a statutory board or government agency context and familiarity with BCA procurement frameworks (e.g. PQM, QFM), GeBIZ and the Government Instruction Manual. Experience managing development project across the full project cycle (i.e. from design to post construction) with minimum project cost of $30 million. Knowledge and experience with (i) dispute resolution mechanisms such as adjudication or mediation, and (ii) collaborative contracting for development and/or facilities management contracts, will be an added advantage. Skills: Good knowledge of construction contract law, standard forms of contract (e.g. PSSCOC), and variation/claims management. Sound judgment in contract governance and dispute resolution. Good leadership qualities – ability to lead and drive teams to perform and achieve desired outcomes, sectoral knowledge and can think strategically. Good interpersonal and communication skills to engage stakeholders (internal and external). Self-driven individual who champions excellence, innovation and digitalisation. Familiarity with Building Information Modelling (BIM) and digital contract management tools will be an added advantage. Only shortlisted candidates whose qualifications and experience best meet our requirements will be contacted.
hrp|17790268|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9ec8-4ab.description: The Deputy Director (Contract Management – Development) leads the end-to-end contract management function for all PA development project contracts, spanning the full project lifecycle from pre-construction design stage through to post-construction final account closure. The role ensures that development contracts are administered with rigour and governance, protecting PA's interests while enabling the timely delivery of community infrastructure. Working closely with project divisions, consultants, and contractors, the role serves as the expert contractual voice to senior management and drives consistent contract administration standards across the development portfolio, while building a high-performing team and maintaining robust governance frameworks that uphold PA's standards of integrity and operational excellence.

hrp|17795362|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9e9d-624.responsibilities: You will be responsible for managing the full spectrum of contract and procurement activities supporting Home Team fitness training and SPF TraCom training programmes. Working closely with internal stakeholders and external service providers, you will ensure that training contracts are effectively managed, service delivery standards are met, and training capabilities are continuously enhanced. Your key responsibilities will include: • Developing, implementing, and sustaining Home Team fitness training capabilities and SPF TraCom training programmes, including governance oversight and concept of operations reviews • Managing the end-to-end procurement process, from defining specifications and conducting tender exercises to processing payments, managing contract variations, and ensuring compliance with service level agreements • Monitoring contract fulfilment and performance indicators across fitness training and TraCom training contracts, with a combined budget of approximately $8 million • Conducting process reviews for IPPT and other training systems, mapping workflows, gathering stakeholder feedback, and driving implementation of improvements • Researching and evaluating innovative training technologies, including AI-enabled solutions, wearable technology, and AR/VR platforms, and collaborating with technology providers on trials and feasibility assessments • Building and maintaining strategic partnerships with external agencies to enhance fitness training resources and programmes across the Home Team and SPF TraCom
hrp|17795362|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9e9d-624.requirements: • Field of studies in a relevant discipline • Strong understanding of project management methodologies and procurement processes • Knowledge of training and development principles, particularly in a law enforcement or public safety context • Experience in managing procurement processes, particularly for technology or service-related contracts • Experience collaborating with diverse internal and external stakeholders, including public agencies and service providers • Strong analytical, communication, and stakeholder management skills • Adaptable, detail-oriented, and able to work effectively under pressure Short-listed candidates will be contacted within two weeks of the application closing date.
hrp|17795362|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9e9d-624.description: This role is part of MHA’s Civilian Generalist career track. Learn more: https://go.gov.sg/civiliangeneralist Are you a driven professional with a passion for training development and a strong eye for contract and procurement management? Do you thrive in a dynamic environment where your work directly enhances the capabilities of Singapore's Home Team? If so, we invite you to join us at the Basic Training School (BTS), Training Command (TraCom), Singapore Police Force (SPF). TraCom is responsible for delivering foundational training programmes that build the operational readiness of HT officers. As a Training Officer 1 (Contract Management), you will play a pivotal role in developing, implementing, and sustaining fitness training capabilities across the Home Team, as well as SPF Training Command programmes managed by BTS. You will be placed under the Management Executive Scheme.
