hrp|17804715|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9ec8-4e2.responsibilities: Manage the solutioning, technical implementation, and delivery of enhancements and new features for NLB Mobile, a one-stop library app serving Singapore's diverse reading community across iOS and Android. Engage internal stakeholders and product owners to shape and finalise the product roadmap, incorporating emerging technologies to keep the app at the cutting edge. Manage Agile sprint delivery, removing blockers for the team and ensuring features are delivered on time and to a high standard of quality. Oversee the full release process for every app update to the iOS App Store and Google Play Store, including coordinating user acceptance testing and ensuring thorough quality assurance across all releases. Provide regular, structured updates to stakeholders and the product owner on project progress, risks, and issues. Manage the timely resolution of bugs and support incidents in adherence to SLAs, ensuring a consistently positive experience for NLB's patrons. Coordinate infrastructure upgrades, security patches, and platform and framework updates, while monitoring changes to dependent systems to safeguard the app's day-to-day functioning. Responsible for end-to-end procurement of IT services, ensuring objectivity, transparency and best value for NLB and its patrons. Manage the vendors and contracts to ensure that the performance of vendors and deliverables are in accordance to the tender and service level agreements.
hrp|17804715|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9ec8-4e2.requirements: Degree or Diploma in IT, Computer Science, or a related discipline, with at least 3 years of relevant experience in mobile app development or mobile app project management. Proven experience working in Agile development environments, with the ability to manage sprint delivery, track progress, and remove blockers effectively. Meticulous and well-organised, with the ability to manage multiple workstreams, stakeholders, and competing priorities concurrently. Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively across technical and non-technical teams and manage stakeholders. Experience in vendor management, , and managing outsourced development or operations teams. The following technical knowledge would be an added advantage: Familiarity with mobile app development concepts, including native and cross-platform frameworks such as Flutter or React Native. Familiarity with cloud infrastructure, basic DevOps practices and software quality assurance practices, and test automation. Awareness of user experience design, mobile accessibility standards (e.g. WCAG), and inclusive design principles. Exposure to emerging technologies such as AI/ML, LLMs, personalisation engines, or chatbots. Familiarity with Government Procurement Process, IM8 guidelines and contract management would have an added advantage. The office location is at ESR BizPark@Chai Chee. Successful candidate will be appointed on a 2-year contract.
hrp|17804715|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9ec8-4e2.description: The National Library Board (NLB) nurtures Readers for Life, Learning Communities and a Knowledgeable Nation by promoting reading, learning and history through our network of 28 libraries across Singapore, the National Library and the National Archives of Singapore. At NLB, you can look forward to a flexible, hybrid work environment with rewarding, impactful deliverables that improve the lives of the community. With caring colleagues, you will be in an ideal environment for professional development, innovation and impact. We can offer you: • A chance to Impact the Community, bridge gaps and empower everyone with the opportunity for learning and discovery. • An opportunity to Innovate and Push Boundaries. We value ideas, curiosity and a passion for innovation to transform our libraries and archives. • An organisation that Cares for your Growth and Wellbeing through investment in staff development and wellbeing in a supportive and collaborative environment.

hrp|17807912|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a497-5c9.responsibilities: You will support the Land Management Team from the Sport Infrastructure Group in administrative and operational support for leasing and tenancy matters. The scope of work includes, but is not limited to, assisting with document preparation, tenancy record maintenance, revenue monitoring, payment tracking, arrears management, valuation request coordination, tenant enquiries, and asset record reconciliation. You will be reporting to the Assistant Director, Land Management. In this role, You will: • Prepare, check, and verify leasing and tenancy-related documents for input into the relevant system to support the monitoring of revenue. • Update and maintain the monthly tenancy schedule to ensure that tenancy details are accurate and current. • Track and monitor ad-hoc and recurring rentals, fees, and other related payments. • Assist in managing valuation requests, including coordinating the required information and verifying payment details where applicable. • Monitor outstanding arrears owed by tenants and assist in following up on overdue payments. • Attend to enquiries and feedback from tenants and members of the public on land, leasing, and tenancy matters, and escalate complex cases where necessary. • Reconcile asset records to ensure that the information is consistent, complete, and properly maintained. Conduct site visit to the premises to verify the records. • Assist with procurement of services related to leasing and tenancy matters, including preparing procurement documents, obtaining quotations where required, coordinating approvals, and tracking service delivery. • Assist with filing, record-keeping, data entry, and other administrative tasks related to leasing and tenancy matters. • Support any other duties assigned that are related to leasing, tenancy administration, revenue tracking, or asset management.
hrp|17807912|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a497-5c9.requirements: We are looking for self-motivated individuals who value integrity, teamwork and take pride in going the extra mile to provide excellent service to stakeholders and the community. This individual should be a sport advocate through living an active lifestyle and staying active. In addition, an ideal candidate should possess the following: • Preferably with prior administrative experience in leasing, tenancy management, revenue tracking, or a related area. • Strong attention to detail and accuracy in handling information. • Able to work independently and follow up on outstanding matters in a timely and systematic manner. • Comfortable handling data entry, document verification, record reconciliation, and basic reporting tasks. • Proficient in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, Word, and Outlook. • Be able to work independently with minimal supervision. • Ability to work effectively in a team and communicate well with colleagues. • Positive, pro-active and good team player. • Passion to work in sports industry. Only shortlisted candidates will be notified. The level of offer will be commensurate with applicants’ experience and track records.

Sport has the unique ability to bring people together through play, regardless of age, gender, race, ability or social status. It imparts life values, nurtures character and builds resilience. It inspires and evokes the Singapore spirit through shared experiences and strengthens our national identity. We help Singaporeans Live Better Through Sport. hrp|17808067|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9ed7-7a1.responsibilities: The Lead Associate/Senior Associate/Associate (Digital Transformation) will be part of the business ops team to conceptualise, plan and execute the implementation of the new GeBIZ system. The scope will include: • Working with agencies across WOG to jointly review, challenge and streamline existing procurement processes to enable the digitalisation of a seamless Budget-Procure-to-Pay experience. • Change management with agencies across WOG to ensure a smooth and effective implementation of the GeBIZ system. • Work with technical partners and stakeholders in the Budget-Procure-to-Pay value chain to align the goals thereby fostering closer collaboration. • Manage the tender and the supplier such that the GeBIZ project is executed efficiently and on schedule in an agile manner. • Explore, leverage and implement innovative new technologies to support end-to-end government procurement requirements. • Undertake data analytics efforts to ensure proper governance of procurement practices.
hrp|17808067|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9ed7-7a1.requirements: • Professionals with experience in one or more of the following areas - procurement, implementing organisational systems, digital transformation, project management. • Ability to look at issues from a WOG perspective, review the status quo and integrate procurement policy considerations and operational requirements with what is technologically feasible. • Have a dare-to-do attitude and not afraid to challenge the status quo. • Self-driven and committed individual able to work independently and within teams. • Strong critical thinking, analytical and project management skills. • Strong communication skills and ability to work collaboratively with internal and external stakeholders. • Excellent writing ability and presentation skills. • Entry-level positions available for candidates with demonstrated interest in procurement and/or digital transformation.
hrp|17808067|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-9ed7-7a1.description: The Government Procurement Function Office (GPFO) oversees the Government procurement policies, practices, systems and workforce. Among other responsibilities, it is responsible for driving transformation of the whole-of-government (WOG) procurement function, including digital transformation. MOF-GPFO is embarking on a project to refresh the current GeBIZ. GeBIZ is a WOG platform for agencies to publish their tenders and suppliers to submit their proposals.

hrp|17809526|005056a3-d347-1fe1-9ee1-4e7.responsibilities: 1. Overall Governance and Centre Oversight Establish and maintain governance frameworks across the 3 Chinatown AACs (Banda, Chin Swee, Jalan Kukoh) and Jalan Besar AAC, ensuring compliance with PA Financial Rules and Regulations, Government Instruction Manual requirements, AIC standards, and other statutory requirements. Coordinate with HQ divisions (Legal Service, Grassroots Service, Internal Audit, Field Governance Office) on policy implementation, audit clearance, and approvals for external agency agreements. 2. Financial Governance, Procurement and Controls Oversee financial controls across centres, ensuring sound accounting practices, expenditure management, and budget monitoring. Oversee procurement and revenue contracting processes in compliance with Grassroots Financial Rules and internal policies. 3. AIC Performance Management and Reporting Develop and maintain systems to track AIC KPIs across centres, ensuring accurate data collection, analysis, and timely reporting of performance outcomes, programme delivery, and governance matters to AIC and PA management. Conduct variance analysis and drive corrective actions to meet performance targets. 4. Community Outreach and Stakeholder Engagement Drive outreach strategies to recruit and engage elderly residents across the centres. Build and maintain relationships with community stakeholders, partners, beneficiaries, and volunteers to strengthen programme reach and impact. Facilitate coordination between centres and external stakeholders to optimise partnerships and resource sharing. 5. Capability Building and Governance Training Coordinate governance, finance, and compliance training for all AAC staff to ensure consistent understanding and application of policies and procedures. Build operational capability across centres to strengthen compliance culture and service delivery standards. 6. Transition to Corporate Outsourcing Model and Transfer of Operations Lead the development of operational processes and governance structures to ensure service continuity and compliance with AIC and PA requirements throughout the outsourcing transition. Oversee service provider performance and accountability, and coordinate structured planning for the eventual transfer of operations back to AIC, covering knowledge transfer, risk management, and operational readiness.
hrp|17809526|005056a3-d347-1fe1-9ee1-4e7.requirements: a. Minimum 3 years of experience in procurement and contract management, or governance and compliance, with experience managing complex procurement processes and outsourcing contracts. b. At least 3 years of supervisory experience with accountability for operational oversight, team management, and delivery of outcomes. c. Experience in stakeholder engagement and multi-agency coordination
hrp|17809526|005056a3-d347-1fe1-9ee1-4e7.description: In support of PA’s mission to foster community participation, the Senior Manager (Special Project) provides governance oversight and operational coordination across the three Chinatown Active Ageing Centres (AACs) and one Jalan Besar AAC. hrp|17834555|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a085-83f.responsibilities: The job holder will be responsible for the following: • Work closely with the HTX divisions, MHA Home Team Departments (HTDs) and MHA HQ (MHQ) in developing appropriate procurement strategies / approaches to achieve effective procurement in supporting the departments’ operations. • Prepare tender documentation and manage the tendering and award process using Government’s electronic procurement system, to ensure timeliness of procurement and contract implementation. • Provide professional advice to HTX divisions, HTDs and MHQ division on best practices in sourcing, contract management and supplier management practices. • Conduct spend analysis on procurement data to formulate long term procurement strategies for better management of procurement for effective procurement. • Capture lessons learnt as case studies including good practices and irregularities and present at procurement Community of Practice forums and / or in-house courses for sharing and learning. • Other ad-hoc initiatives and projects may be assigned.

hrp|17837644|005056a3-d347-1fe1-a091-9d3.responsibilities: Key Responsibilities: You may share and coordinate the responsibilities with other team members, as appropriate, to ensure effective delivery of work. 1. Learning Strategy & Needs Analysis Partner with Professional Groups to regularly review learning requirements and ensure continued relevance. This includes initiating reviews of learning policies and frameworks where necessary and advising officers on local and overseas learning policies. Conduct Learning Needs Analysis for different groups of officers and propose follow-up actions to address learning gaps or fulfil identified needs. 2. Programme Management & Delivery Plan and deliver induction and orientation programmes to support the effective onboarding and integration of new officers. Ensure new hires complete mandatory training requirements under the Career Milestones Training Framework, including tracking and following up on completion status. Organise in-house courses and dedicated training runs based on the Digital Training Framework and the learning needs of the supported Professional Groups. Support the organisation of learning events that promote cross-sharing of work-related and functional knowledge. 3. Digital Learning Lead and coordinate digital learning initiatives, including the annual cybersecurity quiz and other digital programmes identified through learning needs analysis. 4. Sponsorships & Talent Acquisition Manage the in-service sponsorship application process. Manage scholarship and professional training programmes, where required, to build a sustainable talent pipeline for specialist groups of doctors and nurses in support of HSA’s current and future manpower needs. 5. Administration & Operations Manage end-to-end administrative matters relating to learning programmes, including facilitating programme registrations, tracking completion of compulsory training, procurement of training service, administering bond and minimum service period requirements, and ensuring the accuracy of learning records and reports. Prepare reports on digital learning participation and support audit matters relating to Learning and Development. Serve as custodian of an HSA corporate credit card, including monthly statement verification. Oversee the procurement of corporate items for new officers, manage LEARN system accounts, and provide operational support for other Learning Partners, as required. 6. Competency & Capability Development Facilitate the review and management of functional competencies and Professional Actualisation Training (PAT), including the identification of critical professional skills, tracking competency gaps, and supporting capability development initiatives. 7. Others Undertake other projects and duties, as assigned.
hrp|17837644|005056a3-d347-1fe1-a091-9d3.requirements: You should be a self-starter who is passionate about people development and helping colleagues to stay relevant in the workplace through constant skills upgrading.

hrp|17837659|005056a3-d347-1fe1-a091-aa4.responsibilities: Procurement Planning and Strategy Lead end-to-end procurement planning and strategy for annual and ad hoc requirements, managing the Division's procurement requests through demand aggregation and appropriate sourcing methods. Develop and implement procurement plans and strategies aligned with organisational priorities, working closely with stakeholders on requirements, timelines, and budgets. Drive strategic sourcing initiatives, contract renewal planning, and pipeline management whilst ensuring compliance with policies and regulatory frameworks. Monitor procurement progress and resolve issues to ensure the timely delivery of goods, services, and works. Sourcing and Procurement Management Oversee end-to-end sourcing activities, including ITQs, tenders, and quotations, ensuring procurement exercises are conducted in accordance with policies and governance requirements. Lead and manage complex or high-value procurement and tender exercises. Contract Management Oversee contract administration, performance monitoring, renewals, variations, and dispute resolution. Manage supplier performance and ensure suppliers meet their contractual obligations. Ensure compliance with procurement policies and governance requirements, and keep abreast of changes to Government procurement policies, the Instruction Manual (IM) on procurement, and internal NLB processes and guidelines. Stakeholder Management Partner with divisions to understand business needs and provide procurement advice. Provide guidance to users and/or team members on requirement specifications, evaluation reports, and other procurement-related reviews. Build and sustain strong relationships with internal stakeholders and external suppliers to achieve successful procurement outcomes. Team Leadership Lead, mentor, and develop the procurement team, fostering positive culture grounded in integrity and continuous learning. Allocate resources effectively, monitor workload distribution, and foster capability development within the team. Process Improvement Support organisational change initiatives and drive continuous improvement across the procurement function. Identify and implement emerging technologies to improve operational and procurement efficiency. Financial Management Oversee the monitoring of procurement expenditure and support budget planning and fund management to ensure accountability.
hrp|17837659|005056a3-d347-1fe1-a091-aa4.requirements: 5 to 8 years of procurement experience, including a minimum of 2 to 5 years in public sector procurement and at least 3 years in a supervisory position. Demonstrated experience in managing end-to-end procurement, including strategic sourcing, tendering, supplier relationship management, and contract award and management Expertise in tender evaluation and contract negotiations, with strong knowledge of procurement governance, policies, regulatory requirements, and the Government IM. Proven leadership and people management skills, with the ability to lead and develop procurement teams. Proven ability to drive process improvements and procurement transformation initiatives. Excellent stakeholder management, influencing, and communication skills to collaborate effectively across all levels of the organisation. Strong analytical, meticulous, problem-solving, and decision-making abilities. A firm commitment to maintaining the highest standards of integrity, professionalism, and accountability in managing public resources and procurement activities. Work location will be at the Marine Parade Library. As the library is currently closed for renovation, the current work location is at the National Library Building. Successful applicant will be appointed on an initial two-year contract.
hrp|17837659|005056a3-d347-1fe1-a091-aa4.description: The National Library Board (NLB) nurtures Readers for Life, Learning Communities and a Knowledgeable Nation by promoting reading, learning and history through our network of 28 libraries across Singapore, the National Library and the National Archives of Singapore. At NLB, you can look forward to a flexible, hybrid work environment with rewarding, impactful deliverables that improve the lives of the community. With caring colleagues, you will be in an ideal environment for professional development, innovation and impact. We can offer you: • A chance to Impact the Community, bridge gaps and empower everyone with the opportunity for learning and discovery. • An opportunity to Innovate and Push Boundaries. We value ideas, curiosity and a passion for innovation to transform our libraries and archives. • An organisation that Cares for your Growth and Wellbeing through investment in staff development and wellbeing in a supportive and collaborative environment. This Senior Manager/ Manager, supports the Department Head and is accountable for leading the procurement function within Marketing and Corporate Solutions division. His/Her key responsibilities include overseeing procurement planning, sourcing, tender and contract management, and ensuring compliance with procurement policies and governance requirements. The role also drives process improvement, provides strategic procurement advice to stakeholders, develops and supervises the procurement team. Additionally, it involves monitoring procurement performance and budgets, with the aim of delivering transparent, efficient, and value-for-money procurement outcomes that support the organisation's objectives.

hrp|17840654|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a09e-a8c.responsibilities: NMO is looking for a dynamic and collaborative officer to lead product operations, drive user adoption, and support the continuous enhancement of the government martech platform. This role sits at the intersection of marcom governance, martech system operations, stakeholder engagement and data-driven decision-making. The officer will work closely with government agencies, internal stakeholders and industry partners to ensure that the platform is able to deliver meaningful value to users and strengthen campaign planning, reporting and performance measurement across government. Key Responsibilities Proliferate Marcom Best Practices Drive the adoption of data-driven marcom planning across the WoG through: • Developing and delivering user communications, training materials, webinars and training sessions • Engaging marcom officers across WoG to understand their operational pain points, challenges adopting best practices, and/or desired support from central, analysing feedback and improving proliferation strategy Lead Product Operations for Government MarTech Platform Contribute to the success of NMO’s government martech platform product team by: • Driving user adoption through planning and execution of go-to-market strategy (e.g. user training, development of self-help materials, etc.) • Developing and operationalising product operations procedures (e.g. escalation, etc.) to handle user feedback and manage incidents • Regularly analysing user feedback over time and using insights to advise the platform product development team on future product improvements and feature prioritisation. • Developing and operating, with the support of product engineers where needed, the required monitoring of product data quality, utilisation, and other key metrics as may be deemed necessary to support early identification of product issues or failures for prompt remedial action • Overseeing and managing data ecosystem supporting the continued operation of the government martech platform including vendors, government marcom teams, government statistics and research units, and any other data providers as may be brought in over time to support the development of more sophisticated martech capabilities. This responsibility includes: o Monitor data quality of externally provided data to ensure completeness, timeliness, and accuracy o Undertake the necessary activities to rectify issues identified (e.g. engagement with data provider, contract administration, etc.) o Plan and execute procurement of new data, where necessary
hrp|17840654|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a09e-a8c.requirements: • Background in Business, Marketing, Communications or related disciplines. • At least 5 years' experience in marketing communications, campaign planning, stakeholder engagement, programme management, policy implementation or related functions in the public or private sector. • Good understanding of marketing communications planning, measurement and industry developments. • Experience engaging and coordinating multiple stakeholders across organisations and disciplines. • Experience with martech, marketing analytics or marketing innovation would be a strong plus. • Experience and ability to perform data analytics and use common dashboarding tools (e.g. PowerBI, Databricks, etc.) would be a strong plus. • Good analytical and critical thinking skills • Strong interpersonal skills in building effective intra- and inter-organisational connections and networks • Strong verbal and written communication skills, and ability to multi-task with good project management skills Please note that only shortlisted candidates would be notified. For more information on careers in MDDI, please access the link (https://www.mddi.gov.sg/join-us/careers/life-at-mddi/). For more information on our job vacancies, please access Careers@Gov (https://www.careers.gov.sg/) and search for “MDDI” in the Search bar.
hrp|17840654|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a09e-a8c.description: The National Marketing Office (NMO) at MDDI has two broad remits: a) Strengthen government marketing communication (marcom) campaign efficiency and effectiveness, by developing and proliferating marcom best practices across government agency communications teams, developing and operationalising marcom governance frameworks and initiatives, and facilitating the coordination of marcom efforts across the whole of Government (WoG); and b) Support the delivery of a unified SG nation brand to enhance Singapore’s perception and favourability, through strategic thrusts such as Brand Adoption, Brand Governance and Brand Advocacy. In order to deliver these outcomes, NMO also develops and operates a government martech platform, which aims to enhance marcom campaign planning and execution across the WoG.

hrp|17842856|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a0aa-9fa.responsibilities: Lead the end-to-end delivery of software and digital platform projects, ensuring successful outcomes within agreed scope, budget, quality and schedule. Own and drive Agile software delivery processes across the project lifecycle. Serve as Scrum Master and delivery lead where required, organising, facilitating and ensuring the effectiveness of all Scrum ceremonies, including sprint planning, backlog refinement, daily stand-ups, sprint reviews and retrospectives. Work closely with Product Owners and stakeholders to define, refine and prioritise epics, features and user stories, ensuring development teams have a clear and actionable backlog. Track sprint goals, team velocity, burn-down metrics, dependencies and delivery risks, taking proactive actions to maintain delivery momentum and predictability. Remove impediments and facilitate resolution of issues that may impact software delivery. Serve as the primary interface between business stakeholders, product owners, vendors and software engineering teams. Translate business requirements into clear technical deliverables and work packages for engineering teams. Work closely with software architects and engineers to evaluate solution designs, implementation approaches, technical risks and trade-offs. Coordinate internal and external engineering resources to ensure effective delivery and resource utilisation. Monitor project health, identify risks and dependencies, and drive timely mitigation and resolution. Manage stakeholder communications and provide regular updates on project status, key decisions, risks and milestones. Oversee project governance, documentation, procurement activities and vendor performance where applicable. Ensure software solutions comply with cybersecurity, architecture, operational and organisational requirements. Foster collaboration between multidisciplinary teams including software engineers, infrastructure engineers, cybersecurity specialists, data professionals and business users. Support tender and procurement activities, including requirements definition, technical evaluations and vendor engagements.
hrp|17842856|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a0aa-9fa.requirements: Degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering or equivalent. Minimum 7 years of relevant experience in software delivery, digital transformation, product delivery or technology programme management. Proven track record of leading software development projects from concept through delivery and operations. Strong understanding of software development lifecycle (SDLC), Agile methodologies and modern engineering practices. Demonstrated experience leading Agile software delivery teams using Scrum methodologies. Proven experience facilitating sprint planning, backlog grooming, daily stand-ups, sprint reviews and retrospectives. Strong understanding of Agile metrics such as velocity, burn-down charts, cycle time and release planning. Able to engage confidently with software engineers, solution architects and technical specialists on system design, architecture, integration and delivery considerations. Experience managing vendors, system integrators and multidisciplinary project teams. Familiarity with cloud platforms, APIs, enterprise software systems and modern application architectures. Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to engage both technical and non-technical audiences. Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities, resolve issues and drive delivery in complex project environments. Team player with strong people management, facilitation and conflict resolution skills. Ideal Candidate Profile: The successful candidate is not expected to write code, but should possess sufficient software engineering knowledge and delivery experience to challenge assumptions and proposals from vendors and engineering teams. Understand software architecture and engineering trade-offs. Facilitate productive discussions between business and technical stakeholders. Drive Agile software delivery and project governance. Make informed decisions on delivery risks, timelines and dependencies.
hrp|17842856|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a0aa-9fa.description: Ground-breaking projects, such as Punggol Digital District, one-north, Jurong Island, Jurong Rock Cavern and Seletar Aerospace are evidence of the innovative and dynamic side of JTC. Hardly surprising, because at JTC, our mission is to conceive visionary developments in key industrial sectors to create national economic growth for the future. If you want to know how we break new ground and turn vision into reality, visit us at www.jtc.gov.sg.

hrp|17842879|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a0aa-a0c.responsibilities: You will be responsible for the following: Manage and administer the procurement of services and goods and pre and post contract management. Carry out user needs analysis, draft and prepare tender and contract documents, including requirement specifications. Carry out market surveys on services or products that are currently used in the industry. Review and vet tender and contract documents to ensure compliance with Public Sector Standards Conditions of Contract (PSSCOC), government tender procedures and that operational requirements are met before calling and awarding of tenders. Monitors and put in place controls to ensure all procurement processes by internal stakeholders comply with established procurement policies, procedures, and guidelines. Carry out evaluation and prepare recommendation reports of submitted tender bids. Tracks, checks and processes contract variations, exercising of options for contracts under the department. Assists in pre and post contract management such as submission of security deposit, insurances, drawings, plans, warranties, operations & maintenance manuals, and all other documents required under the contracts. Carry out performance review of IFM Contractors for recommendation of payment. Oversees and handle FM and construction-related projects, from project inception to project completion. Provide advisory on contractual matters to other department users tapping on FMED’s contract. Any other tasks assigned by Supervisor.
hrp|17842879|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a0aa-a0c.requirements: Minimum 2 years of experience in procurement and contractual management. Knowledge and experience in government procurement policies (IM, PSSCOC and all other relevant published standards) would be advantageous. Background in Building / Facilities Management, Civil/M&E Engineering, Construction Project Management or Quantity Surveying would be useful. Familiar with local Codes of Practices, statutory authorities’ requirements, and FM operational practices would be useful. Conversant in technical specifications writing. Basic computer skills such as Excel and PowerPoint etc. and able to read and interpret building and M&E drawings/plans. Self-motivated and comfortable with fast-paced environment. Able to work independently with good time management and able to multi-task. Excellent communication and analytical skills with problem solving attitude. Able and willing to work occasionally after office hours, including weekends and Public Holidays. As part of the shortlisting process for this role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment.
hrp|17842879|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a0aa-a0c.description: As an Assistant Manager / Manager in the Business Infrastructure Branch (BIB) of the Facilities Management & Engineering Department (FMED), you will handle and oversee the procurement and management of Facilities Management (FM) and construction-related contracts.

hrp|17844018|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a38e-802.responsibilities: Successful applicant will play an active role in supporting the planning, coordination and management of the organisation’s office and estate operations to ensure that the organisation's facilities, infrastructure and workplace services are safe, reliable and operationally ready. The key responsibilities include: • Planning, monitoring and reviewing preventive and corrective maintenance programmes, including the assessment of work orders, maintenance requests and defect rectification. • Monitoring the condition and performance of building assets, identifying recurring issues, and recommending solutions which include appropriate repair, replacement or improvement works. • Conducting regular inspections and review of maintenance performance to ensure compliance with contractual requirements, statutory regulations and organisational standards. • Coordinating with contractors, consultants and stakeholders to resolve operational issues and ensure timely completion of maintenance works. • Maintaining building records, technical documentation and maintenance information to support effective facilities and asset management. • Administering assigned facilities management contracts and monitoring contractor performance to ensure compliance with contractual obligations, Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and Service Level Agreements (SLAs). • Supporting procurement activities including the preparation of specifications, quotations, tenders, contract variations, extensions and waiver submissions. • Reviewing completed works, verifying service delivery and recommending Certification of Payment (COP) in accordance with contractual requirements. • Managing workplace operations and shared facilities to support the organisation's daily business and examination operations. • Administering the Resource Booking System (RBS) and coordinating room bookings, venue setup and facilities support to ensure the operational readiness of meeting, event and examination venues.
hrp|17844018|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a38e-802.requirements: • Professional Qualification in Facilities Management, Building Services, Estate Management, Engineering, Business Management or related discipline, with at least 2 years of relevant experience is preferred. • Experience in the public sector and familiarity with the Government procurement and contract administration process, workplace operations, project management would be an advantage. • Possess strong analytical, problem-solving, planning and organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver results in a dynamic environment. • Possess good communication, interpersonal and stakeholder management skills, with a proactive, resourceful and customer-centric approach to service delivery.

hrp|17846671|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a79a-915.responsibilities: You will be responsible for the following: Oversee the daily operations of the facility and installations, including building systems and services, landscaping, pest control, and conservancy. Ensure the proper functioning of all Mechanical & Electrical (M&E) systems, including plumbing, Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC), lighting, and fire protection systems. Carry out daily site inspections across the facilities to monitor cleanliness, maintenance standards, and overall site conditions, and follow up promptly on any defects/gaps identified. Supervise a team of facilities, landscaping, pest control, conservancy and other outsourced contractors to ensure works are carried out satisfactorily in accordance with contract requirements. Plan and coordinate preventive and corrective maintenance works in accordance with contract requirements. Monitor maintenance schedules and ensure timely completion of all works. Plan and carry out procurement of office equipment, supplies, stationery, and other operational items. Perform administrative duties, including processing invoices for payment, managing copier rental contracts, tracking paper usage, and coordinating the provision of uniforms. Handle and manage feedback, including investigation and follow-up actions. Ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and maintain safety standards within the facilities. Respond to and investigate any building-related incidents and coordinate with relevant authorities and internal stakeholders, including after office hours. Participate in major events such as Qing Ming Festivals, scheduled fire emergency exercises, annual shutdown servicing and any other organisational level events, including on weekends and Public Holidays. Perform any other duties as assigned by the supervisor.

Proficient in Microsoft Office Applications. Good problem-solving, writing & communication skills. Mature, tactful, independent, committed and resourceful. Ability to interact and foster teamwork. Willing to work in after-life care service environment. Ability and willing to work on weekends and public holidays.

hrp|17853016|005056a3-d347-1fe1-a180-0b5.responsibilities: The jobholder is responsible for the Governance, Risk, audit and process management of enterprise ICT infrastructure services systems (such as end-user devices, virtualised infrastructure, active directory, network, serve, etc.) that are across all MHA Home Team Departments (HTDs). Our shared mission is to amplify, augment and accelerate the Home Team’s advantage and secure Singapore as the safest place on planet earth. You play an important role in the implementation and maintenance of ICT end-user devices, networks and infrastructures for a Home Team Department (e.g. Singapore Police Force, Singapore Civil Defence Force, Singapore Prison Service, Immigration & Checkpoints Authority, etc.), ensuring their operational readiness at all times.

hrp|17881630|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a2b3-72f.responsibilities: - Lead and conduct penetration testing, red teaming, and adversary simulation activities across web, mobile, infrastructure, cloud, OT, and telecommunications environments. - Execute realistic attack scenarios to assess the resilience of Critical Information Infrastructure (CII), including systems supporting essential services. - Support purple-teaming activities by translating offensive techniques into actionable detection and response improvements. - Lead engagements end-to-end, including planning, execution, reporting, and technical debriefs with stakeholders. - Mentor junior consultants and contribute to raising the team’s overall technical standard. - Drive continuous improvement of ASG’s testing methodologies, tooling, and research, including taking on problem spaces outside your primary domain when required. - And because this is government, be prepared to occasionally switch gears by contributing to strategic initiatives, supporting and executing procurement activities, participating in industry outreach, or undertaking coordination work, all of which ultimately help us strengthen security outcomes and make Singapore a safer place to live and work. Why Join ASG at CSA - Work on nationally significant systems, including CII, OT, and telecommunications environments rarely accessible outside government. - Engage in deep, technically challenging work that prioritises realism, learning, and security outcomes over high-volume testing. - Apply your offensive security expertise to a public mission that directly contributes to Singapore’s cyber resilience. - Be part of a specialist team that is deliberately building towards strong technical depth, continuous learning, and moving beyond compliance-driven assurance, and help shape what “good” looks like along the way.
hrp|17881630|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a2b3-72f.requirements: - An attacker’s mindset with strong technical understanding of operating systems, networks, and modern enterprise environments. - Proven ability to identify and execute real-world attack scenarios, beyond automated or checklist-based testing. - Experience in penetration testing and/or red team operations, with exposure to adversary tradecraft and attack chaining. - Demonstrated adaptability to transfer skills across technical domains (e.g. web to mobile, IT to OT, on-prem to cloud). - Strong technical writing skills and the ability to clearly articulate security risks and impact. - Typically 5–8 years of relevant experience in penetration testing, red team operations, or related offensive security roles, with demonstrated depth in hands-on technical work. - Relevant industry certifications such as OSCP, CREST (e.g. CRT, CCT), CRTO, or equivalent are desirable. - That said, we recognise that certifications alone do not define capability. Hands-on experience, problem-solving ability, and technical depth matter more to us than badges.
hrp|17881630|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a2b3-72f.description: You will be part of the Attack Simulation Group (ASG) within the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA), a specialist team responsible for delivering advanced security testing and adversary-led assessments to strengthen the resilience of Critical Information Infrastructure (CII). This is a senior, hands-on role for experienced offensive security practitioners who want to apply real-world attack techniques to complex, high-impact systems in support of Singapore’s national cyber security mission. ASG is a technically driven team within CSA focused on realistic attack simulation, penetration testing, red teaming, and purple-teaming outcomes. Our work goes beyond compliance-driven assurance, emphasising hands-on testing, attacker tradecraft, and practical security improvements. Operating within the realities of government, we value curiosity, adaptability, and out-of-the-box thinking. Specialised training and development opportunities are provided to continuously deepen and expand our technical capabilities, and team members are expected to continuously learn, apply skills across domains, and contribute to the evolution of attack simulation practices across Singapore’s CII. We also believe in sharing and growing our craft where appropriate. Some of our public work and tooling can be found at: 👉 https://github.com/hack-techv2/

hrp|17889767|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a2e4-229.responsibilities: Jobscope • The jobholder primarily supports the CNB Feedback Unit in the area of Feedback Management and reports to the Senior Manager/Assistant Director (Media and Info Planning). The jobholder manages and provides timely resolution to enquiries, requests, feedback and appeals from the public on CNB and/or drug-related information. He/she will work with relevant internal stakeholders, and with external stakeholders if necessary, to ensure timely responses to public feedback. • He/she will also support the Public Communications Unit and Communications Division in the areas of media (daily media monitoring, media publicity), corporate communications (content creation, publications), administrative and logistical support (including procurement, inventory management, visitor management, secretariat/coordination work). He/she may be called upon to support the Communications Division in event management. Responsibilities: Feedback management (primary responsibility) • Manage public feedback via e-services feedback form and correspondence (email, letter). • Handle feedback in a timely manner, and with professionalism, courtesy, efficiency, effectiveness and empathy, according to service standards. • Maintain and update public feedback received into a customer-relationship management system (CRMS) for case-assignment, case-management and records/knowledge management. The CRMS will be used to track and follow-up on each interaction and resolution. • Work with internal stakeholders, and with external stakeholders if necessary, and ensure that the responses to public feedback are robust, relevant, and timely. Monitor and follow up with internal stakeholders on outstanding feedback issues, ensuring proper closure and reply are provided to feedback providers within the stipulated response time. • Draft formal replies as necessary, and manage the escalation of cases as necessary to supervisors and CNB Quality Service Manager. • Analyse feedback statistics and prepare regular statistical reports for Senior Management, and other ad-hoc reports and analysis as required. • Undertake a proactive role in providing operational insights to identify improvements to policies and processes. • Serve as a resource-person for internal stakeholders on service-quality management, and maintain positive working relationship with internal and external stakeholders. Media and corporate communications • Media monitoring and analysis: On a daily basis (weekdays), assist to read and summarise news as assigned, collate inputs from fellow team members and prepare a daily (weekdays) broadcast of news of interest to CNB officers and management. • Media comms support: To support and augment the Public Communications team in the organising of press conferences and media visits, and assist to disseminate approved news releases (including uploading onto the CNB website, and via internal broadcasts) in a timely manner. • Corporate communications and website management: The officer may be called upon to assist the Public Communications team with content creation, simple design work and publications (for both external and internal communications) and to support website management (including enhancements and content migration). Administrative and logistical support • Resource planning and procurement: To support the operational needs of the Public Communications team, the officer will be involved in budget planning and resource planning. The officer will assist in the procurement of goods, services, equipment required for media content and operations. • Management of fixed assets and inventory: To provide administrative and logistical support in the management of corporate gift inventory, fixed assets and publicity collaterals. • Secretariat support, event support and welfare management: The jobholder may be called upon to support the Communications Division in secretariat support for meetings (e.g. visitor management), and in the running of public events (e.g. annual DrugFreeSG Light-Up, book launch, appreciation events). He/she will work with team members to coordinate welfare activities for the Communications Division. Other responsibilities • Perform any other duties that may be assigned from time to time by supervisor.

hrp|17896196|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a6cf-2dc.responsibilities: Key responsibilities include: Engage internal and external stakeholders to gather requirements, clarify constraints (e.g. security, networking, availability, cloud technology limitations), and translate needs into actionable technical work packages. Support the definition of cloud platform and environment architecture, including landing zones, network segmentation, identity, compute, and storage, and contribute to technical specifications and implementation plans. Lead or participate in technical engagements with Cloud Service Providers (CSPs), GovTech, and appointed contractors to shape the target cloud environment approach on GCC, including account or subscription structure, IAM, networking, and baseline security controls. Review vendor sizing and service selections, including virtual machines, containers, and managed services, to assess whether they meet performance, reliability, scalability, and cost objectives. Support the definition of Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) and configuration management standards, such as Terraform/Ansible patterns, module reuse, and review controls, and assess vendor deliverables against these standards. Support the definition of deployment and release management expectations, including CI/CD controls, quality gates, and rollback strategies, and review vendor pipeline designs and implementation evidence. Contribute to DevSecOps and security-by-design requirements, such as scanning, secrets management, and policy-as-code where applicable, and verify contractor compliance through reviews, testing evidence, and audit artefacts. Support the definition of observability and operational readiness requirements, including logging, monitoring, alerting, SLO/SLA, and runbooks, and review vendor proposals, test results, and readiness or handover evidence. Support the development of integration approaches between systems, applications, and databases using APIs, middleware, and event-driven patterns where applicable. Support issue resolution through root-cause analysis (RCA) and track corrective and preventive actions to closure. Support the definition and governance of integration testing and acceptance criteria, including test plans, environment readiness, and defect triage, and validate that contractor evidence meets the required outcomes. Support project governance activities with project managers, including inputs for procurement, technical evaluations, design/specification approvals, and stakeholder coordination. Contribute to project delivery by tracking technical deliverables, dependencies, risks, and timelines, and support delivery in line with approved plans and budgets. Identify technical and integration risks, assess their impact, and recommend mitigation plans to minimise delays and operational impact. Review, comment on, and maintain key technical documents and vendor submissions, such as system design documents, interface control documents, test plans, and acceptance artefacts, to support procurement, delivery, operations, and audit requirements. Assist in coordinating security reviews and support the closure of findings, including hardening, vulnerability remediation, and security monitoring requirements, in accordance with organisational and regulatory requirements. Engage stakeholders to support proper system integration, testing, and operational readiness for air traffic operations. Provide regular status updates, highlight issues early, and propose resolution options to management.
hrp|17896196|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a6cf-2dc.requirements: Trained in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering (Computing), or equivalent practical experience. Experience in delivering large-scale ICT systems across the project lifecycle, including working with vendors or contractors on design reviews, implementation oversight, testing, acceptance, and operational handover, is preferred. Good understanding of cloud architecture, Linux or system administration, networking (VPC/VNet, routing, DNS, TLS), identity and access management, and cybersecurity; experience with containers and Kubernetes would be advantageous. Preferred technical skills include the following areas, and candidates are not expected to be experts in all areas: cloud fundamentals (compute, storage, networking, IAM, encryption/key management, and backup/disaster recovery); operational readiness (monitoring/alerting, incident and problem management, SLO/SLA, runbooks, and capacity and cost management); automation literacy (Terraform/Ansible concepts and Git-based workflows); container orchestration (Docker and Kubernetes); and CI/CD and DevSecOps concepts (pipeline controls, artifact/version management, security scanning, and secrets handling). Relevant certifications would be advantageous, such as Cloud Solution Architect, SysOps, DevOps Engineer, Kubernetes, security certifications such as CISSP, or project management certifications such as PMP or Agile/Scrum. Self-motivated with a strong sense of ownership, and able to work independently and collaboratively across teams and stakeholders. Strong written and verbal communication, stakeholder management, analytical, presentation, and negotiation skills, with attention to detail. Willingness to travel overseas occasionally. Your appointment designation will commensurate with your relevant work experience. Successful candidates will be offered a 3-year contract in the first instance and may be considered for placement on a permanent tenure or subsequent contract renewal.
hrp|17896196|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a6cf-2dc.description: The Next Generation Programme Office (NGPO) in CAAS is seeking a strong, driven, and dynamic engineer to be part of the Info-Centric Air Traffic Management (iATM) workstream. You will be part of the team overseeing the implementation of Next Generation iATM systems, including (but not limited to) flight plan filing and air traffic flow management. You will play a key role across multiple phases of the project lifecycle, such as approvals, procurement, implementation, testing, maintenance, and system enhancements. Depending on the project phase, you will work with relevant stakeholders to define system architectures, gather requirements, formulate technical specifications, manage procurement processes, and oversee system implementation, commissioning, maintenance, and enhancements in accordance with Singapore Government and applicable international standards (e.g. SG IM8, ICAO). You will also support the implementation of cyber and data security measures and contribute to the safe and efficient management of air traffic in Singapore.

hrp|17926356|005056a3-d347-1fe1-a58e-c9e.description: The Auditor-General's Office (AGO) is an independent organ of state and the national auditor. hrp|17944448|005056a3-d347-1fe1-a691-05c.responsibilities: Strategic Sourcing and Category Management Lead the development and implementation of sourcing strategies for assigned spend categories to achieve value-for-money outcomes, operational efficiencies, and sustainable cost savings. Partner stakeholders to optimise requirements and specifications while leveraging HPB's overall purchasing power. Monitor market conditions, industry trends, and supply risks to ensure continuity of essential services and critical supplies. Drive procurement planning and demand management initiatives to strengthen procurement outcomes. Business Partnering and Stakeholder Engagement Serve as a trusted advisor to stakeholders by providing clear, practical, and consistent procurement guidance throughout the procurement lifecycle. Influence and engage stakeholders to make informed sourcing decisions and adopt best procurement practices. Champion a value-driven procurement culture by repositioning procurement from a reactive function to a strategic business partner. Governance, Risk and Compliance Develop, review, and strengthen procurement policies, frameworks, and governance processes to ensure compliance with Government procurement requirements and organisational policies. Review and assess procurement strategies, evaluation outcomes, and award recommendations before submission for approval. Identify procurement and contract-related risks, establish key risk indicators, and implement appropriate mitigation measures. Ensure transparency, accountability, and good governance across procurement activities. Contract and Supplier Management Foster strategic supplier relationships to obtain market intelligence, industry insights, emerging innovations, and leading practices. Drive supplier performance management and contract governance to maximise contract value and minimise operational risks. Analyse critical contract failure points and implement proactive measures to enhance contract performance and service delivery. Procurement Transformation and Analytics Leverage data analytics and market intelligence to support decision-making, develop sourcing strategies, and maximise return on investment. Identify opportunities to streamline procurement processes, enhance efficiency, and improve user experience through digitalisation and automation. Support procurement transformation initiatives and continuous improvement programmes across the organisation.
hrp|17944448|005056a3-d347-1fe1-a691-05c.requirements: Qualifications and Experience At least 8 years of relevant procurement, purchasing, sourcing, or supply chain management experience, with demonstrated experience in leading strategic procurement initiatives in public sector and/or commercial sector. Professional procurement certification such as CPM, CPSM, MCIPS, or equivalent will be an advantage. Experience in managing eSourcing platforms and digital procurement solutions. Technical Competencies Strong expertise in strategic sourcing, category management, contract management, supplier relationship management, and procurement governance. Advanced knowledge of procurement risk management and supplier evaluation methodologies. Proven ability to develop procurement policies, frameworks, and operating procedures. Leadership and Behavioural Competencies Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the ability to engage effectively across all organisational levels. Excellent verbal and written communication skills. Ability to navigate ambiguity, manage competing priorities, and deliver results in a fast-paced environment. Strategic thinker with strong commercial acumen and sound judgement. Proactive, resilient, and results-oriented with a passion for driving procurement excellence and organisational value. Key Success Factors The successful candidate will be a strategic procurement leader who can balance governance with business needs, influence stakeholders effectively, leverage data-driven insights, and drive procurement transformation while delivering measurable value to the organisation. Strong analytical and data interpretation skills with the ability to translate insights into actionable procurement strategies. Good knowledge of Government Procurement Instructions Manual (GPIM), GeBIZ, and related procurement systems will be advantageous. Successful candidates will be offered a 2-year contract in the first instance.

The incumbent will lead the development and execution of procurement strategies that deliver value, strengthen governance, optimise spending, mitigate risks, and ensure business continuity. As a key member of the Procurement team, you will provide leadership and direction in: • Strategic sourcing and category management • Procurement policy, governance and compliance • Contract and supplier relationship management • Stakeholder engagement and business partnering • Procurement transformation and digitalisation • Procurement operations and continuous improvement The role requires strong analytical capabilities, sound judgement, stakeholder influence, and the ability to translate business needs into effective procurement solutions that support organisational objectives.

hrp|17946248|005056a3-d347-1fe1-a5f6-c49.responsibilities: The RO is responsible for the regulatory work for the ME regime, especially the impending Category 3 (“Open Concept”) ME licences. This new licence category will be introduced in the second half of 2026. The Police’s intent in regulating MEs is to support the Police’s mission to ensure that MEs are not operated for vice and/or cause social disamenities As an RO, your role covers the full range of regulatory work: from receiving a licence application, to assessing whether the application should be approved or rejected. You will also work closely with the Police land divisions and agencies such as the URA and HDB, in making your assessment, such as by seeking frontline inputs and considering land use approval. When a licensee fails to comply with the licence conditions or commits a breach, you will be responsible for preparing and issuing the composition notice, assessing and deciding whether the licence should be revoked or not renewed. Daily you will also handle service requests, appeals and feedback from the licensees and general public. Other duties include: • Policy and trend analysis - analysing licensing patterns, identifying emerging challenges and drafting data-driven policies and recommendations for legislative changes to ensure the regime is robust. • Industry engagement - planning and conducting regular, structured engagement sessions with licensees, producing advisories and briefings, and maintaining structured and regular dialogue channels with the ME sector. • Coordination of outsourced compliance checks - managing the end-to-end procurement, supervision and quality-assurance of contracted compliance staff, developing frameworks, monitoring KPIs and delivering training. • Technology utilisation - applying AI, RPA and data-analytics tools in day-to-day work and ensuring data integrity and governance of the PLUS2 system. • Handling PRD Counter duties – attending to walk-in members of public who require assistance or have appointments with PRD officers.

Short-listed candidates will be contacted within two weeks of the application closing date.

You are expected to manage complex environments involving enterprise network technologies, large-scale endpoint services, Active Directory/Azure AD, shared storage and backup management, and Hybrid Cloud networks.

hrp|17975053|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a7e6-012.responsibilities: As Deputy/Assistant Manager, Bus Procurement , you will play a key role in shaping Singapore's next-generation public bus fleet. By 2030, we will be replacing half of our 6,000-strong bus fleet with cutting-edge electric vehicles, and this role will place you at the forefront of this historic transition. Working at the intersection of engineering, policy, and sustainability, you will support strategic bus procurement initiatives that directly influence fleet performance, passenger experience, and long-term asset resilience. Your work will take you beyond Singapore's borders as you scout emerging technologies and collaborate with global manufacturers to bring the most advanced solutions to our streets. You'll witness firsthand the latest innovations in electric propulsion, autonomous systems, and smart connectivity as you help modernise a fleet that's not just safe and reliable, but also future-ready. You will support diverse and impactful responsibilities encompassing comprehensive end-to-end bus procurement and strategic asset management, including: Support Fleet Renewal and Replacement : Assist in developing and executing strategies to renew and replace fleet to meet operational, safety, and sustainability objectives across the public bus network. Tender Specifications & Evaluation : Support the drafting of new bus requirements, preparation of tender specifications, and evaluation of submissions to ensure the best value for the fleet. Quality Assurance : Conduct pre-delivery inspections and testing of bus equipment to ensure they comply with contract specifications and operational standards. Partnership Management : Build and nurture strong relationships with overseas bus manufacturers and suppliers, staying informed on industry innovations and product developments. Market Research & Design Specifications : Conduct in-depth research into emerging bus technologies and trends, making recommendations for design requirements to inform design improvements and future tender specifications. P rocurement Budget : Support cost-effective purchasing while maintaining high standards of quality, all within the boundaries of the procurement budget. Your work will directly support the advancement of Singapore's public bus fleet, enhance operational excellence and sustainability outcomes, and contribute to maintaining Singapore's position as a global leader in innovative and future-ready public transport solutions.

The ideal candidate will possess: Educational Background : Knowledge in Engineering (Electrical, Electrical & Electronic, Mechanical, Automotive or equivalent). Experience : At least 4 years of relevant experience in automotive, engineering, or related industries. Familiarity with battery systems, servicing, and maintenance of buses will be advantageous. Fresh graduates are welcome to apply. Skills : Strong analytical, planning, and problem-solving abilities with attention to detail. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, alongside proficiency in IT. Attributes : A proactive, self-motivated individual with the ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities effectively. As part of the shortlisting process for the role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and / or undergo further assessment.

hrp|17982583|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a88f-98c.responsibilities: This role is centred on the CBRNE Specialised Lab, with the majority of your work involving hands-on analytical functions, sample management, laboratory administration and quality system. Key responsibilities include: • Conduct laboratory analysis and support field-based studies on technologies related to CBRNE preparedness, detection, and decontamination, including the development of new detection chemistries and next-generation sensing technologies. • Perform routine analysis of chemical and biological samples in a specialised laboratory setting, including ad-hoc screening and verification of samples in accordance with established SOPs. • Perform method development, method validation, and troubleshooting on analytical instruments including GC-MS/MS and LC-MS/MS. hrp|17982583|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a88f-98c.description: HTX is Singapore's Science and Technology agency that brings together diverse scientific and engineering capabilities to develop transformative, operationally ready solutions for public safety. As a statutory board under the Ministry of Home Affairs, HTX works at the forefront of science and technology to empower the Home Team with cutting-edge capabilities. Guided by our mission to amplify, augment and accelerate the Home Team's advantage, we are committed to keeping Singapore the safest place on planet Earth. The CBRNE Centre of Expertise (CoE) at the Home Team Science and Technology Agency (HTX) is at the forefront of developing and enhancing Singapore's capabilities to detect, protect against, and respond to Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear, and Explosives (CBRNE) threats. Our work supports the Home Team in safeguarding public safety and national security through cutting-edge science and technology. We are seeking a motivated and technically skilled scientist to join our Specialised laboratory team based in Tuas Checkpoint. This is primarily a hands-on, lab-based role where you will be responsible for the day-to-day running of analytical operations, ensuring that laboratory functions are maintained to the highest standards of accuracy, safety, and compliance. You will also contribute all aspect contributing to the operation of the lab such as method development, evaluation of CBRNE-related technologies, working closely with Home Team agencies and industry partners in support of Singapore's security needs.

Depending on the candidates’ experience, the role may also involves developing strategies and operational plans, driving validation exercises and readiness programmes to strengthen HDB's preparedness for emergencies. hrp|18061136|005056a3-53e2-1fd1-aca8-66b.responsibilities: A. Procurement Management Manage and support end-to-end procurement activities, from procurement planning and sourcing through evaluation, award and contract administration. Review procurement requirements and documentation, and advise stakeholders on appropriate sourcing approaches, evaluation methods and procurement strategies. Manage procurement timelines and ensure procurement exercises are conducted fairly, transparently and in accordance with prevailing policies and procedures. B. Procurement Advisory Provide practical and professional procurement advice to stakeholders across the Group, translating policies and requirements into appropriate procurement solutions. Review and constructively challenge procurement proposals, requirements and approaches to achieve sound procurement outcomes and value for money. Advise stakeholders on procurement risks, controls and alternatives, and escalate significant or exceptional matters to Head (Procurement) where appropriate. C. Governance, Compliance & Risk Management Ensure procurement activities comply with prevailing Government Procurement IM policies, internal procedures, approval requirements and governance controls. Maintain proper procurement documentation and audit trails, and support internal and external audits and reviews. Identify procurement and compliance risks, recommend appropriate controls, and keep abreast of changes in Government Procurement IM policies and good practices. D. Contract Management Monitor contract utilisation, key milestones, expiry dates and upcoming procurement or renewal requirements for assigned units. Support contract administration, including monitoring contractual obligations, expenditure, variations, extensions and other contract-related matters. Maintain appropriate contract records and work with stakeholders to identify and address contract management issues in a timely manner. E. Process Improvement & Digitalisation Maintain procurement trackers, databases and dashboards, and generate procurement reports, statistics and management information. Monitor and analyse procurement patterns and transactional metrics, including procurement volumes and processing timelines, to support planning and decision-making. Review and improve procurement processes, SOPs, templates and guidance, and leverage technology and digital solutions to strengthen efficiency, consistency and governance. F. Capability Development & Team Contribution Share procurement knowledge and good practices, contribute to procurement training and capability-building initiatives. Guide colleagues and stakeholders on procurement processes and, where applicable, coach junior officers in professional procurement practices. Contribute to building a collaborative, service-oriented and professional procurement culture across the Group.

Candidates with other qualifications and relevant experience may also be considered. Preferably at least 3 years of relevant procurement experience, with hands-on exposure to end-to-end procurement activities. Candidates with less experience but strong relevant capabilities may also be considered. Experience in Singapore public sector procurement and familiarity with Government Procurement IM policies would be a strong advantage. Familiarity with procurement and enterprise systems such as GeBIZ and Workday would be advantageous. Experience in procurement governance, stakeholder advisory, contract management and procurement reporting and analytics would be advantageous. Digitally proficient, with working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications and a willingness to adopt data, digital and AI tools to improve productivity and procurement processes. The candidate should possess good procurement knowledge and judgement, with strong analytical, critical thinking and problem-solving skills. Resourceful, meticulous, proactive and results-oriented, the candidate should be able to work independently on assigned procurement matters , and take ownership of their work, and demonstrate excellent written, verbal and interpersonal skills. A collaborative team player with a continuous improvement mindset is essential. Successful candidate will be appointed on a contract basis. In general, applicants can expect to hear from us within 4 weeks of the close of the application window. In the event where we receive a high number of applications, applicants will receive an update on their status within 6 weeks of the close of the application window. hrp|18062946|005056a3-d347-1fe1-acb5-c70.responsibilities: • Operational Needs Assessment: The officer engages CPIB officers to conduct process mapping and requirements gathering, developing a thorough understanding of existing workflows, activities, and pain points. Findings are synthesised into clear operational needs and recommendations, identifying opportunities for tool acquisition, process improvement, or in-house capability development. • Business Process Re-engineering: The officer translates operational needs and pain points into clear, actionable proposals for process improvement. This includes leading or supporting business process re-engineering (BPR) initiatives to redesign and streamline workflows, working closely with relevant work units and stakeholders to ensure that redesigned processes are practical and effectively implemented. • Horizon Scanning and Capability Evaluation: The officer proactively monitors emerging trends, technologies, and developments — including AI and automation — that could meaningfully address operational needs or unlock new capabilities for the department. The officer supports the evaluation and procurement of shortlisted tools and products by providing well-researched analysis of their operational relevance and value and contributes to capability development decisions. The officer also helps establish metrics and evaluation frameworks to assess the effectiveness of acquired tools and technologies. • External Engagement and Partnership: The officer is expected to forge and deepen relationships with strategic inter-agency partners and external stakeholders to facilitate the exchange of insights on capability development and emerging technologies. This includes representing the branch at relevant industry events, briefings, and inter-agency engagements, and providing timely updates on relevant developments and opportunities.
hrp|18062946|005056a3-d347-1fe1-acb5-c70.requirements: • Candidates should have between three and six years of relevant working experience in capabilities development in an enforcement-related field. • The candidate should have the ability to synthesise complex information from multiple sources and translate findings into clear problem statements, insights, and recommendations. • Basic project management and strong requirement gathering skills are required to manage multiple workstreams, prioritise effectively, and deliver outcomes in a dynamic environment. • The candidate must be able to work independently, exercising sound judgement and taking initiative to drive work forward with minimal supervision. • Excellent written and verbal communication skills are needed to engage effectively with officers, senior management, and external partners. • Experience in business process re-engineering, technology evaluation, or procurement in a government context would be advantageous. • Singaporean
hrp|18062946|005056a3-d347-1fe1-acb5-c70.description: The Corrupt Practices Investigation Bureau (CPIB) is a Government agency under the Prime Minister’s Office. Responsible for the investigation and prevention of corruption in Singapore, CPIB strives to keep Singapore corruption-free by combatting corruption through swift and sure, firm but fair action. The officer supports the Assistant Director (Intel Operations Capabilities Development) in developing, strengthening and future-proofing the operational capabilities of CPIB. The role contributes directly to this mission by conducting ground-level engagement with officers to surface operational pain points, mapping existing workflows, and identifying opportunities for improvement. The officer also plays an active role in horizon scanning and engagement with strategic partners, ensuring that the branch maintains a current and informed view of emerging tools, technologies, and capabilities that could enhance CPIB's operational effectiveness.

hrp|18064485|005056a3-d347-1fe1-acc1-898.description: JTC's Digital Transformation Division drives the digitalisation of business operations, enabling smarter planning, development, estate management, and enterprise services through technology, data, and digital innovation. You will work closely with business stakeholders, users, architects, engineers, and vendors to define product priorities, deliver enhancements, and ensure solutions continue to create value for users and the organisation. In addition to product ownership responsibilities, the role will oversee vendor delivery, project coordination, and contract administration for assigned products and platforms.

The successful job holder will join a team of procurement professionals at HTX Central Procurement Office (CPO) which is responsible for the procurement of a wide range of goods and services for all MHA Home Team Departments (HTDs) and HTX requirements.

hrp|18070169|005056a3-d347-1fe1-ace7-d0a.responsibilities: • Lead three teams of officers in MFA’s Business Support Centre (BSC) to provide a seamless, one-stop traveller assistance service for officers on official trips, or who are going on or returning from their overseas postings. • Develop the BSC team’s expertise, experience, and service-oriented culture in managing officers’ and overseas participants’ travels, including foreign guests on exchange and training programmes. • Supervise the procurement of travel, shipment, medical, liaison, transport, and insurance services, and oversee vendors to ensure high standards of service delivery. • Formulate and review policies and enhance processes and systems to support the BSC’s operations. • Ensure that the systems used by the BSC to deliver services and manage data are fit-for-purpose and future-ready, and that officers are trained to use them effectively. • Develop officers’ competencies in operations (e.g., travel and logistics planning and operations), administration (e.g., budgeting and procurement), and ops-policy integration to effectively meet current and future needs.
hrp|18070169|005056a3-d347-1fe1-ace7-d0a.requirements: To meet the challenges of this role, you must be a Singaporean and have: • A good tertiary qualification, preferably in Business Administration/Management, with three to six years’ related experience in a managerial role. • Experience in global mobility, relocation, or a related professional services environment is preferred. • Experience in supporting senior executives and corporate clients is an advantage. • A good track record of leading and developing service teams. • Strong interpersonal skills to work with diverse groups of stakeholders, with drive to manage multiple service streams in a fast-paced environment. • Experience in financial management (including budgeting). Experience in leveraging on technology (e.g. AI) to review and drive business outcomes is an added advantage. Salary will commensurate with experience. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Please contact mfa_career@mfa.gov.sg if you require assistance with your application.
hrp|18070169|005056a3-d347-1fe1-ace7-d0a.description: You head the Business Support Centre (BSC) at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, leading a team dedicated to delivering seamless, end-to-end travel and relocation support for MFA officers. Besides supervising the daily operations, you are pivotal in shaping BSC's service culture, driving and reviewing policies and business processes to ensure their relevance and effectiveness in supporting MFA's mission at home and abroad, and in optimising the use of financial resources.

hrp|18071298|005056a3-d347-1fe1-ad89-11a.responsibilities: The Rail Digitalisation & Guild (Sub-group) is a cross-functional and multidisciplinary team established to drive and deliver Authority’s Railway Common Data Platforms (CDPs), which includes data analytics and artificial intelligence capabilities to support railway performance throughout the Planning, Design, Build, Operation, Maintenance and Asset Management processes. Feedback & Communications: Monitor and manage user feedback, ensuring timely and professional responses. Incident & Problem Management : Provide first and second level support for application incidents. Investigate, troubleshoot and resolve application issues. Asset & License Tracking: Maintain accurate, up-to-date inventories of the team's fixed assets and software licenses. Financial & Procurement Management: Monitor expenditure requests against allocated budgets, track actual spending, and manage the end-to-end procurement of platform and software goods and services. Documentation & Correspondence: Draft, format, and generate official documentation, including internal memos, Purchase Requisitions (PRs), Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs), and standard corporate letters.
